  555. ἀπέκδυσις from ἀπεκδύομαι; divestment: putting off.
  556. ἀπελαύνω from ἀπό and ἐλαύνω; to dismiss: drive.
  557. ἀπελεγμός from a compound of ἀπό and ἐλέγχω; refutation, i.e. (by implication) contempt: nought.
  558. ἀπελεύθερος from ἀπό and ἐλεύθερος; one freed away, i.e. a freedman: freeman.
  559. Ἀπελλῆς of Latin origin; Apelles, a Christian: Apelles.
  560. ἀπελπίζω from ἀπό and ἐλπίζω; to hope out, i.e. fully expect: hope for again.
  561. ἀπέναντι from ἀπό and ἔναντι; from in front, i.e. opposite, before or against: before, contrary, over against, in the presence of.
  562. ἀπέραντος from Α (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of πέραν; unfinished, i.e. (by implication) interminable: endless.
  563. ἀπερισπάστως adverb from a compound of Α (as a negative participle) and a presumed derivative of περισπάω; undistractedly, i.e. free from (domestic) solicitude: without distraction.
  564. ἀπερίτμητος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of περιτέμνω; uncircumcised (figuratively): uncircumcised.
  565. ἀπέρχομαι from ἀπό and ἔρχομαι; to go off (i.e. depart), aside (i.e. apart) or behind (i.e. follow), literally or figuratively: come, depart, go (aside, away, back, out, … ways), pass away, be past.
  566. ἀπέχει third person singular present indicative active of ἀπέχω used impersonally; it is sufficient: it is enough.
  567. ἀπέχομαι middle voice (reflexively) of ἀπέχω; to hold oneself off, i.e. refrain: abstain.
  568. ἀπέχω from ἀπό and ἔχω; (actively) to have out, i.e. receive in full; (intransitively) to keep (oneself) away, i.e. be distant (literally or figuratively): be, have, receive.
  569. ἀπιστέω from ἄπιστος; to be unbelieving, i.e. (transitively) disbelieve, or (by implication) disobey: believe not.
  570. ἀπιστία from ἄπιστος; faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness (disobedience): unbelief.
  571. ἄπιστος from Α (as a negative particle) and πιστός; (actively) disbelieving, i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing): that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing).
  572. ἁπλότης from ἁπλοῦς; singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal): bountifulness, liberal(-ity), simplicity, singleness.
  573. ἁπλοῦς probably from Α (as a particle of union) and the base of πλέκω; properly, folded together, i.e. single (figuratively, clear): single.
  574. ἁπλῶς adverb from ἁπλοῦς (in the objective sense of ἁπλότης); bountifully; --liberally.
  575. ἀπό a primary particle; "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative): (X here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th), from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with. In composition (as a prefix) it usually denotes separation, departure, cessation, completion, reversal, etc.
  576. ἀποβαίνω from ἀπό and the base of βάσις; literally, to disembark; figuratively, to eventuate: become, go out, turn.
  577. ἀποβάλλω from ἀπό and βάλλω; to throw off; figuratively, to lose: cast away.
  578. ἀποβλέπω from ἀπό and βλέπω; to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard: have respect.
  579. ἀπόβλητος from ἀποβάλλω; cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected: be refused.
  580. ἀποβολή from ἀποβάλλω; rejection; figuratively, loss: casting away, loss.
  581. ἀπογενόμενος past participle of a compound of ἀπό and γίνομαι; absent, i.e. deceased (figuratively, renounced): being dead.
  582. ἀπογραφή from ἀπογράφω; an enrollment; by implication, an assessment: taxing.
  583. ἀπογράφω from ἀπό and γράφω; to write off (a copy or list), i.e. enrol: tax, write.
  584. ἀποδείκνυμι from ἀπό and δεικνύω; to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. accredit: (ap-)prove, set forth, shew.
  585. ἀπόδειξις from ἀποδείκνυμι; manifestation: demonstration.
  586. ἀποδεκατόω from ἀπό and δεκατόω; to tithe (as debtor or creditor): (give, pay, take) tithe.
  587. ἀπόδεκτος from ἀποδέχομαι; accepted, i.e. agreeable: acceptable.
  588. ἀποδέχομαι from ἀπό and δέχομαι; to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve (things): accept, receive (gladly).
  589. ἀποδημέω from ἀπόδημος; to go abroad, i.e. visit a foreign land: go (travel) into a far country, journey.
  590. ἀπόδημος from ἀπό and δῆμος; absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign traveller: taking a far journey.
  591. ἀποδίδωμι from ἀπό and δίδωμι; to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various applications): deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield.
  592. ἀποδιορίζω from ἀπό and a compound of Ἀλέξανδρος and ὁρίζω; to disjoin (by a boundary, figuratively, a party): separate.
  593. ἀποδοκιμάζω from ἀπό and δοκιμάζω; to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to repudiate: disallow, reject.
  594. ἀποδοχή from ἀποδέχομαι; acceptance: acceptation.
  595. ἀπόθεσις from ἀποτίθημι; a laying aside (literally or figuratively): putting away (off).
  596. ἀποθήκη from ἀποτίθημι; a repository, i.e. granary: barn, garner.
  597. ἀποθησαυρίζω from ἀπό and θησαυρίζω; to treasure away: lay up in store.
  598. ἀποθλίβω from ἀπό and θλίβω; to crowd (from every side): press.
  599. ἀποθνήσκω from ἀπό and θνήσκω; to die off (literally or figuratively): be dead, death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with).
  600. ἀποκαθίστημι from ἀπό and καθίστημι; to reconstitute (in health, home or organization): restore (again).
  601. ἀποκαλύπτω from ἀπό and καλύπτω; to take off the cover, i.e. disclose: reveal.
  602. ἀποκάλυψις from ἀποκαλύπτω; disclosure: appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation.
  603. ἀποκαραδοκία from a comparative of ἀπό and a compound of kara (the head) and δοκέω (in the sense of watching); intense anticipation: earnest expectation.
  604. ἀποκαταλλάσσω from ἀπό and καταλλάσσω; to reconcile fully: reconcile.
  605. ἀποκατάστασις from ἀποκαθίστημι; reconstitution: restitution.
  606. ἀπόκειμαι from ἀπό and κεῖμαι; to be reserved; figuratively, to await: be appointed, (be) laid up.
  607. ἀποκεφαλίζω from ἀπό and κεφαλή; to decapitate: behead.
  608. ἀποκλείω from ἀπό and κλείω; to close fully: shut up.
  609. ἀποκόπτω from ἀπό and κόπτω; to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts): cut off. Compare κατατομή.
  610. ἀπόκριμα from ἀποκρίνομαι (in its original sense of judging); a judicial decision: sentence.
  611. ἀποκρίνομαι from ἀπό and krino; to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare עָנָה) to begin to speak (where an address is expected): answer.
  612. ἀπόκρισις from ἀποκρίνομαι; a response: answer.
  613. ἀποκρύπτω from ἀπό and κρύπτω; to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep secret: hide.
  614. ἀπόκρυφος from ἀποκρύπτω; secret; by implication, treasured: hid, kept secret.
  615. ἀποκτείνω from ἀπό and kteino (to slay); to kill outright; figuratively, to destroy: put to death, kill, slay.
  616. ἀποκυέω from ἀπό and the base of κῦμα; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively): beget, produce.
  617. ἀποκυλίω from ἀπό and κυλιόω; to roll away: roll away (back).
  618. ἀπολαμβάνω from ἀπό and λαμβάνω; to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside: receive, take.
  619. ἀπόλαυσις from a comparative of ἀπό and lauo (to enjoy); full enjoyment: enjoy(-ment).
  620. ἀπολείπω from ἀπό and λείπω; to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake: leave, remain.
  621. ἀπολείχω from ἀπό and leicho (to "lick"); to lick clean: lick.
  622. ἀπόλλυμι from ἀπό and the base of ὄλεθρος; to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively: destroy, die, lose, mar, perish.
  623. Ἀπολλύων active participle of ἀπόλλυμι; a destroyer (i.e. Satan): Apollyon.
  624. Ἀπολλωνία from the pagan deity Apollon (i.e. the sun; from ἀπόλλυμι); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia: Apollonia.
  625. Ἀπολλῶς probably from the same as Ἀπολλωνία; Apollos, an Israelite: Apollos.
  626. ἀπολογέομαι middle voice from a compound of ἀπό and λόγος; to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self): answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self.
  627. ἀπολογία from the same as ἀπολογέομαι; a plea ("apology"): answer (for self), clearing of self, defence.
  628. ἀπολούω from ἀπό and λούω; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively): wash (away).
  629. ἀπολύτρωσις from a compound of ἀπό and λύτρον; (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation: deliverance, redemption.
  630. ἀπολύω from ἀπό and λύω; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce: (let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty.
  631. ἀπομάσσομαι middle voice from ἀπό and masso (to squeeze, knead, smear); to scrape away: wipe off.
  632. ἀπονέμω from ἀπό and the base of νόμος; to apportion, i.e. bestow: give.
  633. ἀπονίπτω from ἀπό and νίπτω; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically): wash.
  634. ἀποπίπτω from ἀπό and πίπτω; to fall off: fall.
  635. ἀποπλανάω from ἀπό and πλανάω; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth): err, seduce.
  636. ἀποπλέω from ἀπό and πλέω; to set sail: sail away.
  637. ἀποπλύνω from ἀπό and πλύνω; to rinse off: wash.
  638. ἀποπνίγω from ἀπό and πνίγω; to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth): choke.
  639. ἀπορέω from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and the base of πορεύομαι; to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally): (stand in) doubt, be perplexed.
  640. ἀπορία from the same as ἀπορέω; a (state of) quandary: perplexity.
  641. ἀποῤῥίπτω from ἀπό and ῥίπτω; to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself): cast.
  642. ἀπορφανίζω from ἀπό and a derivative of ὀρφανός; to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse): take.
  643. ἀποσκευάζω from ἀπό and a derivative of σκεῦος; to pack up (one's) baggage: take up… carriages.
  644. ἀποσκίασμα from a compound of ἀπό and a derivative of σκιά; a shading off, i.e. obscuration: shadow.
  645. ἀποσπάω from ἀπό and σπάω; to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously): (with-)draw (away), after we were gotten from.
  646. ἀποστασία feminine of the same as ἀποστάσιον; defection from truth (properly, the state) ("apostasy"): falling away, forsake.
  647. ἀποστάσιον neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of ἀφίστημι; properly, something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce: (writing of) divorcement.
  648. ἀποστεγάζω from ἀπό and a derivative of στέγη; to unroof: uncover.
  649. ἀποστέλλω from ἀπό and στέλλω; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively: put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty).
  650. ἀποστερέω from ἀπό and stereo (to deprive); to despoil: defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud.
  651. ἀποστολή from ἀποστέλλω; commission, i.e. (specially) apostolate: apostleship.
  652. ἀπόστολος from ἀποστέλλω; a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers): apostle, messenger, he that is sent.
  653. ἀποστοματίζω from ἀπό and a (presumed) derivative of στόμα; to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious manner): provoke to speak.
  654. ἀποστρέφω from ἀπό and στρέφω; to turn away or back (literally or figuratively): bring again, pervert, turn away (from).
  655. ἀποστυγέω from ἀπό and the base of στυγνητός; to detest utterly: abhor.
  656. ἀποσυνάγωγος from ἀπό and συναγωγή; excommunicated: (put) out of the synagogue(-s).
  657. ἀποτάσσομαι middle voice from ἀπό and τάσσω; literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce: bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away.
  658. ἀποτελέω from ἀπό and τελέω; to complete entirely, i.e. consummate: finish.
  659. ἀποτίθημι from ἀπό and τίθημι; to put away (literally or figuratively): cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off).
  660. ἀποτινάσσω from ἀπό and tinasso (to jostle); to brush off: shake off.
  661. ἀποτίνω from ἀπό and τίνω; to pay in full: repay.
  662. ἀποτολμάω from ἀπό and τολμάω; to venture plainly: be very bold.
  663. ἀποτομία from the base of ἀποτόμως; (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e. rigor: severity.
  664. ἀποτόμως adverb from a derivative of a comparative of ἀπό and temno (to cut); abruptly, i.e. peremptorily: sharply(-ness).
  665. ἀποτρέπω from ἀπό and the base of τροπή; to deflect, i.e. (reflexively) avoid: turn away.
  666. ἀπουσία from the participle of ἄπειμι; a being away: absence.
  667. ἀποφέρω from ἀπό and φέρω; to bear off (literally or relatively): bring, carry (away).
  668. ἀποφεύγω from ἀπό and φεύγω; (figuratively) to escape: escape.
  669. ἀποφθέγγομαι from ἀπό and φθέγγομαι; to enunciate plainly, i.e. declare: say, speak forth, utterance.
  670. ἀποφορτίζομαι from ἀπό and the middle voice of φορτίζω; to unload: unlade.
  671. ἀπόχρησις from a compound of ἀπό and χράομαι; the act of using up, i.e. consumption: using.
  672. ἀποχωρέω from ἀπό and χωρέω; to go away: depart.
  673. ἀποχωρίζω from ἀπό and χωρίζω; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate: depart (asunder).
  674. ἀποψύχω from ἀπό and ψύχω; to breathe out, i.e. faint: hearts failing.
  675. Ἄππιος of Latin origin; (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman: Appii.
  676. ἀπρόσιτος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of πρός and eimi (to go); inaccessible: which no man can approach.
  677. ἀπρόσκοπος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of προσκόπτω; actively, inoffensive, i.e. not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. not led into sin: none (void of, without) offence.
  678. ἀπροσωπολήπτως adverb from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of πρόσωπον and λαμβάνω (compare προσωπολήπτης); in a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially: without respect of persons.
  679. ἄπταιστος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of πταίω; not stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin: from falling.
  680. ἅπτομαι reflexive of ἅπτω; properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations): touch.
  681. ἅπτω a primary verb; properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire: kindle, light.
  682. Ἀπφία probably of foreign origin; Apphia, a woman of Collosæ: Apphia.
  683. ἀπωθέομαι or apothomai from ἀπό and the middle voice of otheo or otho (to shove); to push off, figuratively, to reject: cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from).
  684. ἀπώλεια from a presumed derivative of ἀπόλλυμι; ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal): damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste.
  685. ἀρά probably from αἴρω; properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation: curse.
  686. ἄρα probably from αἴρω (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows): haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other particles, especially γέ or οὖν (after) or εἰ (before). Compare also ἆρα.
  687. ἆρα a form of ἄρα, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed: therefore.
  688. Ἀραβία of Hebrew origin (עֲרָב); Arabia, a region of Asia: Arabia.
  689. Ἀράμ of Hebrew origin (רָם); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite: Aram.
  690. Ἄραψ from Ἀραβία; an Arab or native of Arabia: Arabian.
  691. ἀργέω from ἀργός; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay: linger.
  692. ἀργός from Α (as a negative particle) and ἔργον; inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless: barren, idle, slow.
  693. ἀργύρεος from ἄργυρος; made of silver: (of) silver.
  694. ἀργύριον neuter of a presumed derivative of ἄργυρος; silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel): money, (piece of) silver (piece).
  695. ἀργυροκόπος from ἄργυρος and κόπτω; a beater (i.e. worker) of silver: silversmith.
  696. ἄργυρος from argos (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or coin): silver.
  697. Ἄρειος Πάγος from Ares (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of πήγνυμι; rock of Ares, a place in Athens: Areopagus, Mars' Hill.
  698. Ἀρεοπαγίτης from Ἄρειος Πάγος; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill: Areopagite.
  699. ἀρεσκεία from a derivative of ἀρέσκω; complaisance: pleasing.
  700. ἀρέσκω probably from αἴρω (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so): please.
  701. ἀρεστός from ἀρέσκω; agreeable; by implication, fit: (things that) please(-ing), reason.
  702. Ἀρέτας of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian: Aretas.
  703. ἀρέτη from the same as ἄῤῥην; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed): praise, virtue.
  704. ἀρήν perhaps the same as ἄῤῥην; a lamb (as a male): lamb.
  705. ἀριθμέω from ἀριθμός; to enumerate or count: number.
  706. ἀριθμός from αἴρω; a number (as reckoned up): number.
  707. Ἀριμαθαία of Hebrew origin (רָמָה); Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine: Arimathæa.
  708. Ἀρίσταρχος from the same as ἄριστον and ἄρχω; best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian: Aristarchus.
  709. ἀριστάω from ἄριστον; to take the principle meal: dine.
  710. ἀριστερός apparently a comparative of the same as ἄριστον; the left hand (as second-best): left (hand).
  711. Ἀριστόβουλος from the same as ἄριστον and βουλή; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a Christian: Aristobulus.
  712. ἄριστον apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as ἄῤῥην; the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from eri ("early")), i.e. luncheon: dinner.
  713. ἀρκετός from ἀρκέω; satisfactory: enough, suffice (-ient).
  714. ἀρκέω apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to αἴρω through the idea of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory): be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient.
  715. ἄρκτος probably from ἀρκέω; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity): bear.
  716. ἅρμα probably from αἴρω (perhaps with Α (as a particle of union) prefixed); a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare ἁρμός)): chariot.
  717. Ἀρμαγεδδών of Hebrew origin (הָר and מְגִדּוֹן); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a symbolic name: Armageddon.
  718. ἁρμόζω from ἁρμός; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth): espouse.
  719. ἁρμός from the same as ἅρμα; an articulation (of the body): joint.
  720. ἀρνέομαι perhaps from Α (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of ῥέω; to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate: deny, refuse.
  721. ἀρνίον diminutive from ἀρήν; a lambkin: lamb.
  722. ἀροτριόω from ἄροτρον; to plow: plough.
  723. ἄροτρον from aroo (to till); a plow: plough.
  724. ἁρπαγή from ἁρπάζω; pillage (properly abstract): extortion, ravening, spoiling.
  725. ἁρπαγμός from ἁρπάζω; plunder (properly concrete): robbery.
  726. ἁρπάζω from a derivative of αἱρέομαι; to seize (in various applications): catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).
  727. ἅρπαξ from ἁρπάζω; rapacious: extortion, ravening.
  728. ἀῤῥαβών of Hebrew origin (עֲרָבוֹן); a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest: earnest.
  729. ἄῤῥαφος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as ῥαφίς; unsewed, i.e. of a single piece: without seam.
  730. ἄῤῥην or arsen probably from αἴρω; male (as stronger for lifting): male, man.
  731. ἄῤῥητος from Α (as a negative particle) and the same as ῥητῶς; unsaid, i.e. (by implication) inexpressible: unspeakable.
  732. ἄῤῥωστος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of ῥώννυμι; infirm: sick (folk, -ly).
  733. ἀρσενοκοίτης from ἄῤῥην and κοίτη; a sodomite: abuser of (that defile) self with mankind.
  734. Ἀρτεμάς contracted from a compound of Ἄρτεμις and δῶρον; gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian: Artemas.
  735. Ἄρτεμις probably from the same as ἀρτέμων; prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities: Diana.
  736. ἀρτέμων from a derivative of ἄρτι; properly, something ready (or else more remotely from αἴρω (compare ἄρτος); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel: mainsail.
  737. ἄρτι adverb from a derivative of αἴρω (compare ἄρτος) through the idea of suspension; just now: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present.
  738. ἀρτιγέννητος from ἄρτι and γεννητός; just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert: new born.
  739. ἄρτιος from ἄρτι; fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete: perfect.
  740. ἄρτος from αἴρω; bread (as raised) or a loaf: (shew-)bread, loaf.
  741. ἀρτύω from a presumed derivative of αἴρω; to prepare, i.e. spice (with stimulating condiments): season.
  742. Ἀρφαξάδ of Hebrew origin (אַרְפַּכְשַׁד); Arphaxad, a post-diluvian patriarch: Arphaxad.
  743. ἀρχάγγελος from ἄρχω and ἄγγελος; a chief angel: archangel.
  744. ἀρχαῖος from ἀρχή; original or primeval: (them of) old (time).
  745. Ἀρχέλαος from ἄρχω and Λαοδικεύς; people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king: Archelaus.
  746. ἀρχή from ἄρχομαι; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank): beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule.
  747. ἀρχηγός from ἀρχή and ἄγω; a chief leader: author, captain, prince.
  748. ἀρχιερατικός from ἀρχή and a derivative of ἱερός; high-priestly: of the high-priest.
  749. ἀρχιερεύς from ἀρχή and ἱερεύς; the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.
  750. ἀρχιποίμην from ἀρχή and ποιμήν; a head shepherd: chief shepherd.
  751. Ἄρχιππος from ἀρχή and ἵππος; horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian: Archippus.
  752. ἀρχισυνάγωγος from ἀρχή and συναγωγή; director of the synagogue services: (chief) ruler of the synagogue.
  753. ἀρχιτέκτων from ἀρχή and τέκτων; a chief constructor, i.e. "architect": masterbuilder.
  754. ἀρχιτελώνης from ἀρχή and τελώνης; a principle tax-gatherer: chief among the publicans.
  755. ἀρχιτρίκλινος from ἀρχή and a compound of τρεῖς and κλίνω (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches); director of the entertainment: governor (ruler) of the feast.
  756. ἄρχομαι middle voice of ἄρχω (through the implication, of precedence); to commence (in order of time): (rehearse from the) begin(-ning).
  757. ἄρχω a primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power): reign (rule) over.
  758. ἄρχων present participle of ἄρχω; a first (in rank or power): chief (ruler), magistrate, prince, ruler.
  759. ἄρωμα from αἴρω (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic: (sweet) spice.
  760. Ἀσά of Hebrew origin (אָסָא); Asa, an Israelite: Asa.
  761. ἀσάλευτος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σαλεύω; unshaken, i.e. (by implication) immovable (figuratively): which cannot be moved, unmovable.
  762. ἄσβεστος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σβέννυμι; not extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual: not to be quenched, unquenchable.
  763. ἀσέβεια from ἀσεβής; impiety, i.e. (by implication) wickedness: ungodly(-liness).
  764. ἀσεβέω from ἀσεβής; to be (by implied act) impious or wicked: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly.
  765. ἀσεβής from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of σέβομαι; irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked: ungodly (man).
  766. ἀσέλγεια from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed selges (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other vices): filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.
  767. ἄσημος from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of σημαίνω; unmarked, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble: mean.
  768. Ἀσήρ of Hebrew origin (אָשֵׁר); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe: Aser.
  769. ἀσθένεια from ἀσθενής; feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty: disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness.
  770. ἀσθενέω from ἀσθενής; to be feeble (in any sense): be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.
  771. ἀσθένημα from ἀσθενέω; a scruple of conscience: infirmity.
  772. ἀσθενής from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of σθενόω; strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral): more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing).
  773. Ἀσία of uncertain derivation; Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore: Asia.
  774. Ἀσιανός from Ἀσία; an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia: of Asia.
  775. Ἀσιάρχης from Ἀσία and ἀρχή; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor: chief of Asia.
  776. ἀσιτία from ἄσιτος; fasting (the state): abstinence.
  777. ἄσιτος from Α (as a negative particle) and σῖτος; without (taking) food: fasting.
  778. ἀσκέω probably from the same as σκεῦος; to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive): exercise.
  779. ἀσκός from the same as ἀσκέω; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle: bottle.
  780. ἀσμένως adverb from a derivative of the base of ἡδονή; with pleasure: gladly.
  781. ἄσοφος from Α (as a negative particle) and σοφός; unwise: fool.
  782. ἀσπάζομαι from Α (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of σπάω; to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome: embrace, greet, salute, take leave.
  783. ἀσπασμός from ἀσπάζομαι; a greeting (in person or by letter): greeting, salutation.
  784. ἄσπιλος from Α (as a negative particle) and σπιλόω; unblemished (physically or morally): without spot, unspotted.
  785. ἀσπίς of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp": asp.
  786. ἄσπονδος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of σπένδω; literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless: implacable, truce-breaker.
  787. ἀσσάριον of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin: farthing.
  788. ἆσσον neuter comparative of the base of ἐγγύς; more nearly, i.e. very near: close.
  789. Ἄσσος probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia MInor: Assos.
  790. ἀστατέω from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of ἵστημι; to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless: have no certain dwelling-place.
  791. ἀστεῖος from astu (a city); urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome: fair.
  792. ἀστήρ probably from the base of στρώννυμι; a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively: star.
  793. ἀστήρικτος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of στηρίζω; unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating: unstable.
  794. ἄστοργος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of stergo (to cherish affectionately); hard-hearted towards kindred: without natural affection.
  795. ἀστοχέω from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and stoichos (an aim); to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth: err, swerve.
  796. ἀστραπή from ἀστράπτω; lightning; by analogy, glare: lightning, bright shining.
  797. ἀστράπτω probably from ἀστήρ; to flash as lightning: lighten, shine.
  798. ἄστρον neuter from ἀστήρ; properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial): star.
  799. Ἀσύγκριτος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of συγκρίνω; incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian: Asyncritos.
  800. ἀσύμφωνος from Α (as a negative particle) and σύμφωνος; inharmonious (figuratively): agree not.
  801. ἀσύνετος from Α (as a negative particle) and συνετός; unintelligent; by implication, wicked: foolish, without understanding.
  802. ἀσύνθετος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of συντίθεμαι; properly, not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts: covenant-breaker.
  803. ἀσφάλεια from ἀσφαλής; security (literally or figuratively): certainty, safety.
  804. ἀσφαλής from Α (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); secure (literally or figuratively): certain(-ty), safe, sure.
  805. ἀσφαλίζω from ἀσφαλής; to render secure: make fast (sure).
  806. ἀσφαλῶς adverb from ἀσφαλής; securely (literally or figuratively): assuredly, safely.
  807. ἀσχημονέω from ἀσχήμων; to be (i.e. act) unbecoming: behave self uncomely (unseemly).
  808. ἀσχημοσύνη from ἀσχήμων; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda: shame, that which is unseemly.
  809. ἀσχήμων from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of ἔχω (in the sense of its congener σχῆμα); properly, shapeless, i.e. (figuratively) inelegant: uncomely.
  810. ἀσωτία from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of σώζω; properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication) profligacy: excess, riot.
  811. ἀσώτως adverb from the same as ἀσωτία; dissolutely: riotous.
  812. ἀτακτέω from ἄτακτος; to be (i.e. act) irregular: behave self disorderly.
  813. ἄτακτος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of τάσσω; unarranged, i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously): unruly.
  814. ἀτάκτως adverb from ἄτακτος, irregularly (morally): disorderly.
  815. ἄτεκνος from Α (as a negative particle) and τέκνον; childless: childless, without children.
  816. ἀτενίζω from a compound of Α (as a particle of union) and teino (to stretch); to gaze intently: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes.
  817. ἄτερ a particle probably akin to ἄνευ; aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or figuratively): in the absence of, without.
  818. ἀτιμάζω from ἄτιμος; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.
  819. ἀτιμία from ἄτιμος; infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity, (objectively) disgrace: dishonour, reproach, shame, vile.
  820. ἄτιμος from Α (as a negative particle) and τιμή; (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree).
  821. ἀτιμόω from ἄτιμος; used like ἀτιμάζω, to maltreat: handle shamefully.
  822. ἀτμίς from the same as ἀήρ; mist: vapour.
  823. ἄτομος from Α (as a negative particle) and the base of τομώτερος; uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time): moment.
  824. ἄτοπος from Α (as a negative particle) and τόπος; out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked: amiss, harm, unreasonable.
  825. Ἀττάλεια from Attalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia: Attalia.
  826. αὐγάζω from αὐγή; to beam forth (figuratively): shine.
  827. αὐγή of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn: break of day.
  828. Αὐγοῦστος from Latin ("august"); Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor: Augustus.
  829. αὐθάδης from αὐτός and the base of ἡδονή; self-pleasing, i.e. arrogant: self-willed.
  830. αὐθαίρετος from αὐτός and the same as αἱρετίζω; self-chosen, i.e. (by implication) voluntary: of own accord, willing of self.
  831. αὐθεντέω from a compound of αὐτός and an obsolete hentes (a worker); to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate: usurp authority over.
  832. αὐλέω from αὐλός; to play the flute: pipe.
  833. αὐλή from the same as ἀήρ; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion: court, (sheep-)fold, hall, palace.
  834. αὐλητής from αὐλέω; a flute-player: minstrel, piper.
  835. αὐλίζομαι middle voice from αὐλή; to pass the night (properly, in the open air): abide, lodge.
  836. αὐλός from the same as ἀήρ; a flute (as blown): pipe.
  837. αὐξάνω a prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), i.e. enlarge (literal or figurative, active or passive): grow (up), (give the) increase.
  838. αὔξησις from αὐξάνω; growth: increase.
  839. αὔριον from a derivative of the same as ἀήρ (meaning a breeze, i.e. the morning air); properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of ἡμέρα) to-morrow: (to-)morrow, next day.
  840. αὐστηρός from a (presumed) derivative of the same as ἀήρ (meaning blown); rough (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe: austere.
  841. αὐτάρκεια from αὐτάρκης; self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence: contentment, sufficiency.
  842. αὐτάρκης from αὐτός and ἀρκέω; self-complacent, i.e. contented: content.
  843. αὐτοκατάκριτος from αὐτός and a derivative or κατακρίνω; self-condemned: condemned of self.
  844. αὐτόματος from αὐτός and the same as μάτην; self-moved ("automatic"), i.e. spontaneous: of own accord, of self.
  845. αὐτόπτης from αὐτός and ὀπτάνομαι; self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness: eye-witness.
  846. αὐτός from the particle au (perhaps akin to the base of ἀήρ through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the comparative ἑαυτοῦ) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons: her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy-)self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which. Compare αὑτοῦ.
  847. αὐτοῦ genitive (i.e. possessive) of αὐτός, used as an adverb of location; properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. in this (or that) place: (t-)here.
  848. αὑτοῦ contracted for ἑαυτοῦ; self (in some oblique case or reflexively, relation): her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them(-selves), they.
  849. αὐτόχειρ from αὐτός and χείρ; self-handed, i.e. doing personally: with … own hands.
  850. αὐχμηρός from auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of ἀήρ) (dust, as dried by wind); properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure: dark.
  851. ἀφαιρέω from ἀπό and αἱρέομαι; to remove (literally or figuratively): cut (smite) off, take away.
  852. ἀφανής from Α (as a negative particle) and φαίνω; non-apparent): that is not manifest.
  853. ἀφανίζω from ἀφανής; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed): corrupt, disfigure, perish, vanish away.
  854. ἀφανισμός from ἀφανίζω; disappearance, i.e. (figuratively) abrogation: vanish away.
  855. ἄφαντος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of φαίνω; non-manifested, i.e. invisible: vanished out of sight.
  856. ἀφεδρών from a compound of ἀπό and the base of ἑδραῖος; a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy: draught.
  857. ἀφειδία from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and φείδομαι; unsparingness, i.e. austerity (asceticism): neglecting.
  858. ἀφελότης from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e. (figuratively) simplicity: singleness.
  859. ἄφεσις from ἀφίημι; freedom; (figuratively) pardon: deliverance, forgiveness, liberty, remission.
  860. ἁφή from ἅπτομαι; probably a ligament (as fastening): joint.
  861. ἀφθαρσία from ἄφθαρτος; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness: immortality, incorruption, sincerity.
  862. ἄφθαρτος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of φθείρω; undecaying (in essence or continuance): not (in-, un-)corruptible, immortal.
  863. ἀφίημι from ἀπό and hiemi (to send; an intensive form of eimi, to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow): cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up.
  864. ἀφικνέομαι from ἀπό and the base of ἱκανός; to go (i.e. spread) forth (by rumor): come abroad.
  865. ἀφιλάγαθος from Α (as a negative particle) and φιλάγαθος; hostile to virtue: despiser of those that are good.
  866. ἀφιλάργυρος from Α (as a negative particle) and φιλάργυρος; unavaricious: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.
  867. ἄφιξις from ἀφικνέομαι; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication) departure: departing.
  868. ἀφίστημι from ἀπό and ἵστημι; to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self.
  869. ἄφνω adverb from ἀφανής (contraction); unawares, i.e. unexpectedly: suddenly.
  870. ἀφόβως adverb from a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and φόβος; fearlessly: without fear.
  871. ἀφομοιόω from ἀπό and ὁμοιόω; to assimilate closely: make like.
  872. ἀφοράω from ἀπό and ὁράω; to consider attentively: look.
  873. ἀφορίζω from ἀπό and ὁρίζω; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.: divide, separate, sever.
  874. ἀφορμή from a compound of ἀπό and ὁρμάω; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively) an opportunity: occasion.
  875. ἀφρίζω from ἀφρός; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy): foam.
  876. ἀφρός apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. slaver: foaming.
  877. ἀφροσύνη from ἄφρων; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness: folly, foolishly(-ness).
  878. ἄφρων from Α (as a negative particle) and φρήν; properly, mindless, i.e. stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving: fool(-ish), unwise.
  879. ἀφυπνόω from a compound of ἀπό and ὕπνος; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber: fall asleep.
  880. ἄφωνος from Α (as a negative particle) and φωνή; voiceless, i.e. mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning: dumb, without signification.
  881. Ἀχάζ of Hebrew origin (אָחָז); Achaz, an Israelite: Achaz.
  882. Ἀχαΐα of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe: Achaia.
  883. Ἀχαϊκός from Ἀχαΐα; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian: Achaicus.
  884. ἀχάριστος from Α (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of χαρίζομαι; thankless, i.e. ungrateful: unthankful.
  885. Ἀχείμ probably of Hebrew origin (compare יוֹקִים); Achim, an Israelite: Achim.
  886. ἀχειροποίητος from Α (as a negative particle) and χειροποίητος; unmanufactured, i.e. inartificial: made without (not made with) hands.
  887. ἀχλύς of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract: mist.
  888. ἀχρεῖος from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of χρή (compare χρεία); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious: unprofitable.
  889. ἀχρειόω from ἀχρεῖος; to render useless, i.e. spoil: become unprofitable.
  890. ἄχρηστος from Α (as a negative particle) and χρηστός; inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental: unprofitable.
  891. ἄχρι or achris akh'-rece; akin to ἄκρον (through the idea of a terminus); (of time) until or (of place) up to: as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while. Compare μέχρι.
  892. ἄχυρον perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive): chaff.
  893. ἀψευδής from Α (as a negative particle) and ψεῦδος; veracious: that cannot lie.
  894. ἄψινθος of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity): wormwood.
  895. ἄψυχος from Α (as a negative particle) and ψυχή; lifeless, i.e. inanimate (mechanical): without life.
  896. Βάαλ of Hebrew origin (בַּ֫עַל); Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry): Baal.
  897. Βαβυλών of Hebrew origin (בָּבֶל); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)): Babylon.
  898. βαθμός from the same as βάθος; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of dignity): degree.
  899. βάθος from the same as βαθύς; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery: deep(-ness, things), depth.
  900. βαθύνω from βαθύς; to deepen: deep.
  901. βαθύς from the base of βάσις; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively: deep, very early.
  902. βαΐον a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of βάσις; a palm twig (as going out far): branch.
  903. Βαλαάμ of Hebrew origin (בִּלְעָם); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher): Balaam.
  904. Βαλάκ of Hebrew origin (בָּלָק); Balak, a Moabite: Balac.
  905. βαλάντιον probably remotely from βάλλω (as a depository); a pouch (for money): bag, purse.
  906. βάλλω a primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense): arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare ῥίπτω.
  907. βαπτίζω from a derivative of βάπτω; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism: Baptist, baptize, wash.
  908. βάπτισμα from βαπτίζω; baptism (technically or figuratively): baptism.
  909. βαπτισμός from βαπτίζω; ablution (ceremonial or Christian): baptism, washing.
  910. Βαπτιστής from βαπτίζω; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner: Baptist.
  911. βάπτω a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye): dip.
  912. Βαραββᾶς of Chaldee origin (גָּאוֹן and אֲבַגְתָא); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite: Barabbas.
  913. Βαράκ of Hebrew origin (בָּרָק); Barak, an Israelite: Barak.
  914. Βαραχίας of Hebrew origin (בֶּרֶכְיָה); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite: Barachias.
  915. βάρβαρος of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e. non-Greek): barbarian(-rous).
  916. βαρέω from βαρύς; to weigh down (figuratively): burden, charge, heavy, press.
  917. βαρέως adverb from βαρύς; heavily (figuratively): dull.
  918. Βαρθολομαῖος of Chaldee origin (בַּר and תַּלְמָי); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a Christian apostle: Bartholomeus.
  919. Βαριησοῦς of Chaldee origin (בַּר and יְהוֹשׁ֫וּעַ); son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite: Barjesus.
  920. Βαριωνᾶς of Chaldee origin (בַּר and יוֹנָה); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite: Bar-jona.
  921. Βαρνάβας of Chaldee origin (בַּר and נְבִיָּאה); son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite: Barnabas.
  922. βάρος probably from the same as βάσις (through the notion of going down; compare βάθος); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority: burden(-some), weight.
  923. Βαρσαβᾶς of Chaldee origin (בַּר and probably צְבָא); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites: Barsabas.
  924. Βαρτιμαῖος of Chaldee origin (בַּר and טָמֵא); son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite: Bartimæus.
  925. βαρύνω from βαρύς; to burden (figuratively): overcharge.
  926. βαρύς from the same as βάρος; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave: grievous, heavy, weightier.
  927. βαρύτιμος from βαρύς and τιμή; highly valuable: very precious.
  928. βασανίζω from βάσανος; to torture: pain, toil, torment, toss, vex.
  929. βασανισμός from βασανίζω; torture: torment.
  930. βασανιστής from βασανίζω; a torturer: tormentor.
  931. βάσανος perhaps remotely from the same as βάσις (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture: torment.
  932. βασιλεία from βασιλεύς; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively): kingdom, + reign.
  933. βασίλειον neuter of βασίλειος; a palace: king's court.
  934. βασίλειος from βασιλεύς; kingly (in nature): royal.
  935. βασιλεύς probably from βάσις (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively): king.
  936. βασιλεύω from βασιλεύς; to rule (literally or figuratively): king, reign.
  937. βασιλικός from βασιλεύς; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent: king's, nobleman, royal.
  938. βασίλισσα feminine from βασιλεύω; a queen: queen.
  939. βάσις from baino (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot: foot.
  940. βασκαίνω akin to φάσκω; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations): bewitch.
  941. βαστάζω perhaps remotely derived from the base of βάσις (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.): bear, carry, take up.
  942. βάτος of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub: bramble, bush.
  943. βάτος of Hebrew origin (בָּת); a bath, or measure for liquids: measure.
  944. βάτραχος of uncertain derivation; a frog: frog.
  945. βαττολογέω from Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and λόγος; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously: use vain repetitions.
  946. βδέλυγμα from βδελύσσω; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry: abomination.
  947. βδελυκτός from βδελύσσω; detestable, i.e. (specially) idolatrous: abominable.
  948. βδελύσσω from a (presumed) derivative of bdeo (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry): abhor, abominable.
  949. βέβαιος from the base of βάσις (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively): firm, of force, stedfast, sure.
  950. βεβαιόω from βέβαιος; to stabilitate (figuratively): confirm, (e-)stablish.
  951. βεβαίωσις from βεβαιόω; stabiliment: confirmation.
  952. βέβηλος from the base of βάσις and belos (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked: profane (person).
  953. βεβηλόω from βέβηλος; to desecrate: profane.
  954. Βεελζεβούλ of Chaldee origin (by parody on בַּ֫עַל זְבוּב); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan: Beelzebub.
  955. Βελίαλ of Hebrew origin (בְּלִיַּ֫עַל); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan: Belial.
  956. βέλος from βάλλω; a missile, i.e. spear or arrow: dart.
  957. βελτίον neuter of a compound of a derivative of βάλλω (used for the comparative of ἀγαθός); better: very well.
  958. Βενιαμίν of Hebrew origin (בִּנְיָמִן); Benjamin, an Israelite: Benjamin.
  959. Βερνίκη from a provincial form of φέρω and νίκη; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family: Bernice.
  960. Βέροια perhaps a provincial from a derivative of πέραν (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line); Berœa, a place in Macedonia: Berea.
  961. Βεροιαῖος from Βέροια; a Berœoean or native of Berœa: of Berea.
  962. Βηθαβαρά of Hebrew origin (בָּ֫יִת and עֲבָרָה); ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan: Bethabara.
  963. Βηθανία of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine: Bethany.
  964. Βηθεσδά of Chaldee origin (compare בָּ֫יִת and חָ֫סֶד); house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem: Bethesda.
  965. Βηθλεέμ of Hebrew origin (בֵּית לְעַפְרָה); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine: Bethlehem.
  966. Βηθσαϊδά of Chaldee origin (compare בָּ֫יִת and צַיָּדִים); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine: Bethsaida.
  967. Βηθφαγή of Chaldee origin (compare בָּ֫יִת and פַּגֵּי); fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine: Bethphage.
  968. βῆμα from the base of βάσις; a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal: judgment-seat, set (foot) on, throne.
  969. βήρυλλος of uncertain derivation; a "beryl": beryl.
  970. βία probably akin to βίος (through the idea of vital activity); force: violence.
  971. βιάζω from βίος; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized: press, suffer violence.
  972. βίαιος from βία; violent: mighty.
  973. βιαστής from βιάζω; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic: violent.
  974. βιβλιαρίδιον a diminutive of βιβλίον; a booklet: little book.
  975. βιβλίον a diminutive of βίβλος; a roll: bill, book, scroll, writing.
  976. βίβλος properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing: book.
  977. βιβρώσκω a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of βόσκω); to eat: eat.
  978. Βιθυνία of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia: Bithynia.
  979. βίος a primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood: good, life, living.
  980. βιόω from βίος; to spend existence: live.
  981. βίωσις from βιόω; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode): manner of life.
  982. βιωτικός from a derivative of βιόω; relating to the present existence: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.
  983. βλαβερός from βλάπτω; injurious: hurtful.
  984. βλάπτω a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure: hurt.
  985. βλαστάνω from blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit: bring forth, bud, spring (up).
  986. Βλάστος perhaps the same as the base of βλαστάνω; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa: Blastus.
  987. βλασφημέω from βλάσφημος; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously: (speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.
  988. βλασφημία from βλάσφημος; vilification (especially against God): blasphemy, evil speaking, railing.
  989. βλάσφημος from a derivative of βλάπτω and φήμη; scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God): blasphemer(-mous), railing.
  990. βλέμμα from βλέπω; vision (properly concrete; by implication, abstract): seeing.
  991. βλέπω a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively): behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.
  992. βλητέος from βάλλω; fit to be cast (i.e. applied): must be put.
  993. Βοανεργές of Chaldee origin (בְּנֵי and רְגַז); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles: Boanerges.
  994. βοάω apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way): cry.
  995. βοή from βοάω; a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.): cry.
  996. βοήθεια from βοηθός; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel: help.
  997. βοηθέω from βοηθός; to aid or relieve: help, succor.
  998. βοηθός from βοή and theo (to run); a succorer: helper.
  999. βόθυνος akin to βαθύνω; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern: ditch, pit.
  1000. βολή from βάλλω; a throw (as a measure of distance): cast.
  1001. βολίζω from βολίς; to heave the lead: sound.
  1002. βολίς from βάλλω; a missile, i.e. javelin: dart.
  1003. Βοόζ of Hebrew origin (בֹּ֫עַז); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite: Booz.
  1004. βόρβορος of uncertain derivation; mud: mire.
  1005. βοῤῥᾶς of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind): north.
  1006. βόσκω a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare βιβρώσκω, βοῦς); to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze: feed, keep.
  1007. Βοσόρ of Hebrew origin (בְּעוֹר); Bosor (i.e. Beor), a Moabite: Bosor.
  1008. βοτάνη from βόσκω; herbage (as if for grazing): herb.
  1009. βότρυς of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes): (vine) cluster (of the vine).
  1010. βουλευτής from βουλεύω; an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin: counsellor.
  1011. βουλεύω from βουλή; to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve: consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose.
  1012. βουλή from βούλομαι; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose: + advise, counsel, will.
  1013. βούλημα from βούλομαι; a resolve: purpose, will.
  1014. βούλομαι middle voice of a primary verb; to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be willing: be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing). Compare θέλω.
  1015. βουνός probably of foreign origin; a hillock: hill.
  1016. βοῦς probably from the base of βόσκω; an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of that species ("beef"): ox.
  1017. βραβεῖον from brabeus (an umpire of uncertain derivation); an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games: prize.
  1018. βραβεύω from the same as βραβεῖον; to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail): rule.
  1019. βραδύνω from βραδύς; to delay: be slack, tarry.
  1020. βραδυπλοέω from βραδύς and a prolonged form of πλέω; to sail slowly: sail slowly.
  1021. βραδύς of uncertain affinity; slow; figuratively, dull: slow.
  1022. βραδύτης from βραδύς; tardiness: slackness.
  1023. βραχίων properly, comparative of βραχύς, but apparently in the sense of brasso (to wield); the arm, i.e. (figuratively) strength: arm.
  1024. βραχύς of uncertain affinity; short (of time, place, quantity, or number): few words, little (space, while).
  1025. βρέφος of uncertain affinity; an infant (properly, unborn) literally or figuratively: babe, (young) child, infant.
  1026. βρέχω a primary verb; to moisten (especially by a shower): (send) rain, wash.
  1027. βροντή akin to bremo (to roar); thunder: thunder(-ing).
  1028. βροχή from βρέχω; rain: rain.
  1029. βρόχος of uncertain derivation; a noose: snare.
  1030. βρυγμός from βρύχω; a grating (of the teeth): gnashing.
  1031. βρύχω a primary verb; to grate the teeth (in pain or rage): gnash.
  1032. βρύω a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush: send forth.
  1033. βρῶμα from the base of βιβρώσκω; food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law: meat, victuals.
  1034. βρώσιμος from βρῶσις; eatable: meat.
  1035. βρῶσις from the base of βιβρώσκω; (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively): eating, food, meat.
  1036. βυθίζω from βυθός; to sink; by implication, to drown: begin to sink, drown.
  1037. βυθός a variation of βάθος; depth, i.e. (by implication) the sea: deep.
  1038. βυρσεύς from bursa (a hide); a tanner: tanner.
  1039. βύσσινος from βύσσος; made of linen (neuter a linen cloth): fine linen.
  1040. βύσσος of Hebrew origin (בּוּץ); white linen: fine linen.
  1041. βωμός from the base of βάσις; properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar: altar.
  1042. γαββαθά of Chaldee origin (compare גַּב); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem: Gabbatha.
  1043. Γαβριήλ of Hebrew origin (גַּבְרִיאֵל); Gabriel, an archangel: Gabriel.
  1044. γάγγραινα from graino (to gnaw); an ulcer ("gangrene"): canker.
  1045. Γάδ of Hebrew origin (גָּד); Gad, a tribe of Israelites: Gad.
  1046. Γαδαρηνός from Gadara (a town east of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara: Gadarene.
  1047. γάζα of foreign origin; a treasure: treasure.
  1048. Γάζα of Hebrew origin (עַזָּה); Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine: Gaza.
  1049. γαζοφυλάκιον from γάζα and φυλακή; a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for the collection-boxes: treasury.
  1050. Γάϊος of Latin origin; Gaius (i.e. Caius), a Christian: Gaius.
  1051. γάλα of uncertain affinity; milk (figuratively): milk.
  1052. Γαλάτης from Γαλατία; a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia: Galatian.
  1053. Γαλατία of foreign origin; Galatia, a region of Asia: Galatia.
  1054. Γαλατικός from Γαλατία; Galatic or relating to Galatia: of Galatia.
  1055. γαλήνη of uncertain derivation; tranquillity: calm.
  1056. Γαλιλαία of Hebrew origin (גָּלִיל); Galilæa (i.e. the heathen circle), a region of Palestine: Galilee.
  1057. Γαλιλαῖος from Γαλιλαία; Galilean or belonging to Galilea: Galilean, of Galilee.
  1058. Γαλλίων of Latin origin; Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer: Gallio.
  1059. Γαμαλιήλ of Hebrew origin (גַּמְלִיאֵל); Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an Israelite: Gamaliel.
  1060. γαμέω from γάμος; to wed (of either sex): marry (a wife).
  1061. γαμίσκω from γάμος; to espouse (a daughter to a husband): give in marriage.
  1062. γάμος of uncertain affinity; nuptials: marriage, wedding.
  1063. γάρ a primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles): and, as, because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet.
  1064. γαστήρ of uncertain derivation; the stomach; by analogy, the matrix; figuratively, a gourmand: belly, + with child, womb.
  1065. γέ a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed): and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.
  1066. Γεδεών of Hebrew origin (גִּדְעוֹן); Gedeon (i.e. Gid(e)on), an Israelite: Gedeon (in the King James Version).
  1067. γέεννα of Hebrew origin (גָּיְא and הִנֹּם); valley of (the son of) Hinnom; ge-henna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment: hell.
  1068. Γεθσημανῆ of Chaldee origin (compare גַּת and שָׁ֫מֶן); oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem: Gethsemane.
  1069. γείτων from γῆ; a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a friend: neighbour.
  1070. γελάω of uncertain affinity; to laugh (as a sign of joy or satisfaction): laugh.
  1071. γέλως from γελάω; laughter (as a mark of gratification): laughter.
  1072. γεμίζω transitive from γέμω; to fill entirely: fill (be) full.
  1073. γέμω a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. be full: be full.
  1074. γενεά from (a presumed derivative of) γένος; a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons): age, generation, nation, time.
  1075. γενεαλογέω from γενεά and λόγος; to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in genealogy: count by descent.
  1076. γενεαλογία from the same as γενεαλογέω; tracing by generations, i.e. "genealogy": genealogy.
  1077. γενέσια neuter plural of a derivative of γένεσις; birthday ceremonies: birthday.
  1078. γένεσις from the same as γενεά; nativity; figuratively, nature: generation, nature(-ral).
  1079. γενετή feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of γενεά; birth: birth.
  1080. γεννάω from a variation of γένος; to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate: bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring.
  1081. γέννημα from γεννάω; offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or figuratively): fruit, generation.
  1082. Γεννησαρέτ of Hebrew origin (compare כִּנָּ֫רֶת); Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine: Gennesaret.
  1083. γέννησις from γεννάω; nativity: birth.
  1084. γεννητός from γεννάω; born: they that are born.
  1085. γένος from γίνομαι; "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective): born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock.
  1086. Γεργεσηνός of Hebrew origin (גִּרְגָּשִׁי); a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine: Gergesene.
  1087. γερουσία from γέρων; the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin: senate.
  1088. γέρων of uncertain affinity (compare γῆρας); aged: old.
  1089. γεύομαι a primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill): eat, taste.
  1090. γεωργέω from γεωργός; to till (the soil): dress.
  1091. γεώργιον neuter of a (presumed) derivative of γεωργός; cultivable, i.e. a farm: husbandry.
  1092. γεωργός from γῆ and the base of ἔργον; a land-worker, i.e. farmer: husbandman.
  1093. γῆ contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application): country, earth(-ly), ground, land, world.
  1094. γῆρας akin to γέρων; senility: old age.
  1095. γηράσκω from γῆρας; to be senescent: be (wax) old.
  1096. γίνομαι a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.): arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.
  1097. γινώσκω a prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed): allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand.
  1098. γλεῦκος akin to γλυκύς; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine: new wine.
  1099. γλυκύς of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. not bitter nor salt): sweet, fresh.
  1100. γλῶσσα of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired): tongue.
  1101. γλωσσόκομον from γλῶσσα and the base of κόσμος; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse: bag.
  1102. γναφεύς by variation for a derivative from knapto (to tease cloth); a cloth-dresser: fuller.
  1103. γνήσιος from the same as γενέσια; legitimate (of birth), i.e. genuine: own, sincerity, true.
  1104. γνησίως adverb from γνήσιος; genuinely, i.e. really: naturally.
  1105. γνόφος akin to νέφος; gloom (as of a storm): blackness.
  1106. γνώμη from γινώσκω; cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.): advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will.
  1107. γνωρίζω from a derivative of γινώσκω; to make known; subjectively, to know: certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.
  1108. γνῶσις from γινώσκω; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication) knowledge: knowledge, science.
  1109. γνώστης from γινώσκω; a knower: expert.
  1110. γνωστός from γινώσκω; well-known: acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.
  1111. γογγύζω of uncertain derivation; to grumble: murmur.
  1112. γογγυσμός from γογγύζω; a grumbling: grudging, murmuring.
  1113. γογγυστής from γογγύζω; a grumbler: murmurer.
  1114. γόης from goao (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter: seducer.
  1115. Γολγοθᾶ of Chaldee origin (compare גֻּלְגֹּ֫לֶת); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem: Golgotha.
  1116. Γόμοῤῥα of Hebrew origin (עֲמֹרָה); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea: Gomorrha.
  1117. γόμος from γέμω; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares: burden, merchandise.
  1118. γονεύς from the base of γίνομαι; a parent: parent.
  1119. γόνυ of uncertain affinity; the "knee": knee(X -l).
  1120. γονυπετέω from a compound of γόνυ and the alternate of πίπτω; to fall on the knee: bow the knee, kneel down.
  1121. γράμμα from γράφω; a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning: bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.
  1122. γραμματεύς from γράμμα. a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary: scribe, town-clerk.
  1123. γραπτός from γράφω; inscribed (figuratively): written.
  1124. γραφή from γράφω; a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it): scripture.
  1125. γράφω a primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe: describe, write(-ing, -ten).
  1126. γραώδης from graus (an old woman) and εἶδος; crone-like, i.e. silly: old wives'.
  1127. γρηγορεύω from ἐγείρω; to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively): be vigilant, wake, (be) watch(-ful).
  1128. γυμνάζω from γυμνός; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively): exercise.
  1129. γυμνασία from γυμνάζω; training, i.e. (figuratively) asceticism: exercise.
  1130. γυμνητεύω from a derivative of γυμνός; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad: be naked.
  1131. γυμνός of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative): naked.
  1132. γυμνότης from γυμνός; nudity (absolute or comparative): nakedness.
  1133. γυναικάριον a diminutive from γυνή; a little (i.e. foolish) woman: silly woman.
  1134. γυναικεῖος from γυνή; feminine: wife.
  1135. γυνή probably from the base of γίνομαι; a woman; specially, a wife: wife, woman.
  1136. Γώγ of Hebrew origin (גּוֹג); Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist: Gog.
  1137. γωνία probably akin to γόνυ; an angle: corner, quarter.
  1138. Δαβίδ of Hebrew origin (דָּוִיד); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king: David.
  1139. δαιμονίζομαι middle voice from δαίμων; to be exercised by a dæmon: have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil(-s).
  1140. δαιμόνιον neuter of a derivative of δαίμων; a dæmonic being; by extension a deity: devil, god.
  1141. δαιμονιώδης from δαιμόνιον and δαίμων; dæmon-like: devilish.
  1142. δαίμων from daio (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature): devil.
  1143. δάκνω a prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively) thwart: bite.
  1144. δάκρυ or dakruon of uncertain affinity; a tear: tear.
  1145. δακρύω from δάκρυ; to shed tears: weep. Compare κλαίω.
  1146. δακτύλιος from δάκτυλος; a finger-ring: ring.
  1147. δάκτυλος probably from δέκα; a finger: finger.
  1148. Δαλμανουθά probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine: Dalmanutha.
  1149. Δαλματία probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of Europe: Dalmatia.
  1150. δαμάζω a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame: tame.
  1151. δάμαλις probably from the base of δαμάζω; a heifer (as tame): heifer.
  1152. Δάμαρις probably from the base of δαμάζω; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman: Damaris.
  1153. Δαμασκηνός from Δαμασκός; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus: Damascene.
  1154. Δαμασκός of Hebrew origin (NONE); Damascus, a city of Syria: Damascus.
  1155. δανείζω from δάνειον; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow: borrow, lend.
  1156. δάνειον from danos (a gift); probably akin to the base of δίδωμι; a loan: debt.
  1157. δανειστής from δανείζω; a lender: creditor.
  1158. Δανιήλ of Hebrew origin (דָּנִיֵּאל); Daniel, an Israelite: Daniel.
  1159. δαπανάω from δαπάνη; to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste: be at charges, consume, spend.
  1160. δαπάνη from dapto (to devour); expense (as consuming): cost.
  1161. δέ a primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and, etc.: also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English).
  1162. δέησις from δέομαι; a petition: prayer, request, supplication.
  1163. δεῖ 3rd person singular active present of δέω; also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding): behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should.
  1164. δεῖγμα from the base of δεικνύω; a specimen (as shown): example.
  1165. δειγματίζω from δεῖγμα; to exhibit: make a shew.
  1166. δεικνύω a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show (literally or figuratively): shew.
  1167. δειλία from δειλός; timidity: fear.
  1168. δειλιάω from δειλία; to be timid: be afraid.
  1169. δειλός from deos (dread); timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless: fearful.
  1170. δεῖνα probably from the same as δεινῶς (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange); so and so (when the person is not specified): such a man.
  1171. δεινῶς adverb from a derivative of the same as δειλός; terribly, i.e. excessively: grievously, vehemently.
  1172. δειπνέω from δεῖπνον; to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal: sup (X -er).
  1173. δεῖπνον from the same as δαπάνη; dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the evening): feast, supper.
  1174. δεισιδαιμονέστερος the compound of a derivative of the base of δειλός and δαίμων; more religious than others: too superstitious.
  1175. δεισιδαιμονία from the same as δεισιδαιμονέστερος; religion: superstition.
  1176. δέκα a primary number; ten: (eight-)een, ten.
  1177. δεκαδύο from δέκα and δύο; two and ten, i.e. twelve: twelve.
  1178. δεκαπέντε from δέκα and πέντε; ten and five, i.e. fifteen: fifteen.
  1179. Δεκάπολις from δέκα and πόλις; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria: Decapolis.
  1180. δεκατέσσαρες from δέκα and τέσσαρες; ten and four, i.e. fourteen: fourteen.
  1181. δεκάτη feminine of δέκατος; a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe: tenth (part), tithe.
  1182. δέκατος ordinal from δέκα; tenth: tenth.
  1183. δεκατόω from δεκάτη; to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth: pay (receive) tithes.
  1184. δεκτός from δέχομαι; approved; (figuratively) propitious: accepted(-table).
  1185. δελεάζω from the base of δόλος; to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude: allure, beguile, entice.
  1186. δένδρον probably from drus (an oak); a tree: tree.
  1187. δεξιολάβος from δεξιός and λαμβάνω; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier: spearman.
  1188. δεξιός from δέχομαι; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes): right (hand, side).
  1189. δέομαι middle voice of δέω; to beg (as binding oneself), i.e. petition: beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare πυνθάνομαι.
  1190. Δερβαῖος from Δέρβη; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe: of Derbe.
  1191. Δέρβη of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor: Derbe.
  1192. δέρμα from δέρω; a hide: skin.
  1193. δερμάτινος from δέρμα; made of hide: leathern, of a skin.
  1194. δέρω a primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash: beat, smite.
  1195. δεσμεύω from a (presumed) derivative of δεσμέω; to be a binder (captor), i.e. to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load): bind.
  1196. δεσμέω from δεσμόν; to tie, i.e. shackle: bind.
  1197. δέσμη from δεσμέω; a bundle: bundle.
  1198. δέσμιος from δεσμόν; a captive (as bound): in bonds, prisoner.
  1199. δεσμόν or desmos neuter and masculine respectively from δέω; a band, i.e. ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or disability: band, bond, chain, string.
  1200. δεσμοφύλαξ from δεσμόν and φύλαξ; a jailer (as guarding the prisoners): jailor, keeper of the prison.
  1201. δεσμωτήριον from a derivative of δεσμόν (equivalent to δεσμέω); a place of bondage, i.e. a dungeon: prison.
  1202. δεσμώτης from the same as δεσμωτήριον; (passively) a captive: prisoner.
  1203. δεσπότης perhaps from δέω and posis (a husband); an absolute ruler ("despot"): Lord, master.
  1204. δεῦρο of uncertain affinity; here; used also imperative hither!; and of time, hitherto: come (hither), hither(-to).
  1205. δεῦτε from δεῦρο and an imperative form of eimi (to go); come hither!: come, X follow.
  1206. δευτεραῖος from δεύτερος; secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day: next day.
  1207. δευτερόπρωτος from δεύτερος and πρῶτος; second-first, i.e. (specially) a designation of the Sabbath immediately after the Paschal week (being the second after Passover day, and the first of the seven Sabbaths intervening before Pentecost): second … after the first.
  1208. δεύτερος as the comparative of δύο; (ordinal) second (in time, place, or rank; also adverb): afterward, again, second(-arily, time).
  1209. δέχομαι middle voice of a primary verb; to receive (in various applications, literally or figuratively): accept, receive, take. Compare λαμβάνω.
  1210. δέω a primary verb; to bind (in various applications, literally or figuratively): bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also δεῖ, δέομαι.
  1211. δή probably akin to δέ; a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now, then, etc.: also, and, doubtless, now, therefore.
  1212. δῆλος of uncertain derivation; clear: + bewray, certain, evident, manifest.
  1213. δηλόω from δῆλος; to make plain (by words): declare, shew, signify.
  1214. Δημᾶς probably for Δημήτριος; Demas, a Christian: Demas.
  1215. δημηγορέω from a compound of δῆμος and ἀγορά; to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to address a public assembly: make an oration.
  1216. Δημήτριος from Demeter (Ceres); Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian: Demetrius.
  1217. δημιουργός from δῆμος and ἔργον; a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of the Creator): maker.
  1218. δῆμος from δέω; the public (as bound together socially): people.
  1219. δημόσιος from δῆμος; public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in public: common, openly, publickly.
  1220. δηνάριον of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses): pence, penny(-worth).
  1221. δήποτε from δή and ποτέ; a particle of generalization; indeed, at any time: (what-)soever.
  1222. δήπου from δή and πού; a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless: verily.
  1223. διά a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very wide applications, local, causal, or occasional): after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) … fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with (-in). In composition it retains the same general importance.
  1224. διαβαίνω from διά and the base of βάσις; to cross: come over, pass (through).
  1225. διαβάλλω from διά and βάλλω; (figuratively) to traduce: accuse.
  1226. διαβεβαιόομαι middle voice of a compound of διά and βεβαιόω; to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. asseverate: affirm constantly.
  1227. διαβλέπω from διά and βλέπω; to look through, i.e. recover full vision: see clearly.
  1228. διάβολος from διαβάλλω; a traducer; specially, Satan (compare שָׂטָן): false accuser, devil, slanderer.
  1229. διαγγέλλω from διά and the base of ἄγγελος; to herald thoroughly: declare, preach, signify.
  1230. διαγίνομαι from διά and γίνομαι; to elapse meanwhile: X after, be past, be spent.
  1231. διαγινώσκω from διά and γινώσκω; to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain exactly: (would) enquire, know the uttermost.
  1232. διαγνωρίζω from γραπτός and γνωρίζω; to tell abroad: make known.
  1233. διάγνωσις from διαγινώσκω; (magisterial) examination ("diagnosis"): hearing.
  1234. διαγογγύζω from διά and γογγύζω; to complain throughout a crowd: murmur.
  1235. διαγρηγορέω from διά and γρηγορεύω; to waken thoroughly: be awake.
  1236. διάγω from διά and ἄγω; to pass time or life: lead life, living.
  1237. διαδέχομαι from διά and δέχομαι; to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to: come after.
  1238. διάδημα from a compound of διά and δέω; a "diadem" (as bound about the head): crown. Compare στέφανος.
  1239. διαδίδωμι from διά and δίδωμι; to give throughout a crowd, i.e. deal out; also to deliver over (as to a successor): (make) distribute(-ion), divide, give.
  1240. διάδοχος from διαδέχομαι; a successor in office: room.
  1241. διαζώννυμι from διά and ζώννυμι; to gird tightly: gird.
  1242. διαθήκη from διατίθεμαι; properly, a disposition, i.e. (specially) a contract (especially a devisory will): covenant, testament.
  1243. διαίρεσις from διαιρέω; a distinction or (concretely) variety: difference, diversity.
  1244. διαιρέω from διά and αἱρέομαι; to separate, i.e. distribute: divide.
  1245. διακαθαρίζω from διά and καθαρίζω; to cleanse perfectly, i.e. (specially) winnow: thoroughly purge.
  1246. διακατελέγχομαι middle voice from διά and a compound of κατά and ἐλέγχω; to prove downright, i.e. confute: convince.
  1247. διακονέω from διάκονος; to be an attendant, i.e. wait upon (menially or as a host, friend, or (figuratively) teacher); technically, to act as a Christian deacon: (ad-)minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon.
  1248. διακονία from διάκονος; attendance (as a servant, etc.); figuratively (eleemosynary) aid, (official) service (especially of the Christian teacher, or technically of the diaconate): (ad-)minister(-ing, -tration, -try), office, relief, service(-ing).
  1249. διάκονος probably from an obsolete diako (to run on errands; compare διώκω); an attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a deacon or deaconess): deacon, minister, servant.
  1250. διακόσιοι from δίς and ἑκατόν; two hundred: two hundred.
  1251. διακούομαι middle voice from διά and ἀκούω; to hear throughout, i.e. patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea): hear.
  1252. διακρίνω from διά and κρίνω; to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose; figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or (reflexively) hesitate: contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver.
  1253. διάκρισις from διακρίνω; judicial estimation: discern(-ing), disputation.
  1254. διακωλύω from διά and κωλύω; to hinder altogether, i.e. utterly prohibit: forbid.
  1255. διαλαλέω from διά and λαλέω; to talk throughout a company, i.e. converse or (genitive case) publish: commune, noise abroad.
  1256. διαλέγομαι middle voice from διά and λέγω; to say thoroughly, i.e. discuss (in argument or exhortation): dispute, preach (unto), reason (with), speak.
  1257. διαλείπω from διά and λείπω; to leave off in the middle, i.e. intermit: cease.
  1258. διάλεκτος from διαλέγομαι; a (mode of) discourse, i.e. "dialect": language, tongue.
  1259. διαλλάσσω from διά and ἀλλάσσω; to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to conciliate: reconcile.
  1260. διαλογίζομαι from διά and λογίζομαι; to reckon thoroughly, i.e. (genitive case) to deliberate (by reflection or discussion): cast in mind, consider, dispute, muse, reason, think.
  1261. διαλογισμός from διαλογίζομαι; discussion, i.e. (internal) consideration (by implication, purpose), or (external) debate: dispute, doubtful(-ing), imagination, reasoning, thought.
  1262. διαλύω from διά and λύω; to dissolve utterly: scatter.
  1263. διαμαρτύρομαι from διά and μαρτυρέω; to attest or protest earnestly, or (by implication) hortatively: charge, testify (unto), witness.
  1264. διαμάχομαι from διά and μάχομαι; to fight fiercely (in altercation): strive.
  1265. διαμένω from διά and μένω; to stay constantly (in being or relation): continue, remain.
  1266. διαμερίζω from διά and μερίζω; to partition thoroughly (literally in distribution, figuratively in dissension): cloven, divide, part.
  1267. διαμερισμός from διαμερίζω; disunion (of opinion and conduct): division.
  1268. διανέμω from διά and the base of νόμος; to distribute, i.e. (of information) to disseminate: spread.
  1269. διανεύω from διά and νεύω; to nod (or express by signs) across an intervening space: beckon.
  1270. διανόημα from a compound of διά and νοιέω; something thought through, i.e. a sentiment: thought.
  1271. διάνοια from διά and νοῦς; deep thought, properly, the faculty (mind or its disposition), by implication, its exercise: imagination, mind, understanding.
  1272. διανοίγω from διά and ἀνοίγω; to open thoroughly, literally (as a first-born) or figuratively (to expound): open.
  1273. διανυκτερεύω from διά and a derivative of νύξ; to sit up the whole night: continue all night.
  1274. διανύω from διά and anuo (to effect); to accomplish thoroughly: finish.
  1275. διαπαντός from διά and the genitive case of πᾶς; through all time, i.e. (adverbially) constantly: alway(-s), continually.
  1276. διαπεράω from διά and a derivative of the base of πέραν; to cross entirely: go over, pass (over), sail over.
  1277. διαπλέω from διά and πλέω; to sail through: sail over.
  1278. διαπονέω from διά and a derivative of πόνος; to toil through, i.e. (passively) be worried: be grieved.
  1279. διαπορεύομαι from διά and πορεύομαι; to travel through: go through, journey in, pass by.
