  1994. ἐπιστρέφω from ἐπί and στρέφω; to revert (literally, figuratively or morally): come (go) again, convert, (re-)turn (about, again).
  1995. ἐπιστροφή from ἐπιστρέφω; reversion, i.e. morally, revolution: conversion.
  1996. ἐπισυνάγω from ἐπί and συνάγω; to collect upon the same place: gather (together).
  1997. ἐπισυναγωγή from ἐπισυνάγω; a complete collection; especially a Christian meeting (for worship): assembling (gathering) together.
  1998. ἐπισυντρέχω from ἐπί and συντρέχω; to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion): come running together.
  1999. ἐπισύστασις from the middle voice of a compound of ἐπί and συνιστάω; a conspiracy, i.e. concourse (riotous or friendly): that which cometh upon, + raising up.
  2000. ἐπισφαλής from a compound of ἐπί and sphallo (to trip); figuratively, insecure: dangerous.
  2001. ἐπισχύω from ἐπί and ἰσχύω; to avail further, i.e. (figuratively) insist stoutly: be the more fierce.
  2002. ἐπισωρεύω from ἐπί and σωρεύω; to accumulate further, i.e. (figuratively) seek additionally: heap.
  2003. ἐπιταγή from ἐπιτάσσω; an injunction or decree; by implication, authoritativeness: authority, commandment.
  2004. ἐπιτάσσω from ἐπί and τάσσω; to arrange upon, i.e. order: charge, command, injoin.
  2005. ἐπιτελέω from ἐπί and τελέω; to fulfill further (or completely), i.e. execute; by implication, to terminate, undergo: accomplish, do, finish, (make) (perfect), perform(X -ance).
  2006. ἐπιτήδειος from epitedes (enough); serviceable, i.e. (by implication) requisite: things which are needful.
  2007. ἐπιτίθημι from ἐπί and τίθημι; to impose (in a friendly or hostile sense): add unto, lade, lay upon, put (up) on, set on (up), + surname, X wound.
  2008. ἐπιτιμάω from ἐπί and τιμάω; to tax upon, i.e. censure or admonish; by implication, forbid: (straitly) charge, rebuke.
  2009. ἐπιτιμία from a compound of ἐπί and τιμή; properly, esteem, i.e. citizenship; used (in the sense of ἐπιτιμάω) of a penalty: punishment.
  2010. ἐπιτρέπω from ἐπί and the base of τροπή; to turn over (transfer), i.e. allow: give leave (liberty, license), let, permit, suffer.
  2011. ἐπιτροπή from ἐπιτρέπω; permission, i.e. (by implication) full power: commission.
  2012. ἐπίτροπος from ἐπί and τρόπος (in the sense of ἐπιτροπή); a commissioner, i.e. domestic manager, guardian: steward, tutor.
  2013. ἐπιτυγχάνω from ἐπί and τυγχάνω; to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) to attain: obtain.
  2014. ἐπιφαίνω from ἐπί and φαίνω; to shine upon, i.e. become (literally) visible or (figuratively) known: appear, give light.
  2015. ἐπιφάνεια from ἐπιφανής; a manifestation, i.e. (specially) the advent of Christ (past or future): appearing, brightness.
  2016. ἐπιφανής from ἐπιφαίνω; conspicuous, i.e. (figuratively) memorable: notable.
  2017. ἐπιφαύω a form of ἐπιφαίνω; to illuminate (figuratively): give light.
  2018. ἐπιφέρω from ἐπί and φέρω; to bear upon (or further), i.e. adduce (personally or judicially (accuse, inflict)), superinduce: add, bring (against), take.
  2019. ἐπιφωνέω from ἐπί and φωνέω; to call at something, i.e. exclaim: cry (against), give a shout.
  2020. ἐπιφώσκω a form of ἐπιφαύω; to begin to grow light: begin to dawn, X draw on.
  2021. ἐπιχειρέω from ἐπί and χείρ; to put the hand upon, i.e. undertake: go about, take in hand (upon).
  2022. ἐπιχέω from ἐπί and cheo (to pour); --to pour upon: pour in.
  2023. ἐπιχορηγέω from ἐπί and χορηγέω; to furnish besides, i.e. fully supply, (figuratively) aid or contribute: add, minister (nourishment, unto).
  2024. ἐπιχορηγία from ἐπιχορηγέω; contribution: supply.
  2025. ἐπιχρίω from ἐπί and χρίω; to smear over: anoint.
  2026. ἐποικοδομέω from ἐπί and οἰκοδομέω; to build upon, i.e. (figuratively) to rear up: build thereon (thereupon, on, upon).
  2027. ἐποκέλλω from ἐπί and okello (to urge); to drive upon the shore, i.e. to beach a vessel: run aground.
  2028. ἐπονομάζω from ἐπί and ὀνομάζω; to name further, i.e. denominate: call.
  2029. ἐποπτεύω from ἐπί and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; to inspect, i.e. watch: behold.
  2030. ἐπόπτης from ἐπί and a presumed derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; a looker-on: eye-witness.
  2031. ἔπος from ἔπω; a word: X say.
  2032. ἐπουράνιος from ἐπί and οὐρανός; above the sky: celestial, (in) heaven(-ly), high.
  2033. ἑπτά a primary number; seven: seven.
  2034. ἑπτάκις adverb from ἑπτά; seven times: seven times.
  2035. ἑπτακισχίλιοι from ἑπτάκις and χίλιοι; seven times a thousand: seven thousand.
  2036. ἔπω a primary verb (used only in the definite past tense, the others being borrowed from ἐρέω, ῥέω, and φημί); to speak or say (by word or writing): answer, bid, bring word, call, command, grant, say (on), speak, tell. Compare λέγω.
  2037. Ἔραστος from erao (to love); beloved; Erastus, a Christian: Erastus.
  2038. ἐργάζομαι middle voice from ἔργον; to toil (as a task, occupation, etc.), (by implication) effect, be engaged in or with, etc.: commit, do, labor for, minister about, trade (by), work.
  2039. ἐργασία from ἐργάτης; occupation; by implication, profit, pains: craft, diligence, gain, work.
  2040. ἐργάτης from ἔργον; a toiler; figuratively, a teacher: labourer, worker(-men).
  2041. ἔργον from a primary (but obsolete) ergo (to work); toil (as an effort or occupation); by implication, an act: deed, doing, labour, work.
  2042. ἐρεθίζω from a presumed prolonged form of ἔρις; to stimulate (especially to anger): provoke.
  2043. ἐρείδω of obscure affinity; to prop, i.e. (reflexively) get fast: stick fast.
  2044. ἐρεύγομαι of uncertain affinity; to belch, i.e. (figuratively) to speak out: utter.
  2045. ἐρευνάω apparently from ἐρέω (through the idea of inquiry); to seek, i.e. (figuratively) to investigate: search.
  2046. ἐρέω probably a fuller form of ῥέω; an alternate for ἔπω in certain tenses; to utter, i.e. speak or say: call, say, speak (of), tell.
  2047. ἐρημία from ἔρημος; solitude (concretely): desert, wilderness.
  2048. ἔρημος of uncertain affinity; lonesome, i.e. (by implication) waste (usually as a noun, χώρα being implied): desert, desolate, solitary, wilderness.
  2049. ἐρημόω from ἔρημος; to lay waste (literally or figuratively): (bring to, make) desolate(-ion), come to nought.
  2050. ἐρήμωσις from ἐρημόω; despoliation: desolation.
  2051. ἐρίζω from ἔρις; to wrangle: strive.
  2052. ἐριθεία perhaps as the same as ἐρεθίζω; properly, intrigue, i.e. (by implication) faction: contention(-ious), strife.
  2053. ἔριον of obscure affinity; wool: wool.
  2054. ἔρις of uncertain affinity; a quarrel, i.e. (by implication) wrangling: contention, debate, strife, variance.
  2055. ἐρίφιον from ἔριφος; a kidling, i.e. (genitive case) goat (symbolically, wicked person): goat.
  2056. ἔριφος perhaps from the same as ἔριον (through the idea of hairiness); a kid or (genitive case) goat: goat, kid.
  2057. Ἑρμᾶς probably from Ἑρμῆς; Hermas, a Christian: Hermas.
  2058. ἑρμηνεία from the same as ἑρμηνεύω; translation: interpretation.
  2059. ἑρμηνεύω from a presumed derivative of Ἑρμῆς (as the god of language); to translate: interpret.
  2060. Ἑρμῆς perhaps from ἐρέω; Hermes, the name of the messenger of the Greek deities; also of a Christian: Hermes, Mercury.
  2061. Ἑρμογένης from Ἑρμῆς and γίνομαι; born of Hermes; Hermogenes, an apostate Christian: Hermogenes.
  2062. ἑρπετόν neuter of a derivative of herpo (to creep); a reptile, i.e. (by Hebraism (compare רֶ֫מֶשׂ)) a small animal: creeping thing, serpent.
  2063. ἐρυθρός of uncertain affinity; red, i.e. (with θάλασσα) the Red Sea: red.
  2064. ἔρχομαι middle voice of a primary verb (used only in the present and imperfect tenses, the others being supplied by a kindred (middle voice) eleuthomai el-yoo'-thom-ahee, or (active) eltho el'-tho, which do not otherwise occur); to come or go (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively): accompany, appear, bring, come, enter, fall out, go, grow, X light, X next, pass, resort, be set.
  2065. ἐρωτάω apparently from ἐρέω (compare ἐρευνάω); to interrogate; by implication, to request: ask, beseech, desire, intreat, pray. Compare πυνθάνομαι.
  2066. ἐσθής from hennumi (to clothe); dress: apparel, clothing, raiment, robe.
  2067. ἔσθησις from a derivative of ἐσθής; clothing (concretely): government.
  2068. ἐσθίω strengthened for a primary edo (to eat); used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by φάγω; to eat (usually literal): devour, eat, live.
  2069. Ἐσλί of Hebrew origin (probably for אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי); Esli, an Israelite: Esli.
  2070. ἐσμέν first person plural indicative of εἰμί; we are: are, be, have our being, X have hope, + (the gospel) was (preached unto) us.
  2071. ἔσομαι future of εἰμί; will be: shall (should) be (have), (shall) come (to pass), X may have, X fall, what would follow, X live long, X sojourn.
  2072. ἔσοπτρον from εἰς and a presumed derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; a mirror (for looking into): glass. Compare κατοπτρίζομαι.
  2073. ἑσπέρα feminine of an adjective hesperos (evening); the eve (ὥρα being implied): evening(-tide).
  2074. Ἐσρώμ of Hebrew origin (חֶצְרוֹן); Esrom (i.e. Chetsron), an Israelite: Esrom.
  2075. ἐστέ second person plural present indicative of εἰμί; ye are: be, have been, belong.
  2076. ἐστί third person singular present indicative of εἰμί; he (she or it) is; also (with neuter plural) they are: are, be(-long), call, X can(-not), come, consisteth, X dure for a while, + follow, X have, (that) is (to say), make, meaneth, X must needs, + profit, + remaineth, + wrestle.
  2077. ἔστω second person singular present imperative of εἰμί; be thou; also estosan, third person of the same let them be: be.
  2078. ἔσχατος a superlative probably from ἔχω (in the sense of contiguity); farthest, final (of place or time): ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost.
  2079. ἐσχάτως adverb from ἔσχατος; finally, i.e. (with ἔχω) at the extremity of life: point of death.
  2080. ἔσω from εἰς; inside (as preposition or adjective): (with-)in(-ner, -to, -ward).
  2081. ἔσωθεν from ἔσω; from inside; also used as equivalent to ἔσω (inside): inward(-ly), (from) within, without.
  2082. ἐσώτερος comparative of ἔσω; interior: inner, within.
  2083. ἑταῖρος from etes (a clansman); a comrade: fellow, friend.
  2084. ἑτερόγλωσσος from ἕτερος and γλῶσσα; other- tongued, i.e. a foreigner: man of other tongue.
  2085. ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω from ἕτερος and διδάσκαλος; to instruct differently: teach other doctrine(-wise).
  2086. ἑτεροζυγέω from a compound of ἕτερος and ζυγός; to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly: unequally yoke together with.
  2087. ἕτερος of uncertain affinity; (an-, the) other or different: altered, else, next (day), one, (an-)other, some, strange.
  2088. ἑτέρως adverb from ἕτερος; differently: otherwise.
  2089. ἔτι perhaps akin to ἔτος; "yet," still (of time or degree): after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet.
  2090. ἑτοιμάζω from ἕτοιμος; to prepare: prepare, provide, make ready. Compare κατασκευάζω.
  2091. ἑτοιμασία from ἑτοιμάζω; preparation: preparation.
  2092. ἕτοιμος from an old noun heteos (fitness); adjusted, i.e. ready: prepared, (made) ready(-iness, to our hand).
  2093. ἑτοίμως adverb from ἕτοιμος; in readiness: ready.
  2094. ἔτος apparently a primary word; a year: year.
  2095. εὖ neuter of a primary eus (good); (adverbially) well: good, well (done).
  2096. Εὖα of Hebrew origin (חַוָּה); Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman: Eve.
  2097. εὐαγγελίζω from εὖ and ἄγγελος; to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel: declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel).
  2098. εὐαγγέλιον from the same as εὐαγγελίζω; a good message, i.e. the gospel: gospel.
  2099. εὐαγγελιστής from εὐαγγελίζω; a preacher of the gospel: evangelist.
  2100. εὐαρεστέω from εὐάρεστος; to gratify entirely: please (well).
  2101. εὐάρεστος from εὖ and ἀρεστός; fully agreeable: acceptable(-ted), wellpleasing.
  2102. εὐαρέστως adverb from εὐάρεστος; quite agreeably: acceptably, + please well.
  2103. Εὔβουλος from εὖ and βούλομαι; good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian: Eubulus.
  2104. εὐγενής from εὖ and γίνομαι; well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous: more noble, nobleman.
  2105. εὐδία feminine from εὖ and the alternate of Ζεύς (as the god of the weather); a clear sky, i.e. fine weather: fair weather.
  2106. εὐδοκέω from εὖ and δοκέω; to think well of, i.e. approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing): think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing.
  2107. εὐδοκία from a presumed compound of εὖ and the base of δοκέω; satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose: desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good.
  2108. εὐεργεσία from εὐεργέτης; beneficence (genitive case or specially): benefit, good deed done.
  2109. εὐεργετέω from εὐεργέτης; to be philanthropic: do good.
  2110. εὐεργέτης from εὖ and the base of ἔργον; a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist: benefactor.
  2111. εὔθετος from εὖ and a derivative of τίθημι; well placed, i.e. (figuratively) appropriate: fit, meet.
  2112. εὐθέως adverb from εὐθύς; directly, i.e. at once or soon: anon, as soon as, forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway.
  2113. εὐθυδρομέω from εὐθύς and δρόμος; to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct: (come) with a straight course.
  2114. εὐθυμέω from εὔθυμος; to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully: be of good cheer (merry).
  2115. εὔθυμος from εὖ and θυμός; in fine spirits, i.e. cheerful: of good cheer, the more cheerfully.
  2116. εὐθύνω from εὐθύς; to straighten (level); technically, to steer: governor, make straight.
  2117. εὐθύς perhaps from εὖ and τίθημι; straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once: anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway.
  2118. εὐθύτης from εὐθύς; rectitude: righteousness.
  2119. εὐκαιρέω from εὔκαιρος; to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure: have leisure (convenient time), spend time.
  2120. εὐκαιρία from εὔκαιρος; a favorable occasion: opportunity.
  2121. εὔκαιρος from εὖ and καιρός; well-timed, i.e. opportune: convenient, in time of need.
  2122. εὐκαίρως adverb from εὔκαιρος; opportunely: conveniently, in season.
  2123. εὐκοπώτερος comparative of a compound of εὖ and κόπος; better for toil, i.e. more facile: easier.
  2124. εὐλάβεια from εὐλαβής; properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely): fear(-ed).
  2125. εὐλαβέομαι middle voice from εὐλαβής; to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence: (moved with) fear.
  2126. εὐλαβής from εὖ and λαμβάνω; taking well (carefully), i.e. circumspect (religiously, pious): devout.
  2127. εὐλογέω from a compound of εὖ and λόγος; to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper): bless, praise.
  2128. εὐλογητός from εὐλογέω; adorable: blessed.
  2129. εὐλογία from the same as εὐλογέω; fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess: blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech.
  2130. εὐμετάδοτος from εὖ and a presumed derivative of μεταδίδωμι; good at imparting, i.e. liberal: ready to distribute.
  2131. Εὐνίκη from εὖ and νίκη; victorious; Eunice, a Jewess: Eunice.
  2132. εὐνοέω from a compound of εὖ and νοῦς; to be well- minded, i.e. reconcile: agree.
  2133. εὔνοια from the same as εὐνοέω; kindness; euphemistically, conjugal duty: benevolence, good will.
  2134. εὐνουχίζω from εὐνοῦχος; to castrate (figuratively, live unmarried): make…eunuch.
  2135. εὐνοῦχος from eune (a bed) and ἔχω; a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer): eunuch.
  2136. Εὐοδία from the same as εὐοδόω; fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman: Euodias.
  2137. εὐοδόω from a compound of εὖ and ὁδός; to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs: (have a) prosper(-ous journey).
  2138. εὐπειθής from εὖ and πείθω; good for persuasion, i.e. (intransitively) complaint: easy to be intreated.
  2139. εὐπερίστατος from εὖ and a derivative of a presumed compound of περί and ἵστημι; well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case): which doth so easily beset.
  2140. εὐποιΐα from a compound of εὖ and ποιέω; well-doing, i.e. beneficence: to do good.
  2141. εὐπορέω from a compound of ἑτοιμάζω and the base of πορεία; (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means: ability.
  2142. εὐπορία from the same as εὐπορέω; pecuniary resources: wealth.
  2143. εὐπρέπεια from a compound of εὖ and πρέπω; good suitableness, i.e. gracefulness: grace.
  2144. εὐπρόσδεκτος from εὖ and a derivative of προσδέχομαι; well-received, i.e. approved, favorable: acceptable(-ted).
  2145. εὐπρόσεδρος from εὖ and the same as προσεδρεύω; sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service): X attend upon.
  2146. εὐπροσωπέω from a compound of εὖ and πρόσωπον; to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display: make a fair show.
  2147. εὑρίσκω, a prolonged form of a primary heuro, which (together with another cognate form) heureo is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect; to find (literally or figuratively): find, get, obtain, perceive, see.
  2148. Εὐροκλύδων from Euros (the east wind) and κλύδων; a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter: Euroklydon.
  2149. εὐρύχωρος from eurus (wide) and χώρα; spacious: broad.
  2150. εὐσέβεια from εὐσεβής; piety; specially, the gospel scheme: godliness, holiness.
  2151. εὐσεβέω from εὐσεβής; to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support): show piety, worship.
  2152. εὐσεβής from εὖ and σέβομαι; well-reverent, i.e. pious: devout, godly.
  2153. εὐσεβῶς adverb from εὐσεβής; piously: godly.
  2154. εὔσημος from εὖ and the base of σημαίνω; well indicated, i.e. (figuratively) significant: easy to be understood.
  2155. εὔσπλαγχνος from εὖ and σπλάγχνον; well compassioned, i.e. sympathetic: pitiful, tender-hearted.
  2156. εὐσχημόνως adverb from εὐσχήμων; decorously: decently, honestly.
  2157. εὐσχημοσύνη from εὐσχήμων; decorousness: comeliness.
  2158. εὐσχήμων from εὖ and σχῆμα; well-formed, i.e. (figuratively) decorous, noble (in rank): comely, honourable.
  2159. εὐτόνως adverb from a compound of εὖ and a derivative of teino (to stretch); in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely): mightily, vehemently.
  2160. εὐτραπελία from a compound of εὖ and a derivative of the base of τροπή (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose); witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry: jesting.
  2161. Εὔτυχος from εὖ and a derivative of τυγχάνω; well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man: Eutychus.
  2162. εὐφημία from εὔφημος; good language ("euphemy"), i.e. praise (repute): good report.
  2163. εὔφημος from εὖ and φήμη; well spoken of, i.e. reputable: of good report.
  2164. εὐφορέω from εὖ and φορέω; to bear well, i.e. be fertile: bring forth abundantly.
  2165. εὐφραίνω from εὖ and φρήν; to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good frame of mind, i.e. rejoice: fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice.
  2166. Εὐφράτης of foreign origin (compare פְּרָת); Euphrates, a river of Asia: Euphrates.
  2167. εὐφροσύνη from the same as εὐφραίνω; joyfulness: gladness, joy.
  2168. εὐχαριστέω from εὐχάριστος; to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal: (give) thank(-ful, -s).
  2169. εὐχαριστία from εὐχάριστος; gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act of worship): thankfulness, (giving of) thanks(-giving).
  2170. εὐχάριστος from εὖ and a derivative of χαρίζομαι; well favored, i.e. (by implication) grateful: thankful.
  2171. εὐχή from εὔχομαι; properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in votive obligation: prayer, vow.
  2172. εὔχομαι middle voice of a primary verb; to wish; by implication, to pray to God: pray, will, wish.
  2173. εὔχρηστος from εὖ and χρηστός; easily used, i.e. useful: profitable, meet for use.
  2174. εὐψυχέω from a compound of εὖ and ψυχή; to be in good spirits, i.e. feel encouraged: be of good comfort.
  2175. εὐωδία from a compound of εὖ and a derivative of ὄζω; good-scentedness, i.e. fragrance: sweet savour (smell, -smelling).
  2176. εὐώνυμος from εὖ and ὄνομα; properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as adverbial, at the left hand: (on the) left.
  2177. ἐφάλλομαι from ἐπί and ἅλλομαι; to spring upon: leap on.
  2178. ἐφάπαξ from ἐπί and ἅπαξ; upon one occasion (only): (at) once (for all).
  2179. Ἐφεσῖνος from Ἔφεσος; Ephesine, or situated at Ephesus: of Ephesus.
  2180. Ἐφέσιος from Ἔφεσος; an Ephesian or inhabitant of Ephesus: Ephesian, of Ephesus.
  2181. Ἔφεσος probably of foreign origin; Ephesus, a city of Asia Minor: Ephesus.
  2182. ἐφευρετής from a compound of ἐπί and εὑρίσκω; a discoverer, i.e. contriver: inventor.
  2183. ἐφημερία from ἐφήμερος; diurnality, i.e. (specially) the quotidian rotation or class of the Jewish priests' service at the Temple, as distributed by families: course.
  2184. ἐφήμερος from ἐπί and ἡμέρα; for a day ("ephemeral"), i.e. diurnal: daily.
  2185. ἐφικνέομαι from ἐπί and a cognate of ἥκω; to arrive upon, i.e. extend to: reach.
  2186. ἐφίστημι from ἐπί and ἵστημι; to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal); --assault, come (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before, by, over).
  2187. Ἐφραίμ of Hebrew origin (אֶפְרַ֫יִם or better עֶפְרוֹן); Ephraim, a place in Palestine: Ephraim.
  2188. ἐφφαθά of Chaldee origin (פְּתַח); be opened!: Ephphatha.
  2189. ἔχθρα feminine of ἐχθρός; hostility; by implication, a reason for opposition: enmity, hatred.
  2190. ἐχθρός from a primary echtho (to hate); hateful (passively, odious, or actively, hostile); usually as a noun, an adversary (especially Satan): enemy, foe.
  2191. ἔχιδνα of uncertain origin; an adder or other poisonous snake (literally or figuratively): viper.
  2192. ἔχω; including an alternate form scheo (used in certain tenses only) a primary verb; to hold (used in very various applications, literally or figuratively, direct or remote; such as possession; ability, contiuity, relation, or condition): be (able, X hold, possessed with), accompany, + begin to amend, can(+ -not), X conceive, count, diseased, do + eat, + enjoy, + fear, following, have, hold, keep, + lack, + go to law, lie, + must needs, + of necessity, + need, next, + recover, + reign, + rest, + return, X sick, take for, + tremble, + uncircumcised, use.
  2193. ἕως of uncertain affinity; a conjunction, preposition and adverb of continuance, until (of time and place): even (until, unto), (as) far (as), how long, (un-)til(-l), (hither-, un-, up) to, while(-s).
  2194. Ζαβουλών of Hebrew origin (זְבוּלוּן); Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of Palestine: Zabulon.
  2195. Ζακχαῖος of Hebrew origin (compare זַכָּי); Zacchæus, an Israelite: Zacchæus.
  2196. Ζαρά of Hebrew origin (זָ֫רַח); Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite: Zara.
  2197. Ζαχαρίας of Hebrew origin (זְכַרְיָה); Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two Israelites: Zacharias.
  2198. ζάω a primary verb; to live (literally or figuratively): life(-time), (a-)live(-ly), quick.
  2199. Ζεβεδαῖος of Hebrew origin (compare זַבְדִּי); Zebedæus, an Israelite: Zebedee.
  2200. ζεστός from ζέω; boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively, fervent): hot.
  2201. ζεῦγος from the same as ζυγός; a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together) or brace (of birds tied together): yoke, pair.
  2202. ζευκτηρία feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as ζυγός; a fastening (tiller-rope): band.
  2203. Ζεύς of uncertain affinity; in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name Dis, which is otherwise obsolete; Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks: Jupiter.
  2204. ζέω a primary verb; to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e. (figuratively) be fervid (earnest): be fervent.
  2205. ζῆλος from ζέω; properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice): emulation, envy(-ing), fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal.
  2206. ζηλόω from ζῆλος; to have warmth of feeling for or against: affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect).
  2207. ζηλωτής from ζηλόω; a "zealot": zealous.
  2208. Ζηλωτής the same as ζηλωτής; a Zealot, i.e. (specially) partisan for Jewish political independence: Zelotes.
  2209. ζημία probably akin to the base of δαμάζω (through the idea of violence); detriment: damage, loss.
  2210. ζημιόω from ζημία; to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience detriment: be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss.
  2211. Ζηνᾶς probably contracted from a poetic form of Ζεύς and δῶρον; Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian: Zenas.
  2212. ζητέω of uncertain affinity; to seek (literally or figuratively); specially, (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against life): be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X will) seek (after, for, means). Compare πυνθάνομαι.
  2213. ζήτημα from ζητέω; a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate: question.
  2214. ζήτησις from ζητέω; a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its theme: question.
  2215. ζιζάνιον of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain: tares.
  2216. Ζοροβάβελ of Hebrew origin (זְרֻבָּבֶל); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite: Zorobabel.
  2217. ζόφος akin to the base of νέφος; gloom (as shrouding like a cloud): blackness, darkness, mist.
  2218. ζυγός from the root of zeugnumi (to join, especially by a "yoke"); a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales): pair of balances, yoke.
  2219. ζύμη probably from ζέω; ferment (as if boiling up): leaven.
  2220. ζυμόω from ζύμη; to cause to ferment: leaven.
  2221. ζωγρέω from the same as ζῶον and ἀγρεύω; to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare: take captive, catch.
  2222. ζωή from ζάω; life (literally or figuratively): life(-time). Compare ψυχή.
  2223. ζώνη probably akin to the base of ζυγός; a belt; by implication, a pocket: girdle, purse.
  2224. ζώννυμι from ζώνη; to bind about (especially with a belt): gird.
  2225. ζωογονέω from the same as ζῶον and a derivative of γίνομαι; to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death: live, preserve.
  2226. ζῶον neuter of a derivative of ζάω; a live thing, i.e. an animal: beast.
  2227. ζωοποιέω from the same as ζῶον and ποιέω; to (re-)vitalize (literally or figuratively): make alive, give life, quicken.
  2228. ἤ a primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; disjunctive, or; comparative, than: and, but (either), (n-)either, except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea. Often used in connection with other particles. Compare especially ἤδη, ἤπερ, ἤτοι.
  2229. ἦ an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of ἤ; used only (in the New Testament) before μέν; assuredly: surely.
  2230. ἡγεμονεύω from ἡγεμών; to act as ruler: be governor.
  2231. ἡγεμονία from ἡγεμών; government, i.e. (in time) official term: reign.
  2232. ἡγεμών from ἡγέομαι; a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province: governor, prince, ruler.
  2233. ἡγέομαι middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of ἄγω; to lead, i.e. command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e. consider: account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have the rule over, suppose, think.
  2234. ἡδέως adverb from a derivative of the base of ἡδονή; sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure: gladly.
  2235. ἤδη apparently from ἤ (or possibly ἦ) and δή; even now: already, (even) now (already), by this time.
  2236. ἥδιστα neuter plural of the superlative of the same as ἡδέως; with great pleasure: most (very) gladly.
  2237. ἡδονή from handano (to please); sensual delight; by implication, desire: lust, pleasure.
  2238. ἡδύοσμον neuter of the compound of the same as ἡδέως and ὀσμή; a sweet-scented plant, i.e. mint: mint.
  2239. ἦθος a strengthened form of ἔθος; usage, i.e. (plural) moral habits: manners.
  2240. ἥκω a primary verb; to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively): come.
  2241. ἠλί of Hebrew origin (אֵל with pronominal suffix); my God: Eli.
  2242. Ἡλί of Hebrew origin (עֵלִי); Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite: Heli.
  2243. Ἡλίας of Hebrew origin (אֵלִיָּה); Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite: Elias.
  2244. ἡλικία from the same as ἡλίκος; maturity (in years or size): age, stature.
  2245. ἡλίκος from helix (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much: how (what) great.
  2246. ἥλιος from hele (a ray; perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι); the sun; by implication, light: + east, sun.
  2247. ἧλος of uncertain affinity; a stud, i.e. spike: nail.
  2248. ἡμᾶς accusative case plural of ἐγώ; us: our, us, we.
  2249. ἡμεῖς nominative plural of ἐγώ; we (only used when emphatic): us, we (ourselves).
  2250. ἡμέρα feminine (with ὥρα implied) of a derivative of hemai (to sit; akin to the base of ἑδραῖος) meaning tame, i.e. gentle; day, i.e. (literally) the time space between dawn and dark, or the whole 24 hours (but several days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less clearly by the context): age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), + for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years.
  2251. ἡμέτερος from θνητός; our: our, your (by a different reading).
  2252. ἤμην a prolonged form of ἦν; I was: be, was. (Sometimes unexpressed).
  2253. ἡμιθανής from a presumed compound of the base of ἥμισυ and θνήσκω; half dead, i.e. entirely exhausted: half dead.
  2254. ἡμῖν dative case plural of ἐγώ; to (or for, with, by) us: our, (for) us, we.
  2255. ἥμισυ neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to ἅμα (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as noun) half: half.
  2256. ἡμιώριον from the base of ἥμισυ and ὥρα; a half-hour: half an hour.
  2257. ἡμῶν genitive case plural of ἐγώ; of (or from) us: our (company), us, we.
  2258. ἦν imperfect of εἰμί; I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were): + agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were.
  2259. ἡνίκα of uncertain affinity; at which time: when.
  2260. ἤπερ from ἤ and περ; than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed): than.
  2261. ἤπιος probably from ἔπος; properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind: gentle.
  2262. Ἤρ of Hebrew origin (עֵר); Er, an Israelite: Er.
  2263. ἤρεμος perhaps by transposition from ἔρημος (through the idea of stillness); tranquil: quiet.
  2264. Ἡρώδης compound of heros (a "hero") and εἶδος; heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings: Herod.
  2265. Ἡρωδιανοί plural of a derivative of Ἡρώδης; Herodians, i.e. partisans of Herod: Herodians.
  2266. Ἡρωδιάς from Ἡρώδης; Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family: Herodias.
  2267. Ἡρωδίων from Ἡρώδης; Herodion, a Christian: Herodion.
  2268. Ἡσαΐας of Hebrew origin (יְשַׁעְיָה); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite: Esaias.
  2269. Ἠσαῦ of Hebrew origin (עֵשָׂו); Esau, an Edomite: Esau.
  2270. ἡσυχάζω from the same as ἡσύχιος; to keep still (intransitively), i.e. refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech: cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest.
  2271. ἡσυχία feminine of ἡσύχιος; (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language: quietness, silence.
  2272. ἡσύχιος a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of ἑδραῖος and perhaps ἔχω; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing): peaceable, quiet.
  2273. ἤτοι from ἤ and τοί; either indeed: whether.
  2274. ἡττάω from the same as ἥττον; to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower: be inferior, overcome.
  2275. ἥττημα from ἡττάω; a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss: diminishing, fault.
  2276. ἥττον neuter of comparative of heka (slightly) used for that of κακός; worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb): less, worse.
  2277. ἤτω third person singular imperative of εἰμί; let him (or it) be: let … be.
  2278. ἠχέω from ἦχος; to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate: roar, sound.
  2279. ἦχος of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar; figuratively, a rumor: fame, sound.
  2280. Θαδδαῖος of uncertain origin; Thaddæus, one of the Apostles: Thaddæus.
  2281. θάλασσα probably prolonged from ἅλς; the sea (genitive case or specially): sea.
  2282. θάλπω probably akin to thallo (to warm); to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to foster: cherish.
  2283. Θάμαρ of Hebrew origin (תָּמָר); Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess: Thamar.
  2284. θαμβέω from θάμβος; to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. astound: amaze, astonish.
  2285. θάμβος akin to an obsolete tapho (to dumbfound); stupefaction (by surprise), i.e. astonishment: X amazed, + astonished, wonder.
  2286. θανάσιμος from θάνατος; fatal, i.e. poisonous: deadly.
  2287. θανατήφορος from (the feminine form of) θάνατος and φέρω; death-bearing, i.e. fatal: deadly.
  2288. θάνατος from θνήσκω; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively): X deadly, (be…) death.
  2289. θανατόω from θάνατος to kill (literally or figuratively): become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify.
  2290. θάπτω a primary verb; to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter: bury.
  2291. Θάρα of Hebrew origin (תָּ֫רַח); Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham: Thara.
  2292. θαῤῥέω another form for θαρσέω; to exercise courage: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident. Compare τολμάω.
  2293. θαρσέω from θάρσος; to have courage: be of good cheer (comfort). Compare θαῤῥέω.
  2294. θάρσος akin (by transposition) to thrasos (daring); boldness (subjectively): courage.
  2295. θαῦμα apparently from a form of θεάομαι; wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract): admiration.
  2296. θαυμάζω from θαῦμα; to wonder; by implication, to admire: admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder.
  2297. θαυμάσιος from θαῦμα; wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle: wonderful thing.
  2298. θαυμαστός from θαυμάζω; wondered at, i.e. (by implication) wonderful: marvel(-lous).
  2299. θεά feminine of θεός; a female deity: goddess.
  2300. θεάομαι a prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit: behold, look (upon), see. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.
  2301. θεατρίζω from θέατρον; to expose as a spectacle: make a gazing stock.
  2302. θέατρον from θεάομαι; a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively): spectacle, theatre.
  2303. θεῖον probably neuter of θεῖος (in its original sense of flashing); sulphur: brimstone.
  2304. θεῖος from θεός; godlike (neuter as noun, divinity): divine, godhead.
  2305. θειότης from θεῖος; divinity (abstractly): godhead.
  2306. θειώδης from θεῖον and εἶδος; sulphur-like, i.e. sulphurous: brimstone.
  2307. θέλημα from the prolonged form of θέλω; a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination: desire, pleasure, will.
  2308. θέλησις from θέλω; determination (properly, the act), i.e. option: will.
  2309. θέλω or ethelo, in certain tenses theleo, and etheleo, which are otherwise obsolete apparently strengthened from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι; to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas βούλομαι properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in: desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly)).
  2310. θεμέλιος from a derivative of τίθημι; something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively): foundation.
  2311. θεμελιόω from θεμέλιος; to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate: (lay the) found(- ation), ground, settle.
  2312. θεοδίδακτος from θεός and διδάσκω; divinely instructed: taught of God.
  2313. θεομαχέω from θεομάχος; to resist deity: fight against God.
  2314. θεομάχος from θεός and μάχομαι; an opponent of deity: to fight against God.
  2315. θεόπνευστος from θεός and a presumed derivative of πνέω; divinely breathed in: given by inspiration of God.
  2316. θεός of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with ὁ) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very: X exceeding, God, god(-ly, -ward).
  2317. θεοσέβεια from θεοσεβής; devoutness, i.e. piety: godliness.
  2318. θεοσεβής from θεός and σέβομαι; reverent of God, i.e. pious: worshipper of God.
  2319. θεοστυγής from θεός and the base of στυγνητός; hateful to God, i.e. impious: hater of God.
  2320. θεότης from θεός; divinity (abstractly): godhead.
  2321. Θεόφιλος from θεός and φίλος; friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian: Theophilus.
  2322. θεραπεία from θεραπεύω; attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics: healing, household.
  2323. θεραπεύω from the same as θεράπων; to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease): cure, heal, worship.
  2324. θεράπων apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of θέρος; a menial attendant (as if cherishing): servant.
  2325. θερίζω from θέρος (in the sense of the crop); to harvest: reap.
  2326. θερισμός from θερίζω; reaping, i.e. the crop: harvest.
  2327. θεριστής from θερίζω; a harvester: reaper.
  2328. θερμαίνω from θέρμη; to heat (oneself): (be) warm(-ed, self).
  2329. θέρμη from the base of θέρος; warmth: heat.
  2330. θέρος from a primary thero (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. summer: summer.
  2331. Θεσσαλονικεύς from Θεσσαλονίκη; a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice: Thessalonian.
  2332. Θεσσαλονίκη from Thessalos (a Thessalian) and νίκη; Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor: Thessalonica.
  2333. Θευδᾶς of uncertain origin; Theudas, an Israelite: Theudas.
  2334. θεωρέω from a derivative of θεάομαι (perhaps by addition of ὁράω); to be a spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge)): behold, consider, look on, perceive, see. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.
  2335. θεωρία from the same as θεωρέω; spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle: sight.
  2336. θήκη from τίθημι; a receptacle, i.e. scabbard: sheath.
  2337. θηλάζω from thele (the nipple); to suckle, (by implication) to suck: (give) suck(-ling).
  2338. θῆλυς from the same as θηλάζω; female: female, woman.
  2339. θήρα from ther (a wild animal, as game); hunting, i.e. (figuratively) destruction: trap.
  2340. θηρεύω from θήρα; to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at: catch.
  2341. θηριομαχέω from a compound of θηρίον and μάχομαι; to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men): fight with wild beasts.
  2342. θηρίον diminutive from the same as θήρα; a dangerous animal: (venomous, wild) beast.
  2343. θησαυρίζω from θησαυρός; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively): lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up).
  2344. θησαυρός from τίθημι; a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or figuratively): treasure.
  2345. θιγγάνω a prolonged form of an obsolete primary thigo (to finger); to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure: handle, touch.
  2346. θλίβω akin to the base of τρίβος; to crowd (literally or figuratively): afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble.
  2347. θλῖψις from θλίβω; pressure (literally or figuratively): afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble.
  2348. θνήσκω a strengthened form of a simpler primary thano than'-o (which is used for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or figuratively): be dead, die.
  2349. θνητός from θνήσκω; liable to die: mortal(-ity).
  2350. θορυβέω from θόρυβος; to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar.
  2351. θόρυβος from the base of θροέω; a disturbance: tumult, uproar.
  2352. θραύω a primary verb; to crush: bruise. Compare ῥήγνυμι.
  2353. θρέμμα from τρέφω; stock (as raised on a farm): cattle.
  2354. θρηνέω from θρῆνος; to bewail: lament, mourn.
  2355. θρῆνος from the base of θροέω; wailing: lamentation.
  2356. θρησκεία from a derivative of θρησκός; ceremonial observance: religion, worshipping.
  2357. θρησκός probably from the base of θροέω; ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious: religious.
  2358. θριαμβεύω from a prolonged compound of the base of θροέω; and a derivative of ἅπτομαι (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory: (cause) to triumph (over).
  2359. θρίξ genitive case trichos, etc.; of uncertain derivation; hair: hair. Compare κόμη.
  2360. θροέω from threomai to wail; to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten: trouble.
  2361. θρόμβος perhaps from τρέφω (in the sense of thickening); a clot: great drop.
  2362. θρόνος from thrao (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate: seat, throne.
  2363. Θυάτειρα of uncertain derivation; Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor: Thyatira.
  2364. θυγάτηρ apparently a primary word (compare "daughter"); a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant): daughter.
  2365. θυγάτριον from θυγάτηρ; a daughterling: little (young) daughter.
  2366. θύελλα from θύω (in the sense of blowing) a storm: tempest.
  2367. θύϊνος from a derivative of θύω (in the sense of blowing; denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood: thyine.
  2368. θυμίαμα from θυμιάω; an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself: incense, odour.
  2369. θυμιαστήριον from a derivative of θυμιάω; a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple): censer.
  2370. θυμιάω from a derivative of θύω (in the sense of smoking); to fumigate, i.e. offer aromatic fumes: burn incense.
  2371. θυμομαχέω from a presumed compound of θυμός and μάχομαι; to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated: be highly displeased.
  2372. θυμός from θύω; passion (as if breathing hard): fierceness, indignation, wrath. Compare ψυχή.
  2373. θυμόω from θυμός; to put in a passion, i.e. enrage: be wroth.
  2374. θύρα apparently a primary word (compare "door"); a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively): door, gate.
  2375. θυρεός from θύρα; a large shield (as door-shaped): shield.
  2376. θυρίς from θύρα; an aperture, i.e. window: window.
  2377. θυρωρός from θύρα and ouros (a watcher); a gate- warden: that kept the door, porter.
  2378. θυσία from θύω; sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or figuratively): sacrifice.
  2379. θυσιαστήριον from a derivative of θυσία; a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative): altar.
  2380. θύω a primary verb; properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose): kill, (do) sacrifice, slay.
  2381. Θωμᾶς of Chaldee origin (compare תְאוֹמִים); the twin; Thomas, a Christian: Thomas.
  2382. θώραξ of uncertain affinity; the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet: breast-plate.
  2383. Ἰάειρος of Hebrew origin (יָאּיר); Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite: Jairus.
  2384. Ἰακώβ of Hebrew origin (יַעֲקֹב); Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the Israelites; also an Israelite: Jacob.
  2385. Ἰάκωβος the same as Ἰακώβ Græcized; Jacobus, the name of three Israelites: James.
  2386. ἴαμα from ἰάομαι; a cure (the effect): healing.
  2387. Ἰαμβρῆς of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian: Jambres.
  2388. Ἰαννά probably of Hebrew origin (compare יָנָה); Janna, an Israelite: Janna.
  2389. Ἰαννῆς of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian: Jannes.
  2390. ἰάομαι middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure (literally or figuratively): heal, make whole.
  2391. Ἰάρεδ of Hebrew origin (יָ֫רֶד); Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian: Jared.
  2392. ἴασις from ἰάομαι; curing (the act): cure, heal(-ing).
  2393. ἴασπις probably of foreign origin (see יָשְׁפֵה); "jasper", a gem: jasper.
  2394. Ἰάσων future active participle masculine of ἰάομαι; about to cure; Jason, a Christian: Jason.
  2395. ἰατρός from ἰάομαι; a physician: physician.
  2396. ἴδε second person singular imperative active of εἴδω; used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!: behold, lo, see.
  2397. ἰδέα from εἴδω; a sight (comparative figuratively "idea"), i.e. aspect: countenance.
  2398. ἴδιος of uncertain affinity; pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by implication, private or separate: X his acquaintance, when they were alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our, thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their (own).
  2399. ἰδιώτης from ἴδιος; a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot"): ignorant, rude, unlearned.
  2400. ἰδού second person singular imperative middle voice of εἴδω; used as imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see.
  2401. Ἰδουμαία of Hebrew origin (אֱדוֹם); Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine: Idumæa.
  2402. ἱδρώς a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat); perspiration: sweat.
  2403. Ἰεζαβήλ of Hebrew origin (אּיזָ֫בֶל); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher): Jezabel.
  2404. Ἱεράπολις from ἱερός and πόλις; holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor: Hierapolis.
  2405. ἱερατεία from ἱερατεύω; priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function: office of the priesthood, priest's office.
  2406. ἱεράτευμα from ἱερατεύω; the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively): priesthood.
  2407. ἱερατεύω prolongation from ἱερεύς; to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions: execute the priest's office.
  2408. Ἱερεμίας of Hebrew origin (יִרְמְיָה); Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an Israelite: Jeremiah.
  2409. ἱερεύς from ἱερός; a priest (literally or figuratively): (high) priest.
  2410. Ἱεριχώ of Hebrew origin (יְרֵחוֹ); Jericho, a place in Palestine: Jericho.
  2411. ἱερόν neuter of ἱερός; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas ναός denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere): temple.
  2412. ἱεροπρεπής from ἱερός and the same as πρέπω; reverent: as becometh holiness.
  2413. ἱερός of uncertain affinity; sacred: holy.
  2414. Ἱεροσόλυμα of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ֫םִ); Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine: Jerusalem. Compare Ἱερουσαλήμ.
  2415. Ἱεροσολυμίτης from Ἱεροσόλυμα; a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma: of Jerusalem.
  2416. ἱεροσυλέω from ἱερόσυλος; to be a temple-robber (figuratively): commit sacrilege.
  2417. ἱερόσυλος from ἱερόν and συλάω; a temple-despoiler: robber of churches.
  2418. ἱερουργέω from a compound of ἱερόν and the base of ἔργον; to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively): minister.
  2419. Ἱερουσαλήμ of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ֫םִ); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine: Jerusalem. Compare Ἱεροσόλυμα.
  2420. ἱερωσύνη from ἱερός; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office: priesthood.
  2421. Ἰεσσαί of Hebrew origin (יִשַׁי); Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite: Jesse.
  2422. Ἰεφθάε of Hebrew origin (יִפְתָּח); Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite: Jephthah.
  2423. Ἰεχονίας of Hebrew origin (יְכָנְיָה); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite: Jechonias.
  2424. Ἰησοῦς of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשׁ֫וּעַ); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites: Jesus.
  2425. ἱκανός from hiko (hikano or hikneomai, akin to ἥκω) (to arrive); competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character): able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy.
  2426. ἱκανότης from ἱκανός; ability: sufficiency.
  2427. ἱκανόω from ἱκανός; to enable, i.e. qualify: make able (meet).
  2428. ἱκετηρία from a derivative of the base of ἱκανός (through the idea of approaching for a favor); intreaty: supplication.
  2429. ἱκμάς of uncertain affinity; dampness: moisture.
  2430. Ἰκόνιον perhaps from εἰκών; image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor: Iconium.
  2431. ἱλαρός from the same as ἵλεως; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing: cheerful.
  2432. ἱλαρότης from ἱλαρός; alacrity: cheerfulness.
  2433. ἱλάσκομαι middle voice from the same as ἵλεως; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious: be merciful, make reconciliation for.
  2434. ἱλασμός atonement, i.e. (concretely) an expiator: propitiation.
  2435. ἱλαστήριον neuter of a derivative of ἱλάσκομαι; an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple): mercyseat, propitiation.
  2436. ἵλεως perhaps from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι; cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it: be it far, merciful.
  2437. Ἰλλυρικόν neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation; (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe: Illyricum.
  2438. ἱμάς perhaps from the same as ἅμα; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge): latchet, thong.
  2439. ἱματίζω from ἱμάτιον; to dress: clothe.
  2440. ἱμάτιον neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); a dress (inner or outer): apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture.
  2441. ἱματισμός from ἱματίζω; clothing: apparel (X -led), array, raiment, vesture.
  2442. ἱμείρομαι middle voice from himeros (a yearning; of uncertain affinity); to long for: be affectionately desirous.
  2443. ἵνα probably from the same as the former part of ἑαυτοῦ (through the demonstrative idea; compare ὁ); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result): albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to. Compare ἵνα μή.
  2444. ἱνατί from ἵνα and τίς; for what reason ?, i.e. why?: wherefore, why.
  2445. Ἰόππη of Hebrew origin (יָפוֹ); Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine: Joppa.
  2446. Ἰορδάνης of Hebrew origin (יַרְדֵּן); the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine: Jordan.
  2447. ἰός perhaps from eimi (to go) or hiemi (to send); rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents): poison, rust.
  2448. Ἰουδά of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה or perhaps יֻטָּה); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine: Judah.
  2449. Ἰουδαία feminine of Ἰουδαῖος (with γῆ implied); the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine: Judæa.
  2450. Ἰουδαΐζω from Ἰουδαῖος; to become a Judæan, i.e. "Judaize": live as the Jews.
  2451. Ἰουδαϊκός from Ἰουδαῖος; Judaïc, i.e. resembling a Judæan: Jewish.
  2452. Ἰουδαϊκῶς adverb from Ἰουδαϊκός; Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan: as do the Jews.
  2453. Ἰουδαῖος from Ἰουδά (in the sense of Ἰούδας as a country); Judæan, i.e. belonging to Jehudah: Jew(-ess), of Judæa.
  2454. Ἰουδαϊσμός from Ἰουδαΐζω; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages: Jews' religion.
  2455. Ἰούδας of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region: Juda(-h, -s); Jude.
  2456. Ἰουλία feminine of the same as Ἰούλιος; Julia, a Christian woman: Julia.
  2457. Ἰούλιος of Latin origin; Julius, a centurion: Julius.
  2458. Ἰουνιᾶς of Latin origin; Junias, a Christian: Junias.
  2459. Ἰοῦστος of Latin origin ("just"); Justus, the name of three Christian: Justus.
  2460. ἱππεύς from ἵππος; an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps: horseman.
  2461. ἱππικόν neuter of a derivative of ἵππος; the cavalry force: horse(-men).
  2462. ἵππος of uncertain affinity; a horse: horse.
  2463. ἶρις perhaps from ἐρέω (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities); a rainbow ("iris"): rainbow.
  2464. Ἰσαάκ of Hebrew origin (יִצְחָק); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham: Isaac.
  2465. ἰσάγγελος from ἴσος and ἄγγελος; like an angel, i.e. angelic: equal unto the angels.
  2466. Ἰσαχάρ of Hebrew origin (יִשָּׂשָׂכָר); Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant): Issachar.
  2467. ἴσημι assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of εἴδω; to know: know.
  2468. ἴσθι second person imperative present of εἰμί; be thou: + agree, be, X give thyself wholly to.
  2469. Ἰσκαριώτης of Hebrew origin (probably אּישׁ and קִרְיָא); inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor: Iscariot.
  2470. ἴσος probably from εἴδω (through the idea of seeming); similar (in amount and kind): + agree, as much, equal, like.
  2471. ἰσότης likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity: equal(-ity).
  2472. ἰσότιμος from ἴσος and τιμή; of equal value or honor: like precious.
  2473. ἰσόψυχος from ἴσος and ψυχή; of similar spirit: likeminded.
  2474. Ἰσραήλ of Hebrew origin (יִשְׂרָאֵל); Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively): Israel.
  2475. Ἰσραηλίτης from Ἰσραήλ; an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively): Israelite.
  2476. ἵστημι a prolonged form of a primary stao stah'-o (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses); to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively): abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up). Compare τίθημι.
  2477. ἱστορέω from a derivative of εἴδω; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview): see.
  2478. ἰσχυρός from ἰσχύς; forcible (literally or figuratively): boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant.
  2479. ἰσχύς from a derivative of is (force; compare eschon, a form of ἔχω); forcefulness (literally or figuratively): ability, might(-ily), power, strength.
  2480. ἰσχύω from ἰσχύς; to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively): be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work.
  2481. ἴσως adverb from ἴσος; likely, i.e. perhaps: it may be.
  2482. Ἰταλία probably of foreign origin; Italia, a region of Europe: Italy.
  2483. Ἰταλικός from Ἰταλία; Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia: Italian.
  2484. Ἰτουραΐα of Hebrew origin (יְטוּר); Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine: Ituræa.
  2485. ἰχθύδιον diminutive from ἰχθύς; a petty fish: little (small) fish.
  2486. ἰχθύς of uncertain affinity; a fish: fish.
  2487. ἴχνος from ikneomai (to arrive; compare ἥκω); a track (figuratively): step.
  2488. Ἰωάθαμ of Hebrew origin (יוֹתָם); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite: Joatham.
  2489. Ἰωάννα feminine of the same as Ἰωάννης; Joanna, a Christian: Joanna.
  2490. Ἰωαννᾶς a form of Ἰωάννης; Joannas, an Israelite: Joannas.
  2491. Ἰωάννης of Hebrew origin (יוֹחָנָן); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites: John.
  2492. Ἰώβ of Hebrew origin (אּיּוֹב); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch: Job.
  2493. Ἰωήλ of Hebrew origin (יוֹאֵל); Joel, an Israelite: Joel.
  2494. Ἰωνάν probably for Ἰωάννης or Ἰωνᾶς; Jonan, an Israelite: Jonan.
  2495. Ἰωνᾶς of Hebrew origin (יוֹנָה); Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two Israelites: Jonas.
  2496. Ἰωράμ of Hebrew origin (יוֹרָם); Joram, an Israelite: Joram.
  2497. Ἰωρείμ perhaps for Ἰωράμ; Jorim, an Israelite: Jorim.
  2498. Ἰωσαφάτ of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); Josaphat (i.e. Jehoshaphat), an Israelite: Josaphat.
  2499. Ἰωσή genitive case of Ἰωσῆς; Jose, an Israelite: Jose.
  2500. Ἰωσῆς perhaps for Ἰωσήφ; Joses, the name of two Israelites: Joses. Compare Ἰωσή.
  2501. Ἰωσήφ of Hebrew origin (יוֹסֵף); Joseph, the name of seven Israelites: Joseph.
  2502. Ἰωσίας of Hebrew origin (יֹאשִׁיָּה); Josias (i.e. Joshiah), an Israelite: Josias.
  2503. ἰῶτα of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet); "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything: jot.
  2504. κἀγώ from καί and ἐγώ; so also the dative case kamoi kam-oy', and accusative case kame kam-eh' and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me: (and, even, even so, so) I (also, in like wise), both me, me also.
  2505. καθά from κατά and the neuter plural of ὅς; according to which things, i.e. just as: as.
  2506. καθαίρεσις from καθαιρέω; demolition; figuratively, extinction: destruction, pulling down.
  2507. καθαιρέω from κατά and αἱρέομαι (including its alternate); to lower (or with violence) demolish (literally or figuratively): cast (pull, put, take) down, destroy.
  2508. καθαίρω from καθαρός; to cleanse, i.e. (specially) to prune; figuratively, to expiate: purge.
  2509. καθάπερ from καθά and περ; exactly as: (even, as well) as.
  2510. καθάπτω from κατά and ἅπτομαι; to seize upon: fasten on.
  2511. καθαρίζω from καθαρός; to cleanse (literally or figuratively): (make) clean(-se), purge, purify.
  2512. καθαρισμός from καθαρίζω; a washing off, i.e. (ceremonially) ablution, (morally) expiation: cleansing, + purge, purification(-fying).
  2513. καθαρός of uncertain affinity; clean (literally or figuratively): clean, clear, pure.
  2514. καθαρότης from καθαρός; cleanness (ceremonially): purification.
  2515. καθέδρα from κατά and the same as ἑδραῖος; a bench (literally or figuratively): seat.
  2516. καθέζομαι from κατά and the base of ἑδραῖος; to sit down: sit.
  2517. καθεξῆς from κατά and ἑξῆς; thereafter, i.e. consecutively; as a noun (by ellipsis of noun) a subsequent person or time: after(-ward), by (in) order.
  2518. καθεύδω from κατά and heudo (to sleep); to lie down to rest, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep (literally or figuratively): (be a-)sleep.
  2519. καθηγητής from a compound of κατά and ἡγέομαι; a guide, i.e. (figuratively) a teacher: master.
  2520. καθήκω from κατά and ἥκω; to reach to, i.e. (neuter of present active participle, figuratively as adjective) becoming: convenient, fit.
  2521. κάθημαι from κατά; and hemai (to sit; akin to the base of ἑδραῖος); to sit down; figuratively, to remain, reside: dwell, sit (by, down).
  2522. καθημερινός from κατά and ἡμέρα; quotidian: daily.
  2523. καθίζω another (active) form for καθέζομαι; to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively, appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle (hover, dwell): continue, set, sit (down), tarry.
  2524. καθίημι from κατά; and hiemi (to send); to lower: let down.
  2525. καθίστημι from κατά and ἵστημι; to place down (permanently), i.e. (figuratively) to designate, constitute, convoy: appoint, be, conduct, make, ordain, set.
  2526. καθό from κατά and ὅς; according to which thing, i.e. precisely as, in proportion as: according to that, (inasmuch) as.
  2527. καθόλου from κατά and ὅλος; on the whole, i.e. entirely: at all.
  2528. καθοπλίζω from κατά; and ὁπλίζω; to equip fully with armor: arm.
  2529. καθοράω from κατά and ὁράω; to behold fully, i.e. (figuratively) distinctly apprehend: clearly see.
  2530. καθότι from κατά; and ὅς and τὶς; according to which certain thing, i.e. as far (or inasmuch) as: (according, forasmuch) as, because (that).
  2531. καθώς from κατά and ὡς; just (or inasmuch) as, that: according to, (according, even) as, how, when.
  2532. καί apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also a cumulative force; and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words: and, also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when, yet.
  2533. Καϊάφας of Chaldee origin; the dell; Caiaphas (i.e. Cajepha), an Israelite: Caiaphas.
  2534. καίγε from καί and γέ; and at least (or even, indeed): and, at least.
  2535. Κάϊν of Hebrew origin (קָ֫יִן); Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam: Cain.
  2536. Καϊνάν of Hebrew origin (קֵינָן); Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two patriarchs: Cainan.
  2537. καινός of uncertain affinity; new (especially in freshness; while νέος is properly so with respect to age: new.
  2538. καινότης from καινός; renewal (figuratively): newness.
  2539. καίπερ from καί and περ; and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or notwithstanding: and yet, although.
  2540. καιρός of uncertain affinity; an occasion, i.e. set or proper time: X always, opportunity, (convenient, due) season, (due, short, while) time, a while. Compare χρόνος.
  2541. Καῖσαρ of Latin origin; Cæsar, a title of the Roman emperor: Cæsar.
  2542. Καισάρεια from Καῖσαρ; Cæsaria, the name of two places in Palestine: Cæsarea.
  2543. καίτοι from καί and τοί; and yet, i.e. nevertheless: although.
  2544. καίτοιγε from καίτοι and γέ; and yet indeed, i.e. although really: nevertheless, though.
  2545. καίω apparently a primary verb; to set on fire, i.e. kindle or (by implication) consume: burn, light.
  2546. κἀκεῖ from καί and ἐκεῖ; likewise in that place: and there, there (thither) also.
  2547. κἀκεῖθεν from καί and ἐκεῖθεν; likewise from that place (or time): and afterward (from) (thence), thence also.
  2548. κἀκεῖνος from καί and ἐκεῖνος; likewise that (or those): and him (other, them), even he, him also, them (also), (and) they.
  2549. κακία from κακός; badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble: evil, malice(-iousness), naughtiness, wickedness.
  2550. κακοήθεια from a compound of κακός and ἦθος; bad character, i.e. (specially) mischievousness: malignity.
  2551. κακολογέω from a compound of κακός and λόγος; to revile: curse, speak evil of.
  2552. κακοπάθεια from a compound of ἡμιώριον and πάθος; hardship: suffering affliction.
  2553. κακοπαθέω from the same as κακοπάθεια; to undergo hardship: be afflicted, endure afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble.
  2554. κακοποιέω from κακοποιός; to be a bad-doer, i.e. (objectively) to injure, or (genitive) to sin: do(ing) evil.
  2555. κακοποιός from κακός and ποιέω; a bad-doer; (specially), a criminal: evil-doer, malefactor.
  2556. κακός apparently a primary word; worthless (intrinsically, such; whereas πονηρός properly refers to effects), i.e. (subjectively) depraved, or (objectively) injurious: bad, evil, harm, ill, noisome, wicked.
  2557. κακοῦργος from κακός and the base of ἔργον; a wrong-doer, i.e. criminal: evil-doer, malefactor.
  2558. κακουχέω from a presumed compound of κακός and ἔχω; to maltreat: which suffer adversity, torment.
  2559. κακόω from κακός; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate: make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex.
  2560. κακῶς from κακός; badly (physically or morally): amiss, diseased, evil, grievously, miserably, sick, sore.
  2561. κάκωσις from κακόω; maltreatment: affliction.
  2562. καλάμη feminine of κάλαμος; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble: stubble.
  2563. κάλαμος of uncertain affinity; a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a similar plant); by implication, a pen: pen, reed.
  2564. καλέω akin to the base of κελεύω; to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a variety of applications, directly or otherwise): bid, call (forth), (whose, whose sur-)name (was (called)).
  2565. καλλιέλαιος from the base of καλλίον and ἐλαία; a cultivated olive tree, i.e. a domesticated or improved one: good olive tree.
  2566. καλλίον neuter of the (irregular) comparative of καλός; (adverbially) better than many: very well.
  2567. καλοδιδάσκαλος from καλός and διδάσκαλος; a teacher of the right: teacher of good things.
  2568. Καλοὶ Λιμένες plural of καλός and λιμήν; Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete: fair havens.
  2569. καλοποιέω from καλός and ποιέω; to do well, i.e. live virtuously: well doing.
  2570. καλός of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively) good (literally or morally), i.e. valuable or virtuous (for appearance or use, and thus distinguished from ἀγαθός, which is properly intrinsic): X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy.
  2571. κάλυμα from καλύπτω; a cover, i.e. veil: vail.
  2572. καλύπτω akin to κλέπτω and κρύπτω; to cover up (literally or figuratively): cover, hide.
  2573. καλῶς adverb from καλός; well (usually morally): (in a) good (place), honestly, + recover, (full) well.
  2574. κάμηλος of Hebrew origin (גָּמָל); a "camel": camel.
  2575. κάμινος probably from καίω; a furnace: furnace.
  2576. καμμύω from a compound of κατά and the base of μυστήριον; to shut down, i.e. close the eyes: close.
  2577. κάμνω apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken): faint, sick, be wearied.
  2578. κάμπτω apparently a primary verb; to bend: bow.
  2579. κἄν from καί and ἐάν; and (or even) if: and (also) if (so much as), if but, at the least, though, yet.
  2580. Κανᾶ of Hebrew origin (compare קָנָה); Cana, a place in Palestine: Cana.
  2581. Κανανίτης of Chaldee origin (compare קַנָּא); zealous; Cananites, an epithet: Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from Chanaan).
  2582. Κανδάκη of foreign origin; Candacè, an Egyptian queen: Candace.
  2583. κανών from kane (a straight reed, i.e. rod); a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity): line, rule.
  2584. Καπερναούμ of Hebrew origin (probably כְּפַר and נַחוּם); Capernaum (i.e. Caphanachum), a place in Palestine: Capernaum.
  2585. καπηλεύω from kapelos (a huckster); to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively): corrupt.
  2586. καπνός of uncertain affinity; smoke: smoke.
  2587. Καππαδοκία of foreign origin; Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor: Cappadocia.
  2588. καρδία prolonged from a primary kar (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle: (+ broken-)heart(-ed).
  2589. καρδιογνώστης from καρδία and γινώσκω; a heart-knower: which knowest the hearts.
  2590. καρπός probably from the base of ἁρπάζω; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively: fruit.
  2591. Κάρπος perhaps for καρπός; Carpus, probably a Christian: Carpus.
  2592. καρποφορέω from καρποφόρος; to be fertile (literally or figuratively): be (bear, bring forth) fruit(-ful).
  2593. καρποφόρος from καρπός and φέρω; fruitbearing (figuratively): fruitful.
  2594. καρτερέω from a derivative of κράτος (transposed); to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient): endure.
  2595. κάρφος from karpho (to wither); a dry twig or straw: mote.
  2596. κατά a primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined): about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), … by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with. In composition it retains many of these applications, and frequently denotes opposition, distribution, or intensity.
  2597. καταβαίνω from κατά and the base of βάσις; to descend (literally or figuratively): come (get, go, step) down, fall (down).
  2598. καταβάλλω from κατά and βάλλω; to throw down: cast down, lay.
  2599. καταβαρέω from κατά and βαρέω; to impose upon: burden.
  2600. κατάβασις from καταβαίνω; a declivity: descent.
  2601. καταβιβάζω from κατά and a derivative of the base of βάσις; to cause to go down, i.e. precipitate: bring (thrust) down.
  2602. καταβολή from καταβάλλω; a deposition, i.e. founding; figuratively, conception: conceive, foundation.
  2603. καταβραβεύω from κατά and βραβεύω (in its original sense); to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation): beguile of reward.
  2604. καταγγελεύς from καταγγέλλω; a proclaimer: setter forth.
  2605. καταγγέλλω from κατά and the base of ἄγγελος; to proclaim, promulgate: declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach.
  2606. καταγελάω to laugh down, i.e. deride: laugh to scorn.
  2607. καταγινώσκω from κατά and γινώσκω; to note against, i.e. find fault with: blame, condemn.
  2608. κατάγνυμι from κατά and the base of ῥήγνυμι; to rend in pieces, i.e. crack apart: break.
  2609. κατάγω from κατά and ἄγω; to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel: bring (down, forth), (bring to) land, touch.
  2610. καταγωνίζομαι from κατά and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome: subdue.
  2611. καταδέω from κατά and δέω; to tie down, i.e. bandage (a wound): bind up.
  2612. κατάδηλος from κατά intensive and δῆλος; manifest: far more evident.
  2613. καταδικάζω from κατά and a derivative of δίκη; to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty: condemn.
  2614. καταδιώκω from κατά and διώκω; to hunt down, i.e. search for: follow after.
  2615. καταδουλόω from κατά and δουλόω; to enslave utterly: bring into bondage.
  2616. καταδυναστεύω from κατά and a derivative of δυνάστης; to exercise dominion against, i.e. oppress: oppress.
  2617. καταισχύνω from κατά and αἰσχύνομαι; to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush: confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d).
  2618. κατακαίω from κατά and καίω; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. consume wholly: burn (up, utterly).
  2619. κατακαλύπτω from κατά and καλύπτω; to cover wholly, i.e. veil: cover, hide.
  2620. κατακαυχάομαι from κατά and καυχάομαι; to exult against (i.e. over): boast (against), glory, rejoice against.
  2621. κατάκειμαι from κατά and κεῖμαι; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal: keep, lie, sit at meat (down).
  2622. κατακλάω from κατά and κλάω; to break down, i.e. divide: break.
  2623. κατακλείω from κατά and κλείω; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. incarcerate: shut up.
  2624. κατακληροδοτέω from κατά and a derivative of a compound of κλῆρος and δίδωμι; to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate: divide by lot.
  2625. κατακλίνω from κατά and κλίνω; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table: (make) sit down (at meat).
  2626. κατακλύζω from κατά and the base of κλύδων; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge: overflow.
  2627. κατακλυσμός from κατακλύζω; an inundation: flood.
  2628. κατακολουθέω from κατά and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany closely: follow (after).
  2629. κατακόπτω from κατά and κόπτω; to chop down, i.e. mangle: cut.
  2630. κατακρημνίζω from κατά and a derivative of κρημνός; to precipitate down: cast down headlong.
  2631. κατάκριμα from κατακρίνω; an adverse sentence (the verdict): condemnation.
  2632. κατακρίνω from κατά and κρίνω; to judge against, i.e. sentence: condemn, damn.
  2633. κατάκρισις from κατακρίνω; sentencing adversely (the act): condemn(-ation).
  2634. κατακυριεύω from κατά and κυριεύω; to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate: exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.
  2635. καταλαλέω from κατάλαλος; to be a traducer, i.e. to slander: speak against (evil of).
  2636. καταλαλία from κατάλαλος; defamation: backbiting, evil speaking.
  2637. κατάλαλος from κατά and the base of λαλέω; talkative against, i.e. a slanderer: backbiter.
  2638. καταλαμβάνω from κατά and λαμβάνω; to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively): apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.
  2639. καταλέγω from κατά and λέγω (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol: take into the number.
  2640. κατάλειμμα from καταλείπω; a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few: remnant.
  2641. καταλείπω from κατά and λείπω; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining: forsake, leave, reserve.
  2642. καταλιθάζω from κατά and λιθάζω; to stone down, i.e. to death: stone.
  2643. καταλλαγή from καταλλάσσω; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor: atonement, reconciliation(-ing).
  2644. καταλλάσσω from κατά and ἀλλάσσω; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference: reconcile.
  2645. κατάλοιπος from κατά and λοιποί; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest): residue.
  2646. κατάλυμα from καταλύω; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place: guestchamber, inn.
  2647. καταλύω from κατά and λύω; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare κατάλυμα) to halt for the night: destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down.
  2648. καταμανθάνω from κατά and μανθάνω; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully: consider.
  2649. καταμαρτυρέω from κατά and μαρτυρέω; to testify against: witness against.
  2650. καταμένω from κατά and μένω; to stay fully, i.e. reside: abide.
  2651. καταμόνας from κατά and accusative case plural feminine of μόνος (with χώρα implied); according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately: alone.
  2652. κατανάθεμα from κατά (intensive) and ἀνάθεμα; an imprecation: curse.
  2653. καταναθεματίζω from κατά (intensive) and ἀναθεματίζω; to imprecate: curse.
  2654. καταναλίσκω from κατά and ἀναλίσκω; to consume utterly: consume.
  2655. καταναρκάω from κατά and narkao (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive): be burdensome (chargeable).
  2656. κατανεύω from κατά and νεύω; to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make signs to: beckon.
  2657. κατανοέω from κατά and νοιέω; to observe fully: behold, consider, discover, perceive.
  2658. καταντάω from κατά and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet against, i.e. arrive at (literally or figuratively): attain, come.
  2659. κατάνυξις from κατανύσσω; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with νεύω or even with νύξ)) stupor (lethargy): slumber.
  2660. κατανύσσω from κατά and νύσσω; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick"): prick.
  2661. καταξιόω from κατά and ἀξιόω; to deem entirely deserving: (ac-)count worthy.
  2662. καταπατέω from κατά and πατέω; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain: trample, tread (down, underfoot).
  2663. κατάπαυσις from καταπαύω; reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode: rest.
  2664. καταπαύω from κατά and παύω; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist: cease, (give) rest(-rain).
  2665. καταπέτασμα from a compound of κατά and a congener of πέτομαι; something spread thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place) in the Jewish Temple: vail.
  2666. καταπίνω from κατά and πίνω; to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or figuratively): devour, drown, swallow (up).
  2667. καταπίπτω from κατά and πίπτω; to fall down: fall (down).
  2668. καταπλέω from κατά and πλέω; to sail down upon a place, i.e. to land at: arrive.
  2669. καταπονέω from κατά and a derivative of πόνος; to labor down, i.e. wear with toil (figuratively, harass): oppress, vex.
  2670. καταποντίζω from κατά and a derivative of the same as Πόντος; to plunge down, i.e. submerge: drown, sink.
  2671. κατάρα from κατά (intensive) and ἀρά; imprecation, execration: curse(-d, ing).
  2672. καταράομαι middle voice from κατάρα; to execrate; by analogy, to doom: curse.
  2673. καταργέω from κατά and ἀργέω; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively: abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void.
  2674. καταριθμέω from κατά and ἀριθμέω; to reckon among: number with.
  2675. καταρτίζω from κατά and a derivative of ἄρτιος; to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust: fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore.
  2676. κατάρτισις from καταρτίζω; thorough equipment (subjectively): perfection.
  2677. καταρτισμός from καταρτίζω; complete furnishing (objectively): perfecting.
  2678. κατασείω from κατά and σείω; to sway downward, i.e. make a signal: beckon.
  2679. κατασκάπτω from κατά and σκάπτω; to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy: dig down, ruin.
  2680. κατασκευάζω from κατά and a derivative of σκεῦος; to prepare thoroughly (properly, by external equipment; whereas ἑτοιμάζω refers rather to internal fitness); by implication, to construct, create: build, make, ordain, prepare.
  2681. κατασκηνόω from κατά and σκηνόω; to camp down, i.e. haunt; figuratively, to remain: lodge, rest.
  2682. κατασκήνωσις from κατασκηνόω; an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch: nest.
  2683. κατασκιάζω from κατά and a derivative of σκιά; to overshade, i.e. cover: shadow.
  2684. κατασκοπέω from κατάσκοπος; to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously: spy out.
  2685. κατάσκοπος from κατά (intensive) and σκοπός (in the sense of a watcher); a reconnoiterer: spy.
  2686. κατασοφίζομαι middle voice from κατά and σοφίζω; to be crafty against, i.e. circumvent: deal subtilly with.
  2687. καταστέλλω from κατά and στέλλω; to put down, i.e. quell: appease, quiet.
  2688. κατάστημα from καθίστημι; properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively) demeanor: behaviour.
  2689. καταστολή from καταστέλλω; a deposit, i.e. (specially) costume: apparel.
  2690. καταστρέφω from κατά and στρέφω; to turn upside down, i.e. upset: overthrow.
  2691. καταστρηνιάω from κατά and στρηνιάω; to become voluptuous against: begin to wax wanton against.
  2692. καταστροφή from καταστρέφω; an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively, apostasy: overthrow, subverting.
  2693. καταστρώννυμι from κατά and στρώννυμι; to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate (slay): overthrow.
  2694. κατασύρω from κατά and σύρω; to drag down, i.e. arrest judicially: hale.
