  2695. κατασφάττω from κατά and σφάζω; to kill down, i.e. slaughter: slay.
  2696. κατασφραγίζω from κατά and σφραγίζω; to seal closely: seal.
  2697. κατάσχεσις from κατέχω; a holding down, i.e. occupancy: possession.
  2698. κατατίθημι from κατά and τίθημι; to place down, i.e. deposit (literally or figuratively): do, lay, shew.
  2699. κατατομή from a compound of κατά and temno (to cut); a cutting down (off), i.e. mutilation (ironically): concision. Compare ἀποκόπτω.
  2700. κατατοξεύω from κατά and a derivative of τόξον; to shoot down with an arrow or other missile: thrust through.
  2701. κατατρέχω from κατά and τρέχω; to run down, i.e. hasten from a tower: run down.
  2702. καταφέρω from κατά and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote: fall, give, sink down.
  2703. καταφεύγω from κατά and φεύγω; to flee down (away): flee.
  2704. καταφθείρω from κατά and φθείρω; to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or (figuratively) to deprave; --corrupt, utterly perish.
  2705. καταφιλέω from κατά and φιλέω; to kiss earnestly: kiss.
  2706. καταφρονέω from κατά and φρονέω; to think against, i.e. disesteem: despise.
  2707. καταφροντής from καταφρονέω; a contemner: despiser.
  2708. καταχέω from κατά and cheo (to pour); to pour down (out): pour.
  2709. καταχθόνιος from κατά and chthon (the ground); subterranean, i.e. infernal (belonging to the world of departed spirits): under the earth.
  2710. καταχράομαι from κατά and χράομαι; to overuse, i.e. misuse: abuse.
  2711. καταψύχω from κατά and ψύχω; to cool down (off), i.e. refresh: cool.
  2712. κατείδωλος from κατά (intensively) and εἴδωλον; utterly idolatrous: wholly given to idolatry.
  2713. κατέναντι from κατά and ἔναντι; directly opposite: before, over against.
  2714. κατενώπιον from κατά and ἐνώπιον; directly in front of: before (the presence of), in the sight of.
  2715. κατεξουσιάζω from κατά and ἐξουσιάζω; to have (wield) full privilege over: exercise authority.
  2716. κατεργάζομαι from κατά and ἐργάζομαι; to work fully, i.e. accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion: cause, to (deed), perform, work (out).
  2717. κατέρχομαι from κατά and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to come (or go) down (literally or figuratively): come (down), depart, descend, go down, land.
  2718. κατεσθίω from κατά and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to eat down, i.e. devour (literally or figuratively): devour.
  2719. κατευθύνω from κατά and εὐθύνω; to straighten fully, i.e. (figuratively) direct: guide, direct.
  2720. κατεφίστημι from κατά and ἐφίστημι; to stand over against, i.e. rush upon (assault): make insurrection against.
  2721. κατέχω from κατά and ἔχω; to hold down (fast), in various applications (literally or figuratively): have, hold (fast), keep (in memory), let, X make toward, possess, retain, seize on, stay, take, withhold.
  2722. κατηγορέω from κατήγορος; to be a plaintiff, i.e. to charge with some offence: accuse, object.
  2723. κατηγορία from κατήγορος; a complaint ("category"), i.e. criminal charge: accusation (X -ed).
  2724. κατήγορος from κατά and ἀγορά; against one in the assembly, i.e. a complainant at law; specially, Satan: accuser.
  2725. κατήφεια from a compound of κατά and perhaps a derivative of the base of φαίνω (meaning downcast in look); demureness, i.e. (by implication) sadness: heaviness.
  2726. κατηχέω from κατά and ἦχος; to sound down into the ears, i.e. (by implication) to indoctrinate ("catechize") or (genitive case) to apprise of: inform, instruct, teach.
  2727. κατιόω from κατά and a derivative of ἰός; to rust down, i.e. corrode: canker.
  2728. κατισχύω from κατά and ἰσχύω; to overpower: prevail (against).
  2729. κατοικέω from κατά and οἰκέω; to house permanently, i.e. reside (literally or figuratively): dwell(-er), inhabitant(-ter).
  2730. κατοίκησις from κατοικέω; residence (properly, the act; but by implication, concretely, the mansion): dwelling.
  2731. κατοικητήριον from a derivative of κατοικέω; a dwelling-place: habitation.
  2732. κατοικία residence (properly, the condition; but by implication, the abode itself): habitation.
  2733. κατοπτρίζομαι middle voice from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (compare ἔσοπτρον); to mirror oneself, i.e. to see reflected (figuratively): behold as in a glass.
  2734. κατόρθωμα from a compound of κατά and a derivative of ὀρθός (compare διόρθωσις); something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration): very worthy deed.
  2735. κάτω; also (compare) katotero (compare κατώτερος); adverb from κατά; downwards: beneath, bottom, down, under.
  2736. κατώτερος comparative from κάτω; inferior (locally, of Hades): lower.
  2737. καῦμα from καίω; properly, a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a glow: heat.
  2738. καυματίζω from καῦμα; to burn: scorch.
  2739. καῦσις from καίω; burning (the act): be burned.
  2740. καυσόω from καῦσις; to set on fire: fervent heat.
  2741. καύσων from καυσόω; a glare: (burning) heat.
  2742. καυτηριάζω from a derivative of καίω; to brand ("cauterize"), i.e. (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively): sear with a hot iron.
  2743. καυχάομαι from some (obsolete) base akin to that of aucheo (to boast) and εὔχομαι; to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense): (make) boast, glory, joy, rejoice.
  2744. καύχημα from καυχάομαι; a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in a good or a bad sense: boasting, (whereof) to glory (of), glorying, rejoice(-ing).
  2745. καύχησις from καυχάομαι; boasting (properly, the act; by implication, the object), in a good or a bad sense: boasting, whereof I may glory, glorying, rejoicing.
  2746. Κεγχρεαί probably from kegchros (millet); Cenchreæ, a port of Corinth: Cencrea.
  2747. Κεδρών of Hebrew origin (קִדְרוֹן); Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem: Cedron.
  2748. κεῖμαι middle voice of a primary verb; to lie outstretched (literally or figuratively): be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie. Compare τίθημι.
  2749. κειρία of uncertain affinity; a swathe, i.e. winding-sheet: graveclothes.
  2750. κείρω a primary verb; to shear: shear(-er).
  2751. κέλευμα from κελεύω; a cry of incitement: shout.
  2752. κελεύω from a primary kello (to urge on); "hail"; to incite by word, i.e. order: bid, (at, give) command(-ment).
  2753. κενοδοξία from κενόδοξος; empty glorying, i.e. self-conceit: vain-glory.
  2754. κενόδοξος from κενός and δόξα; vainly glorifying, i.e. self-conceited: desirous of vain-glory.
  2755. κενός apparently a primary word; empty (literally or figuratively): empty, (in) vain.
  2756. κενοφωνία from a presumed compound of κενός and φωνή; empty sounding, i.e. fruitless discussion: vain.
  2757. κενόω from κενός; to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify: make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain.
  2758. κέντρον from kenteo (to prick); a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse): prick, sting.
  2759. κεντυρίων of Latin origin; a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred soldiers: centurion.
  2760. κενῶς adverb from κενός; vainly, i.e. to no purpose: in vain.
  2761. κεραία feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of κέρας; something horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively, the least particle): tittle.
  2762. κεραμεύς from κέραμος; a potter: potter.
  2763. κεραμικός from κέραμος; made of clay, i.e. earthen: of a potter.
  2764. κεράμιον neuter of a presumed derivative of κέραμος; an earthenware vessel, i.e. jar: pitcher.
  2765. κέραμος probably from the base of κεράννυμι (through the idea of mixing clay and water); earthenware, i.e. a tile (by analogy, a thin roof or awning): tiling.
  2766. κεράννυμι prolonged form of a more primary kerao ker-ah'-o (which is used in certain tenses); to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for drinking): fill, pour out. Compare μίγνυμι.
  2767. κέρας from a primary kar (the hair of the head); a horn (literally or figuratively): horn.
  2768. κεράτιον neuter of a presumed derivative of κέρας; something horned, i.e. (specially) the pod of the carob-tree: husk.
  2769. κερδαίνω from κέρδος; to gain (literally or figuratively): (get) gain, win.
  2770. κέρδος of uncertain affinity; gain (pecuniary or genitive case): gain, lucre.
  2771. κέρμα from κείρω; a clipping (bit), i.e. (specially) a coin: money.
  2772. κερματιστής from a derivative of κέρμα; a handler of coins, i.e. money-broker: changer of money.
  2773. κεφάλαιον neuter of a derivative of κεφαλή; a principal thing, i.e. main point; specially, an amount (of money): sum.
  2774. κεφαλαιόω from the same as κεφάλαιον; (specially) to strike on the head: wound in the head.
  2775. κεφαλή from the primary kapto (in the sense of seizing); the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively: head.
  2776. κεφαλίς from κεφαλή; properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled): volume.
  2777. κῆνσος of Latin origin; properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by implication) a tax: tribute.
  2778. κῆπος of uncertain affinity; a garden: garden.
  2779. κηπουρός from κῆπος and ouros (a warden); a garden-keeper, i.e. gardener: gardener.
  2780. κηρίον diminutive from keos (wax); a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb: (honey-)comb.
  2781. κήρυγμα from κηρύσσω; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication, the gospel itself): preaching.
  2782. κῆρυξ from κηρύσσω; a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the gospel): preacher.
  2783. κηρύσσω of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel): preacher(-er), proclaim, publish.
  2784. κῆτος probably from the base of χάσμα; a huge fish (as gaping for prey): whale.
  2785. Κηφᾶς of Chaldee origin (compare כֵּפִים); the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a surname of Peter: Cephas.
  2786. κιβωτός of uncertain derivation; a box, i.e. the sacred ark and that of Noah: ark.
  2787. κιθάρα of uncertain affinity; a lyre: harp.
  2788. κιθαρίζω from κιθάρα; to play on a lyre: harp.
  2789. κιθαρῳδός from κιθάρα and a derivative of the same as ᾠδή; a lyre-singer(-player), i.e. harpist: harper.
  2790. Κιλικία probably of foreign origin; Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor: Cilicia.
  2791. κινάμωμον of foreign origin (compare קִנָּמוֹן); cinnamon: cinnamon.
  2792. κινδυνεύω from κίνδυνος; to undergo peril: be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy.
  2793. κίνδυνος of uncertain derivation; danger: peril.
  2794. κινέω from kio (poetic for eimi, to go); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively: (re-)move(-r), way.
  2795. κίνησις from κινέω; a stirring: moving.
  2796. Κίς of Hebrew origin (קִישׁ); Cis (i.e. Kish), an Israelite: Cis.
  2797. κλάδος from κλάω; a twig or bough (as if broken off): branch.
  2798. κλαίω of uncertain affinity; to sob, i.e. wail aloud (whereas δακρύω is rather to cry silently): bewail, weep.
  2799. κλάσις from κλάω; fracture (the act): breaking.
  2800. κλάσμα from κλάω; a piece (bit): broken, fragment.
  2801. Κλαύδη of uncertain derivation; Claude, an island near Crete: Clauda.
  2802. Κλαυδία feminine of Κλαύδιος; Claudia, a Christian woman: Claudia.
  2803. Κλαύδιος of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans: Claudius.
  2804. κλαυθμός from κλαίω; lamentation: wailing, weeping, X wept.
  2805. κλάω a primary verb; to break (specially, of bread): break.
  2806. κλείς from κλείω; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively: key.
  2807. κλείω a primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively): shut (up).
  2808. κλέμμα from κλέπτω; stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act): theft.
  2809. Κλεόπας probably contracted from Kleopatros (compound of κλέος and πατήρ); Cleopas, a Christian: Cleopas.
  2810. κλέος from a shorter form of καλέω; renown (as if being called): glory.
  2811. κλέπτης from κλέπτω; a stealer (literally or figuratively): thief. Compare λῃστής.
  2812. κλέπτω a primary verb; to filch: steal.
  2813. κλῆμα from κλάω; a limb or shoot (as if broken off): branch.
  2814. Κλήμης of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a Christian: Clement.
  2815. κληρονομέω from κληρονόμος; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively): be heir, (obtain by) inherit(-ance).
  2816. κληρονομία from κληρονόμος; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession: inheritance.
  2817. κληρονόμος from κλῆρος and the base of νόμος (in its original sense of partitioning, i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e. inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a possessor: heir.
  2818. κλῆρος probably from κλάω (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose; a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively): heritage, inheritance, lot, part.
  2819. κληρόω from κλῆρος; to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege): obtain an inheritance.
  2820. κλῆσις from a shorter form of καλέω; an invitation (figuratively): calling.
  2821. κλητός from the same as κλῆσις; invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a saint: called.
  2822. κλίβανος of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in: oven.
  2823. κλίμα from κλίνω; a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country: part, region.
  2824. κλίνη from κλίνω; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating): bed, table.
  2825. κλινίδιον neuter of a presumed derivative of κλίνη; a pallet or little couch: bed.
  2826. κλίνω a primary verb; to slant or slope, i.e. incline or recline (literally or figuratively): bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away.
  2827. κλισία from a derivative of κλίνω; properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and specially), a party at a meal: company.
  2828. κλοπή from κλέπτω; stealing: theft.
  2829. κλύδων from kluzo (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively): raging, wave.
  2830. κλυδωνίζομαι middle voice from κλύδων; to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to fluctuate: toss to and fro.
  2831. Κλωπᾶς of Chaldee origin (corresponding to אַחְאָב); Clopas, an Israelite: Cleophas.
  2832. κνήθω from a primary knao (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle: X itching.
  2833. Κνίδος probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor: Cnidus.
  2834. κοδράντης of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as: farthing.
  2835. κοιλία from koilos ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart: belly, womb.
  2836. κοιμάω from κεῖμαι; to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to slumber; figuratively, to decease: (be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead.
  2837. κοίμησις from κοιμάω; sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose: taking of rest.
  2838. κοινός probably from σύν; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane: common, defiled, unclean, unholy.
  2839. κοινόω from κοινός; to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially): call common, defile, pollute, unclean.
  2840. κοινωνέω from κοινωνός; to share with others (objectively or subjectively): communicate, distribute, be partaker.
  2841. κοινωνία from κοινωνός; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction: (to) communicate(-ation), communion, (contri-)distribution, fellowship.
  2842. κοινωνικός from κοινωνός; communicative, i.e. (pecuniarily) liberal: willing to communicate.
  2843. κοινωνός from κοινός; a sharer, i.e. associate: companion, X fellowship, partaker, partner.
  2844. κοίτη from κεῖμαι; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm: bed, chambering, X conceive.
  2845. κοιτών from κοίτη; a bedroom: + chamberlain.
  2846. κόκκινος from κόκκος (from the kernel-shape of the insect); crimson-colored: scarlet (colour, coloured).
  2847. κόκκος apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed: corn, grain.
  2848. κολάζω from kolos (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction): punish.
  2849. κολακεία from a derivative of kolax (a fawner); flattery: X flattering.
  2850. κόλασις from κολάζω; penal infliction: punishment, torment.
  2851. κολαφίζω from a derivative of the base of κολάζω; to rap with the fist: buffet.
  2852. κολλάω from kolla ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively): cleave, join (self), keep company.
  2853. κολλούριον neuter of a presumed derivative of kollura (a cake; prob akin to the base of κολλάω); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster: eyesalve.
  2854. κολλυβιστής from a presumed derivative of kollubos (a small coin; probably akin to κολλούριον); a coin-dealer: (money-)changer.
  2855. κολοβόω from a derivative of the base of κολάζω; to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge: shorten.
  2856. Κολοσσαί apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossæ, a place in Asia Minor: Colosse.
  2857. Κολοσσαεύς from Κολοσσαί; a Colossæan, (i.e. inhabitant of Colossæ: Colossian.
  2858. κόλπος apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay: bosom, creek.
  2859. κολυμβάω from kolumbos (a diver); to plunge into water: swim.
  2860. κολυμβήθρα from κολυμβάω; a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming): pool.
  2861. κολωνία of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans: colony.
  2862. κομάω from κόμη; to wear tresses of hair: have long hair.
  2863. κόμη apparently from the same as κομίζω; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from θρίξ; which properly denotes merely the scalp): hair.
  2864. κομίζω from a primary komeo (to tend, i.e. take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain): bring, receive.
  2865. κομψότερον neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of κομίζω (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. nice); figuratively, convalescent: + began to amend.
  2866. κονιάω from konia (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash: whiten.
  2867. κονιορτός from the base of κονιάω and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about): dust.
  2868. κοπάζω from κόπος; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax: cease.
  2869. κοπετός from κόπτω; mourning (properly, by beating the breast): lamentation.
  2870. κοπή from κόπτω; cutting, i.e. carnage: slaughter.
  2871. κοπιάω from a derivative of κόπος; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard: (bestow) labour, toil, be wearied.
  2872. κόπος from κόπτω; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains: labour, + trouble, weariness.
  2873. κοπρία from kopros (ordure; perhaps akin to κόπτω); manure: dung(-hill).
  2874. κόπτω a primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief: cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of τομώτερος.
  2875. κόραξ perhaps from κορέννυμι; a crow (from its voracity): raven.
  2876. κοράσιον neuter of a presumed derivative of kore (a maiden); a (little) girl: damsel, maid.
  2877. κορβᾶν and korbanas of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (קָרְבָן); a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where the contribution boxes stood: Corban, treasury.
  2878. Κορέ of Hebrew origin (קֹ֫רַח); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite: Core.
  2879. κορέννυμι a primary verb; to cram, i.e. glut or sate: eat enough, full.
  2880. Κορίνθιος from Κόρινθος; a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth: Corinthian.
  2881. Κόρινθος of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece: Corinth.
  2882. Κορνήλιος of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman: Cornelius.
  2883. κόρος of Hebrew origin (כֹּר); a cor, i.e. a specific measure: measure.
  2884. κοσμέω from κόσμος; to put in proper order, i.e. decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick): adorn, garnish, trim.
  2885. κοσμικός from κόσμος (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt): worldly.
  2886. κόσμιος from κόσμος (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. decorous: of good behaviour, modest.
  2887. κοσμοκράτωρ from κόσμος and κρατέω; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan: ruler.
  2888. κόσμος probably from the base of κομίζω; orderly arrangement, i.e. decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)): adorning, world.
  2889. Κούαρτος of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian: Quartus.
  2890. κοῦμι of Chaldee origin (קוּם); cumi (i.e. rise!): cumi.
  2891. κουστωδία of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry: watch.
  2892. κουφίζω from kouphos (light in weight); to unload: lighten.
  2893. κόφινος of uncertain derivation; a (small) basket: basket.
  2894. κράββατος probably of foreign origin; a mattress: bed.
  2895. κράζω a primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat): cry (out).
  2896. κραιπάλη probably from the same as ἁρπάζω; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut): surfeiting.
  2897. κρανίον diminutive of a derivative of the base of κέρας; a skull ("cranium"): Calvary, skull.
  2898. κράσπεδον of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel: border, hem.
  2899. κραταιός from κράτος; powerful: mighty.
  2900. κραταιόω from κραταιός; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor: be strengthened, be (wax) strong.
  2901. κρατέω from κράτος; to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or figuratively): hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by).
  2902. κράτιστος superlative of a derivative of κράτος; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable: most excellent (noble).
  2903. κράτος perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively): dominion, might(-ily), power, strength.
  2904. κραυγάζω from κραυγή; to clamor: cry out.
  2905. κραυγή from κράζω; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief): clamour, cry(-ing).
  2906. κρέας perhaps a primary word; (butcher's) meat: flesh.
  2907. κρεῖσσον neuter of an alternate form of κρείττων; (as noun) better, i.e. greater advantage: better.
  2908. κρείττων comparative of a derivative of κράτος; stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. nobler: best, better.
  2909. κρεμάννυμι a prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang: hang.
  2910. κρημνός from κρεμάννυμι; overhanging, i.e. a precipice: steep place.
  2911. Κρής from Κρήτη; a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete: Crete, Cretian.
  2912. Κρήσκης of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian: Crescens.
  2913. Κρήτη of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean: Crete.
  2914. κριθή of uncertain derivation; barley: barley.
  2915. κρίθινος from κριθή; consisting of barley: barley.
  2916. κρίμα from κρίνω; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")): avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.
  2917. κρίνον perhaps a prim word; a lily: lily.
  2918. κρίνω properly, to distinguish, i.e. decide (mentally or judicially); by implication, to try, condemn, punish: avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.
  2919. κρίσις decision (subjectively or objectively, for or against); by extension, a tribunal; by implication, justice (especially, divine law): accusation, condemnation, damnation, judgment.
  2920. Κρίσπος of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian: Crispus.
  2921. κριτήριον neuter of a presumed derivative of κριτής; a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal: to judge, judgment (seat).
  2922. κριτής from κρίνω; a judge (genitive case or specially): judge.
  2923. κριτικός from κριτής; decisive ("critical"), i.e. discriminative: discerner.
  2924. κρούω apparently a primary verb; to rap: knock.
  2925. κρύπτη feminine of κρυπτός; a hidden place, i.e. cellar ("crypt"): secret.
  2926. κρυπτός from κρύπτω; concealed, i.e. private: hid(-den), inward(-ly), secret.
  2927. κρύπτω a primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering): hide (self), keep secret, secret(-ly).
  2928. κρυσταλλίζω from κρύσταλλος; to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize"): be clear as crystal.
  2929. κρύσταλλος from a derivative of kruos (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal": crystal.
  2930. κρυφῆ adverb from κρύπτω; privately: in secret.
  2931. κτάομαι a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own): obtain, possess, provide, purchase.
  2932. κτῆμα from κτάομαι; an acquirement, i.e. estate: possession.
  2933. κτῆνος from κτάομαι; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal: beast.
  2934. κτήτωρ from κτάομαι; an owner: possessor.
  2935. κτίζω probably akin to κτάομαι (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. found (form originally): create, Creator, make.
  2936. κτίσις from κτίζω; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively): building, creation, creature, ordinance.
  2937. κτίσμα from κτίζω; an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created thing): creature.
  2938. κτίστης from κτίζω; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things): Creator.
  2939. κυβεία from kubos (a "cube", i.e. die for playing); gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud: sleight.
  2940. κυβέρνησις from kubernao (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church): government.
  2941. κυβερνήτης from the same as κυβέρνησις; helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain: (ship) master.
  2942. κυκλόθεν adverb from the same as κύκλῳ; from the circle, i.e. all around: (round) about.
  2943. κυκλόω from the same as κύκλῳ; to encircle, i.e. surround: compass (about), come (stand) round about.
  2944. κύκλῳ as if dative case of kuklos (a ring, "cycle"; akin to κυλιόω); i.e. in a circle (by implication, of ἐν), i.e. (adverbially) all around: round about.
  2945. κύλισμα from κυλιόω; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth: wallowing.
  2946. κυλιόω from the base of κῦμα (through the idea of circularity; compare κύκλῳ, εἱλίσσω); to roll about: wallow.
  2947. κυλλός from the same as κυλιόω; rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands): maimed.
  2948. κῦμα from kuo (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling): wave.
  2949. κύμβαλον from a derivative of the base of κῦμα; a "cymbal" (as hollow): cymbal.
  2950. κύμινον of foreign origin (compare כַּמֹּן); dill or fennel ("cummin"): cummin.
  2951. κυνάριον neuter of a presumed derivative of κύων; a puppy: dog.
  2952. Κύπριος from Κύπρος; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus: of Cyprus.
  2953. Κύπρος of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean: Cyprus.
  2954. κύπτω probably from the base of κῦμα; to bend forward: stoop (down).
  2955. Κυρηναῖος from Κυρήνη; i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene: of Cyrene, Cyrenian.
  2956. Κυρήνη of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa: Cyrene.
  2957. Κυρήνιος of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman: Cyrenius.
  2958. Κυρία feminine of κύριος; Cyria, a Christian woman: lady.
  2959. κυριακός from κύριος; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus): Lord's.
  2960. κυριεύω from κύριος; to rule: have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over.
  2961. κύριος from kuros (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title): God, Lord, master, Sir.
  2962. κυριότης from κύριος; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers: dominion, government.
  2963. κυρόω from the same as κύριος; to make authoritative, i.e. ratify: confirm.
  2964. κύων a primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively): dog.
  2965. κῶλον from the base of κολάζω; a limb of the body (as if lopped): carcase.
  2966. κωλύω from the base of κολάζω; to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or act): forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.
  2967. κώμη from κεῖμαι; a hamlet (as if laid down): town, village.
  2968. κωμόπολις from κώμη and πόλις; an unwalled city: town.
  2969. κῶμος from κεῖμαι; a carousal (as if letting loose): revelling, rioting.
  2970. κώνωψ apparently a derivative of the base of κέντρον and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis): gnat.
  2971. Κώς of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean: Cos.
  2972. Κωσάμ of Hebrew origin (compare קָ֫סֶם); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite: Cosam.
  2973. κωφός from κόπτω; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb): deaf, dumb, speechless.
  2974. λαγχάνω a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot: his lot be, cast lots, obtain.
  2975. Λάζαρος probably of Hebrew origin (אֶלְעָזָר); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary): Lazarus.
  2976. λάθρα adverb from λανθάνω; privately: privily, secretly.
  2977. λαῖλαψ of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall): storm, tempest.
  2978. λακτίζω from adverb lax (heelwise); to recalcitrate: kick.
  2979. λαλέω a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. utter words: preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare λέγω.
  2980. λαλιά from λαλέω; talk: saying, speech.
  2981. λαμά or lamma; of Hebrew origin (מָה with prepositional prefix); lama (i.e. why): lama.
  2982. λαμβάνω a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas δέχομαι is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while αἱρέομαι is more violent, to seize or remove)): accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).
  2983. Λάμεχ of Hebrew origin (לָ֫מֶך); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch: Lamech.
  2984. λαμπάς from λάμπω; a "lamp" or flambeau: lamp, light, torch.
  2985. λαμπρός from the same as λαμπάς; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance): bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white.
  2986. λαμπρότης from λαμπρός; brilliancy: brightness.
  2987. λαμπρῶς adverb from λαμπρός; brilliantly, i.e. figuratively, luxuriously: sumptuously.
  2988. λάμπω a primary verb; to beam, i.e. radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively): give light, shine.
  2989. λανθάνω a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly: be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.
  2990. λαξευτός from a compound of las (a stone) and the base of ξηρός (in its original sense of scraping); rock-quarried: hewn in stone.
  2991. λαός apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from δῆμος, which denotes one's own populace): people.
  2992. Λαοδίκεια from a compound of λαός and δίκη; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor: Laodicea.
  2993. Λαοδικεύς from Λαοδίκεια; a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia: Laodicean.
  2994. λάρυγξ of uncertain derivation; the throat ("larynx"): throat.
  2995. Λασαία of uncertain origin; Lasæa, a place in Crete: Lasea.
  2996. λάσχω a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall): burst asunder.
  2997. λατομέω from the same as the first part of λαξευτός and the base of τομώτερος; to quarry: hew.
  2998. λατρεία from λατρεύω; ministration of God, i.e. worship: (divine) service.
  2999. λατρεύω from latris (a hired menial); to minister (to God), i.e. render religious homage: serve, do the service, worship(-per).
  3000. λάχανον from lachaino (to dig); a vegetable: herb.
  3001. Λεββαῖος of uncertain origin; Lebbæus, a Christian: Lebbæus.
  3002. λεγεών of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively): legion.
  3003. λέγω a primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas ἔπω and φημί generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while ῥέω is properly to break silence merely, and λαλέω means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean: ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter.
  3004. λεῖμμα from λείπω; a remainder: remnant.
  3005. λεῖος apparently a primary word; smooth, i.e. "level": smooth.
  3006. λείπω a primary verb; to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail or be absent: be destitute (wanting), lack.
  3007. λειτουργέω from λειτουργός; to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve): minister.
  3008. λειτουργία from λειτουργέω; public function (as priest ("liturgy") or almsgiver): ministration(-try), service.
  3009. λειτουργικός from the same as λειτουργέω; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. beneficient: ministering.
  3010. λειτουργός from a derivative of λαός and ἔργον; a public servant, i.e. a functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man): minister(-ed).
  3011. λέντιον of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. apron: towel.
  3012. λεπίς from lepo (to peel); a flake: scale.
  3013. λέπρα from the same as λεπίς; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy": leprosy.
  3014. λεπρός from the same as λέπρα; scaly, i.e. leprous (a leper): leper.
  3015. λεπτόν neuter of a derivative of the same as λεπίς; something scaled (light), i.e. a small coin: mite.
  3016. Λευΐ of Hebrew origin (לֵוִי); Levi, the name of three Israelites: Levi. Compare Λευΐς.
  3017. Λευΐς a form of Λευΐ; Lewis (i.e. Levi), a Christian: Levi.
  3018. Λευΐτης from Λευΐ; a Levite, i.e. descendant of Levi: Levite.
  3019. Λευϊτικός from Λευΐτης; Levitic, i.e. relating to the Levites: Levitical.
  3020. λευκαίνω from λευκός; to whiten: make white, whiten.
  3021. λευκός from luke ("light"); white: white.
  3022. λέων a primary word; a "lion": lion.
  3023. λήθη from λανθάνω; forgetfulness: + forget.
  3024. ληνός apparently a primary word; a trough, i.e. wine-vat: winepress.
  3025. λῆρος apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. an incredible story: idle tale.
  3026. λῃστής from leizomai (to plunder); a brigand: robber, thief.
  3027. λῆμψις from λαμβάνω; receipt (the act): receiving.
  3028. λίαν of uncertain affinity; much (adverbially): exceeding, great(-ly), sore, very (+ chiefest).
  3029. λίβανος of foreign origin (לְבוֹנָה); the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself: frankincense.
  3030. λιβανωτός from λίβανος; frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it: censer.
  3031. Λιβερτῖνος of Latin origin; a Roman freedman: Libertine.
  3032. Λιβύη probably from λίψ; Libye, a region of Africa: Libya.
  3033. λιθάζω from λίθος; to lapidate: stone.
  3034. λίθινος from λίθος; stony, i.e. made of stone: of stone.
  3035. λιθοβολέω from a compound of λίθος and βάλλω; to throw stones, i.e. lapidate: stone, cast stones.
  3036. λίθος apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively): (mill-, stumbling-)stone.
  3037. λιθόστρωτος from λίθος and a derivative of στρώννυμι; stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed: Pavement.
  3038. λικμάω from likmos, the equivalent of liknon (a winnowing fan or basket); to winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate: grind to powder.
  3039. λιμήν apparently a primary word; a harbor: haven. Compare Καλοὶ Λιμένες.
  3040. λίμνη probably from λιμήν (through the idea of nearness of shore); a pond (large or small): lake.
  3041. λιμός probably from λείπω (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food: dearth, famine, hunger.
  3042. λίνον probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen": linen.
  3043. Λίνος perhaps from λίνον; Linus, a Christian: Linus.
  3044. λιπαρός from lipos (grease); fat, i.e. (figuratively) sumptuous: dainty.
  3045. λίτρα of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight: pound.
  3046. λίψ probably from leibo (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter): southwest.
  3047. λογία from λόγος (in the commercial sense); a contribution: collection, gathering.
  3048. λογίζομαι middle voice from λόγος; to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally or figuratively): conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).
  3049. λογικός from λόγος; rational ("logical"): reasonable, of the word.
  3050. λόγιον neuter of λόγιος; an utterance (of God): oracle.
  3051. λόγιος from λόγος; fluent, i.e. an orator: eloquent.
  3052. λογισμός from λογίζομαι; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit): imagination, thought.
  3053. λογομαχέω from a compound of λόγος and μάχομαι; to be disputatious (on trifles): strive about words.
  3054. λογομαχία from the same as λογομαχέω; disputation about trifles ("logomachy"): strife of words.
  3055. λόγος from λέγω; something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ): account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work.
  3056. λόγχη perhaps a primary word; a "lance": spear.
  3057. λοιδορέω from λοίδορος; to reproach, i.e. vilify: revile.
  3058. λοιδορία from λοίδορος; slander or vituperation: railing, reproach(-fully).
  3059. λοίδορος from loidos (mischief); abusive, i.e. a blackguard: railer, reviler.
  3060. λοιμός of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally, the disease, or figuratively, a pest): pestilence(-t).
  3061. λοιποί masculine plural of a derivative of λείπω; remaining ones: other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest.
  3062. λοιπόν neuter singular of the same as λοιποί; something remaining (adverbially): besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then.
  3063. λοιποῦ genitive case singular of the same as λοιποί; remaining time: from henceforth.
  3064. Λουκᾶς contracted from Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian: Lucas, Luke.
  3065. Λούκιος of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian: Lucius.
  3066. λουτρόν from λούω; a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism: washing.
  3067. λούω a primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas νίπτω means to wet a part only, and πλύνω to wash, cleanse garments exclusively): wash.
  3068. Λύδδα of Hebrew origin (לֹד); Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine: Lydda.
  3069. Λυδία properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor); Lydia, a Christian woman: Lydia.
  3070. Λυκαονία perhaps remotely from λύκος; Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor: Lycaonia.
  3071. Λυκαονιστί adverb from a derivative of Λυκαονία; Lycaonistically, i.e. in the language of the Lycaonians: in the speech of Lycaonia.
  3072. Λυκία probably remotely from λύκος; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor: Lycia.
  3073. λύκος perhaps akin to the base of λευκός (from the whitish hair); a wolf: wolf.
  3074. λυμαίνομαι middle voice from a probably derivative of λύω (meaning filth); properly, to soil, i.e. (figuratively) insult (maltreat): make havock of.
  3075. λυπέω from λύπη; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad: cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry.
  3076. λύπη apparently a primary word; sadness: grief, grievous, + grudgingly, heaviness, sorrow.
  3077. Λυσανίας from λύσις and ania (trouble); grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene: Lysanias.
  3078. Λυσίας of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman: Lysias.
  3079. λύσις from λύω; a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce: to be loosed.
  3080. λυσιτελεῖ third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of λύσις and τέλος; impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e. is advantageous: it is better.
  3081. Λύστρα of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor: Lystra.
  3082. λύτρον from λύω; something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price (figuratively, atonement): ransom.
  3083. λυτρόω from λύτρον; to ransom (literally or figuratively): redeem.
  3084. λύτρωσις from λυτρόω; a ransoming (figuratively): + redeemed, redemption.
  3085. λυτρωτής from λυτρόω; a redeemer (figuratively): deliverer.
  3086. λυχνία from λύχνος; a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively): candlestick.
  3087. λύχνος from the base of λευκός; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively): candle, light.
  3088. λύω a primary verb; to "loosen" (literally or figuratively): break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off. Compare ῥήγνυμι.
  3089. Λωΐς of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman: Lois.
  3090. Λώτ of Hebrew origin (לוֹט); Lot, a patriarch: Lot.
  3091. Μαάθ probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite: Maath.
  3092. Μαγδαλά of Chaldee origin (compare מִגְדָּל); the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine: Magdala.
  3093. Μαγδαληνή feminine of a derivative of Μαγδαλά; a female Magdalene, i.e. inhabitant of Magdala: Magdalene.
  3094. μαγεία from μαγεύω; "magic": sorcery.
  3095. μαγεύω from μάγος; to practice magic: use sorcery.
  3096. μάγος of foreign origin (רַב־מָג); a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician: sorcerer, wise man.
  3097. Μαγώγ of Hebrew origin (NONE); Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party: Magog.
  3098. Μαδιάν of Hebrew origin (מִדְיָן); Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia: Madian.
  3099. μαθητεύω from μαθητής; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar: be disciple, instruct, teach.
  3100. μαθητής from μανθάνω; a learner, i.e. pupil: disciple.
  3101. μαθήτρια feminine from μαθητής; a female pupil: disciple.
  3102. Μαθουσάλα of Hebrew origin (מְתוּשֶׁ֫לַח); Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an antediluvian: Mathusala.
  3103. Μαϊνάν probably of Hebrew origin; Mainan, an Israelite: Mainan.
  3104. μαίνομαι middle voice from a primary mao (to long for; through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac": be beside self (mad).
  3105. μακαρίζω from μακάριος; to beatify, i.e. pronounce (or esteem) fortunate: call blessed, count happy.
  3106. μακάριος a prolonged form of the poetical makar (meaning the same); supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off: blessed, happy(X -ier).
  3107. μακαρισμός from μακαρίζω; beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune: blessedness.
  3108. Μακεδονία from Μακεδών; Macedonia, a region of Greece: Macedonia.
  3109. Μακεδών of uncertain derivation; a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of Macedonia: of Macedonia, Macedonian.
  3110. μάκελλον of Latin origin (macellum); a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop: shambles.
  3111. μακράν feminine accusative case singular of μακρός (ὁδός being implied); at a distance (literally or figuratively): (a-)far (off), good (great) way off.
  3112. μακρόθεν adverb from μακρός; from a distance or afar: afar off, from far.
  3113. μακροθυμέω from the same as μακροθυμώς; to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient: bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure.
  3114. μακροθυμία from the same as μακροθυμώς; longanimity, i.e. (objectively) forbearance or (subjectively) fortitude: longsuffering, patience.
  3115. μακροθυμώς adverb of a compound of μακρός and θυμός; with long (enduring) temper, i.e. leniently: patiently.
  3116. μακρός from μῆκος; long (in place (distant) or time (neuter plural)): far, long.
  3117. μακροχρόνιος from μακρός and χρόνος; long-timed, i.e. long-lived: live long.
  3118. μαλακία from μαλακός; softness, i.e. enervation (debility): disease.
  3119. μαλακός of uncertain affinity; soft, i.e. fine (clothing); figuratively, a catamite: effeminate, soft.
  3120. Μαλελεήλ of Hebrew origin (מַהֲלַלְאֵל); Maleleel (i.e. Mahalalel), an antediluvian: Maleleel.
  3121. μάλιστα neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb mala (very); (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly: chiefly, most of all, (e-)specially.
  3122. μᾶλλον neuter of the comparative of the same as μάλιστα; (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather: + better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather.
  3123. Μάλχος of Hebrew origin (מֶ֫לֶך); Malchus, an Israelite: Malchus.
  3124. μάμμη of natural origin ("mammy"); a grandmother: grandmother.
  3125. μαμμωνᾶς of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. wealth, personified); mammonas, i.e. avarice (deified): mammon.
  3126. Μαναήν of uncertain origin; Manaën, a Christian: Manaen.
  3127. Μανασσῆς of Hebrew origin (מְנַשֶּׁה); Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an Israelite: Manasses.
  3128. μανθάνω prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, matheo, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn (in any way): learn, understand.
  3129. μανία from μαίνομαι; craziness: (+ make) X mad.
  3130. μάννα of Hebrew origin (מָן); manna (i.e. man), an edible gum: manna.
  3131. μαντεύομαι from a derivative of μαίνομαι (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration); to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of foretelling: by soothsaying.
  3132. μαραίνω of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away: fade away.
  3133. μαρὰν ἀθά of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); maranatha, i.e. an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment: Maran-atha.
  3134. μαργαρίτης from margaros (a pearl-oyster); a pearl: pearl.
  3135. Μάρθα probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); Martha, a Christian woman: Martha.
  3136. Μαρία or Mariam of Hebrew origin (מִרְיָם); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females: Mary.
  3137. Μάρκος of Latin origin; Marcus, a Christian: Marcus, Mark.
  3138. μάρμαρος from marmairo (to glisten); marble (as sparkling white): marble.
  3139. μαρτυρέω from μάρτυς; to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively): charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness.
  3140. μαρτυρία from μάρτυς; evidence given (judicially or genitive case): record, report, testimony, witness.
  3141. μαρτύριον neuter of a presumed derivative of μάρτυς; something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle): to be testified, testimony, witness.
  3142. μαρτύρομαι middle voice from μάρτυς; to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation): take to record, testify.
  3143. μάρτυς of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr": martyr, record, witness.
  3144. μασσάομαι from a primary masso (to handle or squeeze); to chew: gnaw.
  3145. μαστιγόω from μάστιξ; to flog (literally or figuratively): scourge.
  3146. μαστίζω from μαστός; to whip (literally): scourge.
  3147. μάστιξ probably from the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of contact); a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease): plague, scourging.
  3148. μαστός from the base of μασσάομαι; a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded up): pap.
  3149. ματαιολογία from ματαιολόγος; random talk, i.e. babble: vain jangling.
  3150. ματαιολόγος from μάταιος and λέγω; an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler: vain talker.
  3151. μάταιος from the base of μάτην; empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol: vain, vanity.
  3152. ματαιότης from μάταιος; inutility; figuratively, transientness; morally, depravity: vanity.
  3153. ματαιόω from μάταιος; to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous: become vain.
  3154. μάτην accusative case of a derivative of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose: in vain.
  3155. Ματθαῖος a shorter form of μάχομαι; Matthæus (i.e. Matthitjah), an Israelite and a Christian: Matthew.
  3156. Ματθάν of Hebrew origin (מַתָּן); Matthan (i.e. Mattan), an Israelite: Matthan.
  3157. Ματθάτ probably a shortened form of Ματταθίας; Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites: Mathat.
  3158. Ματθίας apparently a shortened form of Ματταθίας; Matthias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite: Matthias.
  3159. Ματταθά probably a shortened form of Ματταθίας (compare σωτήριον); Mattatha (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite: Mattatha.
  3160. Ματταθίας of Hebrew origin (מַתִּתְיָה); Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite and a Christian: Mattathias.
  3161. μάχαιρα probably feminine of a presumed derivative of μάχη; a knife, i.e. dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment: sword.
  3162. μάχη from μάχομαι; a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy: fighting, strive, striving.
  3163. μάχομαι middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute: fight, strive.
  3164. μέ a shorter (and probably original) from of ἐμέ; me: I, me, my.
  3165. μεγαλαυχέω from a compound of μέγας and aucheo (to boast; akin to αὐξάνω and καυχάομαι); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic): boast great things.
  3166. μεγαλεῖος from μέγας; magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection: great things, wonderful works.
  3167. μεγαλειότης from μεγαλεῖος; superbness, i.e. glory or splendor: magnificence, majesty, mighty power.
  3168. μεγαλοπρεπής from μέγας and πρέπω; befitting greatness or magnificence (majestic): excellent.
  3169. μεγαλύνω from μέγας; to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol: enlarge, magnify, shew great.
  3170. μεγάλως adverb from μέγας; much: greatly.
  3171. μεγαλωσύνη from μέγας; greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God himself): majesty.
  3172. μέγας (including the prolonged forms, feminine megale, plural megaloi, etc.; compare also μέγιστος, μείζων); big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application): (+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years.
  3173. μέγεθος from μέγας; magnitude (figuratively): greatness.
  3174. μεγιστᾶνες plural from μέγιστος; grandees: great men, lords.
  3175. μέγιστος superlative of μέγας; greatest or very great: exceeding great.
  3176. μεθερμηνεύω from μετά and ἑρμηνεύω; to explain over, i.e. translate: (by) interpret(-ation).
  3177. μέθη apparently a primary word; an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication) intoxication: drunkenness.
  3178. μεθίστημι, or (1 Cor. 13:2) methistano from μετά and ἵστημι; to transfer, i.e. carry away, depose or (figuratively) exchange, seduce: put out, remove, translate, turn away.
  3179. μεθοδεία from a compound of μετά and ὁδεύω (compare "method"); travelling over, i.e. travesty (trickery): wile, lie in wait.
  3180. μεθόριος from μετά and ὅριον; bounded alongside, i.e. contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier): border.
  3181. μεθύσκω a prolonged (transitive) form of μεθύω; to intoxicate: be drunk(-en).
  3182. μέθυσος from μεθύω; tipsy, i.e. (as noun) a sot: drunkard.
  3183. μεθύω from another form of μέθη; to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk: drink well, make (be) drunk(-en).
  3184. μεῖζον neuter of μείζων; (adverbially) in greater degree: the more.
  3185. μειζότερος continued comparative of μείζων; still larger (figuratively): greater.
  3186. μείζων irregular comparative of μέγας; larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age): elder, greater(-est), more.
  3187. μέλαν neuter of μέλας as noun; ink: ink.
  3188. μέλας apparently a primary word; black: black.
  3189. Μελεᾶς of uncertain origin; Meleas, an Israelite: Meleas.
  3190. μελετάω from a presumed derivative of μέλω; to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind: imagine, (pre-)meditate.
  3191. μέλι apparently a primary word; honey: honey.
  3192. μελίσσιος from μέλι; relating to honey, i.e. bee (comb): honeycomb.
  3193. Μελίτη of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean: Melita.
  3194. μέλλω a strengthened form of μέλω (through the idea of expectation); to intend, i.e. be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation): about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend, was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry, which was for, will, would, be yet.
  3195. μέλος of uncertain affinity; a limb or part of the body: member.
  3196. Μελχί of Hebrew origin (מֶ֫לֶך with pronominal suffix, my king); Melchi (i.e. Malki), the name of two Israelites: Melchi.
  3197. Μελχισεδέκ of Hebrew origin (מַלְכִּי־צֶ֫דֶק); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch: Melchisedec.
  3198. μέλω a primary verb; to be of interest to, i.e. to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters): (take) care.
  3199. μεμβράνα of Latin origin ("membrane"); a (written) sheep-skin: parchment.
  3200. μέμφομαι middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame: find fault.
  3201. μεμψίμοιρος from a presumed derivative of μέμφομαι and moira (fate; akin to the base of μέρος); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented): complainer.
  3202. μέν a primary particle; properly, indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with δέ (this one, the former, etc.): even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily. Often compounded with other particles in an intensive or asseverative sense.
  3203. μενοῦνγε from μέν and οὖν and γέ; so then at least: nay but, yea doubtless (rather, verily).
  3204. μέντοι from μέν and τοί; indeed though, i.e. however: also, but, howbeit, nevertheless, yet.
  3205. μένω a primary verb; to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy): abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own.
  3206. μερίζω from μέρος; to part, i.e. (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or (figuratively) to disunite, differ: deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give participle.
  3207. μέριμνα from μερίζω (through the idea of distraction); solicitude: care.
  3208. μεριμνάω from μέριμνα; to be anxious about: (be, have) care(-ful), take thought.
  3209. μερίς feminine of μέρος; a portion, i.e. province, share or (abstractly) participation: part (X -akers).
  3210. μερισμός from μερίζω; a separation or distribution: dividing asunder, gift.
  3211. μεριστής from μερίζω; an apportioner (administrator): divider.
  3212. μέρος from an obsolete but more primary form of meiromai (to get as a section or allotment); a division or share (literally or figuratively, in a wide application): behalf, course, coast, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort(-what).
  3213. μεσημβρία from μέσος and ἡμέρα; midday; by implication, the south: noon, south.
  3214. μεσιτεύω from μεσίτης; to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety): confirm.
  3215. μεσίτης from μέσος; a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor): mediator.
  3216. μεσονύκτιον neuter of compound of μέσος and νύξ; midnight (especially as a watch): midnight.
  3217. Μεσοποταμία from μέσος and ποταμός; Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare אֲרַם נַהֲרַ֫יִם), a region of Asia: Mesopotamia.
  3218. μέσος from μετά; middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun): among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way.
  3219. μεσότοιχον from μέσος and τοῖχος; a partition (figuratively): middle wall.
  3220. μεσουράνημα from a presumed compound of μέσος and οὐρανός; mid-sky: midst of heaven.
  3221. μεσόω from μέσος; to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way over: be about the midst.
  3222. Μεσσίας of Hebrew origin (מָשִׁ֫יחַ); the Messias (i.e. Mashiach), or Christ: Messias.
  3223. μεστός of uncertain derivation; replete (literally or figuratively): full.
  3224. μεστόω from μεστός; to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate: fill.
  3225. μετά a primary preposition (often used adverbially); properly, denoting accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according to the case (genitive association, or accusative succession) with which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between ἀπό or ἐκ and εἰς or πρός; less intimate than ἐν and less close than σύν): after(-ward), X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-)on, + our, X and setting, since, (un-)to, + together, when, with (+ -out). Often used in composition, in substantially the same relations of participation or proximity, and transfer or sequence.
  3226. μεταβαίνω from μετά and the base of βάσις; to change place: depart, go, pass, remove.
  3227. μεταβάλλω from μετά and βάλλω; to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion: change mind.
  3228. μετάγω from μετά and ἁρμόζω; to lead over, i.e. transfer (direct): turn about.
  3229. μεταδίδωμι from μετά and δίδωμι; to give over, i.e. share: give, impart.
  3230. μετάθεσις from μετατίθημι; transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law): change, removing, translation.
  3231. μεταίρω from μετά and αἴρω; to betake oneself, i.e. remove (locally): depart.
  3232. μετακαλέω from μετά and καλέω; to call elsewhere, i.e. summon: call (for, hither).
  3233. μετακινέω from μετά and κινέω; to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove (figuratively): move away.
  3234. μεταλαμβάνω from μετά and λαμβάνω; to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use): eat, have, be partaker, receive, take.
  3235. μετάλημψις from μεταλαμβάνω; participation: taking.
  3236. μεταλλάσσω from μετά and ἀλλάσσω; to exchange: change.
  3237. μεταμέλλομαι from μετά and the middle voice of μέλω; to care afterwards, i.e. regret: repent (self).
  3238. μεταμορφόω from μετά and μορφόω; to transform (literally or figuratively, "metamorphose"): change, transfigure, transform.
  3239. μετανοέω from μετά and νοιέω; to think differently or afterwards, i.e. reconsider (morally, feel compunction): repent.
  3240. μετάνοια from μετανοέω; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's) decision): repentance.
  3241. μεταξύ from μετά and a form of σύν; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining: between, mean while, next.
  3242. μεταπέμπω from μετά and πέμπω; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite: call (send) for.
  3243. μεταστρέφω from μετά and στρέφω; to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively) corrupt: pervert, turn.
  3244. μετασχηματίζω from μετά and a derivative of σχῆμα; to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation): transfer, transform (self).
  3245. μετατίθημι from μετά and τίθημι; to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert: carry over, change, remove, translate, turn.
  3246. μετέπειτα from μετά and ἔπειτα; thereafter: afterward.
  3247. μετέχω from μετά and ἔχω; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink): be partaker, pertain, take part, use.
  3248. μετεωρίζω from a compound of μετά and a collateral form of αἴρω or perhaps rather ἀήρ (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious): be of doubtful mind.
  3249. μετοικεσία from a derivative of a compound of μετά and οἶκος; a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation: X brought, carried(-ying) away (in-)to.
  3250. μετοικίζω from the same as μετοικεσία; to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile: carry away, remove into.
  3251. μετοχή from μετέχω; participation, i.e. intercourse: fellowship.
  3252. μέτοχος from μετέχω; participant, i.e. (as noun) a sharer; by implication, an associate: fellow, partaker, partner.
  3253. μετρέω from μέτρον; to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule); figuratively, to estimate: measure, mete.
  3254. μετρητής from μετρέω; a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids: firkin.
  3255. μετριοπαθέω from a compound of the base of μετρίως and πάθος; to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently): have compassion.
  3256. μετρίως adverb from a derivative of μέτρον; moderately, i.e. slightly: a little.
  3257. μέτρον an apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree): measure.
  3258. μέτωπον from μετά and ops (the face); the forehead (as opposite the countenance): forehead.
  3259. μέχρι or mechris from μῆκος; as far as, i.e. up to a certain point (as a preposition, of extent (denoting the terminus, whereas ἄχρι refers especially to the space of time or place intervening) or conjunction): till, (un-)to, until.
  3260. μή a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas οὐ expresses an absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas οὐ expects an affirmative one)) whether: any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without. Often used in compounds in substantially the same relations. See also ἐὰν μή, ἵνα μή, οὐ μή, μῆκος, μηκύνω, μήν, μή0.
  3261. ἐὰν μή i.e. ἐάν and μή; if not, i.e. unless: X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not.
  3262. ἵνα μή i.e. ἵνα and μή; in order (or so) that not: albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing)).
  3263. οὐ μή i.e. οὐ and μή; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all: any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare μὴ οὐκ.
  3264. μηδαμῶς adverb from a compound of μή and amos (somebody); by no means: not so.
  3265. μηδέ from μή and δέ; but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor: neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as).
  3266. μηδείς, including the irregular feminine medemia, and the neuter meden from μή and εἷς; not even one (man, woman, thing): any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay.
  3267. μηδέποτε from μηδέ and ποτέ; not even ever: never.
  3268. μηδέπω from μηδέ and -πω; not even yet: not yet.
  3269. Μῆδος of foreign origin (compare NONE); a Median, or inhabitant of Media: Mede.
  3270. μηκέτι from μή and ἔτι; no further: any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more.
  3271. μῆκος probably akin to μέγας; length (literally or figuratively) length.
  3272. μηκύνω from μῆκος; to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge: grow up.
  3273. μηλωτή from melon (a sheep); a sheep-skin: sheepskin.
  3274. μήν a stronger form of μέν; a particle of affirmation (only with ἦ); assuredly: + surely.
  3275. μήν a primary word; a month: month.
  3276. μηνύω probably from the same base as μασσάομαι and μνάομαι (i.e. mao, to strive); to disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind), i.e. report, declare, intimate: shew, tell.
  3277. μὴ οὐκ i.e. μή and οὐ; as interrogative and negative, is it not that?: neither (followed by no), + never, not. Compare οὐ μή.
  3278. μήποτε or me pote from μή and ποτέ; not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps): if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not.
  3279. μήπω from μή and -πω; not yet: not yet.
  3280. μήπως or me pos from μή and -πώς; lest somehow: lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps).
  3281. μηρός perhaps a primary word; a thigh: thigh.
  3282. μήτε from μή and τέ; not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even: neither, (n-)or, so as much.
  3283. μήτηρ apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote): mother.
  3284. μήτι from μή and the neuter of τὶς; whether at all: not (the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question).
  3285. μήτιγε from μήτι and γέ; not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still): how much more.
  3286. μήτις or me tis from μή and τὶς; whether any: any (sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence).
  3287. μήτρα from μήτηρ; the matrix: womb.
  3288. μητραλῴας from μήτηρ and the base of ἅλων; a mother-thresher, i.e. matricide: murderer of mothers.
  3289. μητρόπολις from μήτηρ and πόλις; a mother city, i.e. "metropolis": chiefest city.
  3290. μία irregular feminine of εἷς; one or first: a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other.
  3291. μιαίνω perhaps a primary verb; to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate (ceremonially or morally): defile.
  3292. μίασμα from μιαίνω ("miasma"); (morally) foulness (properly, the effect): pollution.
  3293. μιασμός from μιαίνω; (morally) contamination (properly, the act): uncleanness.
  3294. μίγμα from μίγνυμι; a compound: mixture.
  3295. μίγνυμι a primary verb; to mix: mingle.
  3296. μικρόν masculine or neuter singular of μικρός (as noun); a small space of time or degree: a (little) (while).
  3297. μικρός, including the comparative mikroteros apparently a primary word; small (in size, quantity, number or (figuratively) dignity): least, less, little, small.
  3298. Μίλητος of uncertain origin; Miletus, a city of Asia Minor: Miletus.
  3299. μίλιον of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile": mile.
  3300. μιμέομαι middle voice from mimos (a "mimic"); to imitate: follow.
  3301. μιμητής from μιμέομαι; an imitator: follower.
  3302. μιμνήσκω a prolonged form of μνάομαι (from which some of the tenses are borrowed); to remind, i.e. (middle voice) to recall to mind: be mindful, remember.
  3303. μισέω from a primary misos (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by extension, to love less: hate(-ful).
  3304. μισθαποδοσία from μισθαποδότης; requital (good or bad): recompence of reward.
  3305. μισθαποδότης from μισθόω and ἀποδίδωμι; a renumerator: rewarder.
  3306. μίσθιος from μισθός; a wage-earner: hired servant.
  3307. μισθός apparently a primary word; pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad: hire, reward, wages.
  3308. μισθόω from μισθός; to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire: hire.
  3309. μίσθωμα from μισθόω; a rented building: hired house.
  3310. μισθωτός from μισθόω; a wage-worker (good or bad): hired servant, hireling.
  3311. Μιτυλήνη for mutilene (abounding in shellfish); Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos: Mitylene.
  3312. Μιχαήλ of Hebrew origin (מִיכָאֵל); Michael, an archangel: Michael.
  3313. μνᾶ of Latin origin; a mna (i.e. mina), a certain weight: pound.
  3314. μνάομαι middle voice of a derivative of μένω or perhaps of the base of μασσάομαι (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); to bear in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish: be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance. Compare μιμνήσκω.
  3315. Μνάσων of uncertain origin; Mnason, a Christian: Mnason.
  3316. μνεία from μνάομαι or μιμνήσκω; recollection; by implication, recital: mention, remembrance.
  3317. μνῆμα from μνάομαι; a memorial, i.e. sepulchral monument (burial-place): grave, sepulchre, tomb.
  3318. μνημεῖον from μνήμη; a remembrance, i.e. cenotaph (place of interment): grave, sepulchre, tomb.
  3319. μνήμη from μιμνήσκω; memory: remembrance.
  3320. μνημονεύω from a derivative of μνήμη; to exercise memory, i.e. recollect; by implication, to punish; also to rehearse: make mention; be mindful, remember.
  3321. μνημόσυνον from μνημονεύω; a reminder (memorandum), i.e. record: memorial.
  3322. μνηστεύω from a derivative of μνάομαι; to give a souvenir (engagement present), i.e. betroth: espouse.
  3323. μογιλάλος from μόγις and λαλέω; hardly talking, i.e. dumb (tongue-tied): having an impediment in his speech.
  3324. μόγις adverb from a primary mogos (toil); with difficulty: hardly.
  3325. μόδιος of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil): bushel.
  3326. μοί the simpler form of ἐμοί; to me: I, me, mine, my.
  3327. μοιχαλίς a prolonged form of the feminine of μοιχός; an adulteress (literally or figuratively): adulteress(-ous, -y).
  3328. μοιχάω from μοιχός; (middle voice) to commit adultery: commit adultery.
  3329. μοιχεία from μοιχεύω; adultery: adultery.
  3330. μοιχεύω from μοιχός; to commit adultery: commit adultery.
  3331. μοιχός perhaps a primary word; a (male) paramour; figuratively, apostate: adulterer.
  3332. μόλις probably by variation for μόγις; with difficulty: hardly, scarce(-ly), + with much work.
  3333. Μολόχ of Hebrew origin (מֹ֫לֶך); Moloch (i.e. Molek), an idol: Moloch.
  3334. μολύνω probably from μέλας; to soil (figuratively): defile.
  3335. μολυσμός from μολύνω; a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality: filthiness.
  3336. μομφή from μέμφομαι; blame, i.e. (by implication), a fault: quarrel.
  3337. μονή from μένω; a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place): abode, mansion.
  3338. μονογενής from μόνος and γίνομαι; only-born, i.e. sole: only (begotten, child).
  3339. μόνον neuter of μόνος as adverb; merely: alone, but, only.
  3340. μόνος probably from μένω; remaining, i.e. sole or single; by implication, mere: alone, only, by themselves.
  3341. μονόφθαλμος from μόνος and ὀφθαλμός; one-eyed: with one eye.
  3342. μονόω from μόνος; to isolate, i.e. bereave: be desolate.
  3343. μορφή perhaps from the base of μέρος (through the idea of adjustment of parts); shape; figuratively, nature: form.
  3344. μορφόω from the same as μορφή; to fashion (figuratively): form.
  3345. μόρφωσις from μορφόω; formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or (concretely) formula): form.
  3346. μοσχοποιέω from μόσχος and ποιέω; to fabricate the image of a bullock: make a calf.
  3347. μόσχος probably strengthened for oschos (a shoot); a young bullock: calf.
  3348. μόχθος from the base of μόγις; toil, i.e. (by implication) sadness: painfulness, travail.
  3349. μοῦ the simpler form of ἐμοῦ; of me: I, me, mine (own), my.
  3350. μουσικός from Mousa (a Muse); "musical", i.e. (as noun) a minstrel: musician.
  3351. μυελός perhaps a primary word; the marrow: marrow.
  3352. μυέω from the base of μυστήριον; to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach: instruct.
  3353. μῦθος perhaps from the same as μυέω (through the idea of tuition); a tale, i.e. fiction ("myth"): fable.
  3354. μυκάομαι from a presumed derivative of muzo ( to "moo"); to bellow (roar): roar.
  3355. μυκτηρίζω from a derivative of the base of μυκάομαι (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds); to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule: mock.
  3356. μυλικός from μύλος; belonging to a mill: mill(-stone).
  3357. μύλος probably ultimately from the base of μόλις (through the idea of hardship); a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder (millstone): millstone.
  3358. μύλων from μύλος; a mill-house: mill.
  3359. Μύρα of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor: Myra.
  3360. μυριάς from μύριοι; a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite number: ten thousand.
  3361. μυρίζω from μύρον; to apply (perfumed) unguent to: anoint.
  3362. μύριοι plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many); ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many: ten thousand.
  3363. μύρον probably of foreign origin (compare מֹר, σμύρνα); "myrrh", i.e. (by implication) perfumed oil: ointment.
  3364. Μυσία of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor: Mysia.
  3365. μυστήριον from a derivative of muo (to shut the mouth); a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites): mystery.
  3366. μυωπάζω from a compound of the base of μυστήριον and ops (the face; from ὀπτάνομαι); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly): cannot see far off.
  3367. μώλωψ from molos ("moil"; probably akin to the base of μόλις) and probably ops (the face; from ὀπτάνομαι); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark: stripe.
  3368. μωμάομαι from μῶμος; to carp at, i.e. censure (discredit): blame.
  3369. μῶμος perhaps from μέμφομαι; a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person: blemish.
  3370. μωραίνω from μωρός; to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act) as a simpleton: become fool, make foolish, lose savour.
  3371. μωρία from μωρός; silliness, i.e. absurdity: foolishness.
  3372. μωρολογία from a compound of μωρός and λέγω; silly talk, i.e. buffoonery: foolish talking.
  3373. μωρός probably from the base of μυστήριον; dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e. heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd: fool(-ish, X -ishness).
  3374. Μωσεύς or Moses, or Mouses of Hebrew origin; (מֹשֶׁה); Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver: Moses.
  3375. Ναασσών of Hebrew origin (נַחְשׁוֹן); Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an Israelite: Naasson.
  3376. Ναγγαί probably of Hebrew origin (compare נֹ֫גַהּ); Nangæ (i.e. perhaps Nogach), an Israelite: Nagge.
  3377. Ναζαρέθ or Nazaret; of uncertain derivation; Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine: Nazareth.
  3378. Ναζαρηνός from Ναζαρέθ; a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth: of Nazareth.
  3379. Ναζωραῖος from Ναζαρέθ; a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian: Nazarene, of Nazareth.
  3380. Ναθάν of Hebrew origin (נָתָן); Nathan, an Israelite: Nathan.
  3381. Ναθαναήλ of Hebrew origin (נְתַנְאֵל); Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian: Nathanael.
  3382. ναί a primary particle of strong affirmation; yes: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes.
  3383. Ναΐν probably of Hebrew origin (compare נְאוֹת); Nain, a place in Palestine: Nain.
  3384. ναός from a primary naio (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple : shrine, temple. Compare ἱερόν.
  3385. Ναούμ of Hebrew origin (נַחוּם); Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite: Naum.
  3386. νάρδος of foreign origin (compare נֵרְדְּ); "nard": (spike-)nard.
  3387. Νάρκισσος a flower of the same name, from narke (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman: Narcissus.
  3388. ναυαγέω from a compound of ναῦς and ἄγω; to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively: make (suffer) shipwreck.
  3389. ναύκληρος from ναῦς and κλῆρος ("clerk"); a captain: owner of a ship.
  3390. ναῦς from nao or neo (to float); a boat (of any size): ship.
  3391. ναύτης from ναῦς; a boatman, i.e. seaman: sailor, shipman.
  3392. Ναχώρ of Hebrew origin (נָחוֹר); Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham: Nachor.
  3393. νεανίας from a derivative of νέος; a youth (up to about forty years): young man.
  3394. νεανίσκος from the same as νεανίας; a youth (under forty): young man.
  3395. Νεάπολις from νέος and πόλις; new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia: Neapolis.
  3396. Νεεμάν of Hebrew origin (נַעֲמָן); Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian: Naaman.
  3397. νεκρός from an apparently primary nekus (a corpse); dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun): dead.
  3398. νεκρόω from νεκρός; to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue: be dead, mortify.
  3399. νέκρωσις from νεκρόω; decease; figuratively, impotency: deadness, dying.
  3400. νέος including the comparative neoteros neh-o'-ter-os; a primary word; "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate: new, young.
  3401. νεοσσός from νέος; a youngling (nestling): young.
  3402. νεότης from νέος; newness, i.e. youthfulness: youth.
  3403. νεόφυτος from νέος and a derivative of φύω; newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"): novice.
  3404. Νέρων of Latin origin; Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor: Nero.
  3405. νεύω apparently a primary verb; to "nod", i.e. (by analogy), signal: beckon.
  3406. νεφέλη from νέφος; properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud: cloud.
  3407. Νεφθαλείμ of Hebrew origin (נַפְתָּלִי); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine: Nephthalim.
  3408. νέφος apparently a primary word; a cloud: cloud.
  3409. νεφρός of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind: reins.
  3410. νεωκόρος from a form of ναός and koreo (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary: worshipper.
  3411. νεωτερικός from the comparative of νέος; appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile: youthful.
  3412. νή probably an intensive form of ναί; a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as: I protest by.
  3413. νήθω from neo (of like meaning); to spin: spin.
  3414. νηπιάζω from νήπιος; to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently: be a child.
  3415. νήπιος from an obsolete particle ne- (implying negation) and ἔπος; not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian: babe, child (+ -ish).
  3416. Νηρεύς apparently from a derivative of the base of ναῦς (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian: Nereus.
  3417. Νηρί of Hebrew origin (נֵרִיָּה); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite: Neri.
  3418. νησίον diminutive of νῆσος; an islet: island.
  3419. νῆσος probably from the base of ναῦς; an island: island, isle.
  3420. νηστεία from νηστεύω; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement: fast(-ing).
  3421. νηστεύω from νῆστις; to abstain from food (religiously): fast.
  3422. νῆστις from the inseparable negative particle ne- (not) and ἐσθίω; not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously): fasting.
  3423. νηφάλεος, or nephalios from νήφω; sober, i.e. (figuratively) circumspect: sober.
  3424. νήφω of uncertain affinity; to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet: be sober, watch.
  3425. Νίγερ of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian: Niger.
  3426. Νικάνωρ probably from νικάω; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian: Nicanor.
  3427. νικάω from νίκη; to subdue (literally or figuratively): conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory.
  3428. νίκη apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success: victory.
  3429. Νικόδημος from νῖκος and δῆμος; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite: Nicodemus.
  3430. Νικολαΐτης from Νικόλαος; a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus: Nicolaitane.
  3431. Νικόλαος from νῖκος and Λαοδικεύς; victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic: Nicolaus.
  3432. Νικόπολις from νῖκος and πόλις; victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia: Nicopolis.
