  4059. ποιέω apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary; to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct): abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do(-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield. Compare πράσσω.
  4060. ποίημα from ποιέω; a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively): thing that is made, workmanship.
  4061. ποίησις from ποιέω; action, i.e. performance (of the law): deed.
  4062. ποιητής from ποιέω; a performer; specially, a "poet"; --doer, poet.
  4063. ποικίλος of uncertain derivation; motley, i.e. various in character: divers, manifold.
  4064. ποιμαίνω from ποιμήν; to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser): feed (cattle), rule.
  4065. ποιμήν of uncertain affinity; a shepherd (literally or figuratively): shepherd, pastor.
  4066. ποίμνη contraction from ποιμαίνω; a flock (literally or figuratively): flock, fold.
  4067. ποίμνιον neuter of a presumed derivative of ποίμνη; a flock, i.e. (figuratively) group (of believers): flock.
  4068. ποῖος from the base of ποῦ and οἷος; individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one: what (manner of), which.
  4069. πολεμέω from πόλεμος; to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively): fight, (make) war.
  4070. πόλεμος from pelomai (to bustle); warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series): battle, fight, war.
  4071. πόλις probably from the same as πόλεμος, or perhaps from πολύς; a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size): city.
  4072. πολιτάρχης from πόλις and ἄρχω; a town-officer, i.e. magistrate: ruler of the city.
  4073. πολιτεία from πολίτης ("polity"); citizenship; concretely, a community: commonwealth, freedom.
  4074. πολίτευμα from πολιτεύομαι; a community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively): conversation.
  4075. πολιτεύομαι middle voice of a derivative of πολίτης; to behave as a citizen (figuratively): let conversation be, live.
  4076. πολίτης from πόλις; a townsman: citizen.
  4077. πολλάκις multiplicative adverb from πολύς; many times, i.e. frequently: oft(-en, -entimes, -times).
  4078. πολλαπλασίων from πολύς and probably a derivative of πλέκω; manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more: manifold more.
  4079. πολυλογία from a compound of πολύς and λόγος; loquacity, i.e. prolixity: much speaking.
  4080. πολυμερῶς adverb from a compound of πολύς and μέρος; in many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal): at sundry times.
  4081. πολυποίκιλος from πολύς and ποικίλος; much variegated, i.e. multifarious: manifold.
  4082. πολύς including the forms from the alternate pollos; (singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft(-en (-times)), plenteous, sore, straitly. Compare πλεῖστος, πλείων.
  4083. πολύσπλαγχνος from πολύς and σπλάγχνον (figuratively); extremely compassionate: very pitiful.
  4084. πολυτελής from πολύς and τέλος; extremely expensive: costly, very precious, of great price.
  4085. πολύτιμος from πολύς and τιμή; extremely valuable: very costly, of great price.
  4086. πολυτρόπως adverb from a compound of πολύς and τρόπος; in many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form: in divers manners.
  4087. πόμα from the alternate of πίνω; a beverage: drink.
  4088. πονηρία from πονηρός; depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins: iniquity, wickedness.
  4089. πονηρός from a derivative of πόνος; hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from κακός, which refers rather to essential character, as well as from σαπρός, which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners: bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness). See also πονηρότερος.
  4090. πονηρότερος comparative of πονηρός; more evil: more wicked.
  4091. πόνος from the base of πένης; toil, i.e. (by implication) anguish: pain.
  4092. Ποντικός from Πόντος; a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus: born in Pontus.
  4093. Πόντιος of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman: Pontius.
  4094. Πόντος of Latin origin; a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor: Pontus.
  4095. Πόπλιος of Latin origin; apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a Roman: Publius.
  4096. πορεία from πορεύομαι; travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e. career: journey(-ing), ways.
  4097. πορεύομαι middle voice from a derivative of the same as πεῖρα; to traverse, i.e. travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively, die), live, etc.); --depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk.
  4098. πορθέω prolongation from pertho (to sack); to ravage (figuratively): destroy, waste.
  4099. πορισμός from a derivative of poros (a way, i.e. means); furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition): gain.
  4100. Πόρκιος of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman: Porcius.
  4101. πορνεία from πορνεύω; harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry: fornication.
  4102. πορνεύω from πόρνη; to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry: commit (fornication).
  4103. πόρνη feminine of πόρνος; a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater: harlot, whore.
  4104. πόρνος from pernemi (to sell; akin to the base of πιπράσκω); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine): fornicator, whoremonger.
  4105. πόῤῥω adverb from πρό; forwards, i.e. at a distance: far, a great way off. See also πόῤῥωθεν.
  4106. πόῤῥωθεν from πόῤῥω with adverbial enclitic of source; from far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly: afar off.
  4107. ποῤῥωτέρω adverb comparative of πόῤῥω; further, i.e. a greater distance: farther.
  4108. πορφύρα of Latin origin; the "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it: purple.
  4109. πορφυροῦς from πορφύρα; purpureal, i.e. bluish red: purple.
  4110. πορφυρόπωλις feminine of a compound of πορφύρα and πωλέω; a female trader in purple cloth: seller of purple.
  4111. ποσάκις multiplicative from πόσος; how many times: how oft(-en).
  4112. πόσις from the alternate of πίνω; a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught: drink.
  4113. πόσος from an absolute pos (who, what) and ὅς; interrogative pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many): how great (long, many), what.
  4114. ποταμός probably from a derivative of the alternate of πίνω (compare πότος); a current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water: flood, river, stream, water.
  4115. ποταμοφόρητος from ποταμός and a derivative of φορέω; river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream: carried away of the flood.
  4116. ποταπός apparently from πότε and the base of ποῦ; interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort: what (manner of).
  4117. ποτέ from the base of πού and τέ; indefinite adverb, at some time, ever: afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n-)ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when.
  4118. πότε from the base of ποῦ and τέ; interrogative adverb, at what time: + how long, when.
  4119. πότερον neuter of a comparative of the base of ποῦ; interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that: whether.
  4120. ποτήριον neuter of a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; a drinking-vessel; by extension, the contents thereof, i.e. a cupful (draught); figuratively, a lot or fate: cup.
  4121. ποτίζω from a derivative of the alternate of πίνω; to furnish drink, irrigate: give (make) to drink, feed, water.
  4122. Ποτίολοι of Latin origin; little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy: Puteoli.
  4123. πότος from the alternate of πίνω; a drinking-bout or carousal: banqueting.
  4124. πού genitive case of an indefinite pronoun pos (some) otherwise obsolete (compare πόσος); as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly: about, a certain place.
  4125. ποῦ genitive case of an interrogative pronoun pos (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as πού used with the rising slide of inquiry); as adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what locality: where, whither.
  4126. Πούδης of Latin origin; modest; Pudes (i.e. Pudens), a Christian: Pudens.
  4127. πούς a primary word; a "foot" (figuratively or literally): foot(-stool).
  4128. πρᾶγμα from πράσσω; a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object (material): business, matter, thing, work.
  4129. πραγματεία from πραγματεύομαι; a transaction, i.e. negotiation: affair.
  4130. πραγματεύομαι from πρᾶγμα; to busy oneself with, i.e. to trade: occupy.
  4131. πραιτώριον of Latin origin; the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp): (common, judgment) hall (of judgment), palace, prætorium.
  4132. πράκτωρ from a derivative of πράσσω; a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector: officer.
  4133. πρᾶξις from πράσσω; practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a function: deed, office, work.
  4134. πρᾷος a form of πραΰς, used in certain parts; gentle, i.e. humble: meek.
  4135. πρᾳότης from πρᾷος; gentleness, by implication, humility: meekness.
  4136. πρασιά perhaps from prason (a leek, and so an onion-patch); a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement): in ranks.
  4137. πράσσω a primary verb; to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from ποιέω, which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally): commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts.
  4138. πραΰς apparently a primary word; mild, i.e. (by implication) humble: meek. See also πρᾷος.
  4139. πραΰτης from πραΰς; mildness, i.e. (by implication) humility: meekness.
  4140. πρέπω apparently a primary verb; to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right): become, comely.
  4141. πρεσβεία from πρεσβεύω; seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy (concretely, ambassadors): ambassage, message.
  4142. πρεσβεύω from the base of πρεσβύτερος; to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher): be an ambassador.
  4143. πρεσβυτέριον neuter of a presumed derivative of πρεσβύτερος; the order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery": (estate of) elder(-s), presbytery.
  4144. πρεσβύτερος comparative of presbus (elderly); older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter": elder(-est), old.
  4145. πρεσβύτης from the same as πρεσβύτερος; an old man: aged (man), old man.
  4146. πρεσβῦτις feminine of πρεσβύτης; an old woman: aged woman.
  4147. πρηνής from πρό; leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. head foremost: headlong.
  4148. πρίζω a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); to saw in two: saw asunder.
  4149. πρίν adverb from πρό; prior, sooner: before (that), ere.
  4150. Πρίσκα of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman: Prisca. See also Πρίσκιλλα.
  4151. Πρίσκιλλα diminutive of Πρίσκα; Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman: Priscilla.
  4152. πρό a primary preposition; "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to: above, ago, before, or ever. In the comparative, it retains the same significations.
  4153. προάγω from πρό and ἄγω; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous)): bring (forth, out), go before.
  4154. προαιρέομαι from πρό and αἱρέομαι; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend): purpose.
  4155. προαιτιάομαι from πρό and a derivative of αἰτία; to accuse already, i.e. previously charge: prove before.
  4156. προακούω from πρό and ἀκούω; to hear already,i.e. anticipate: hear before.
  4157. προαμαρτάνω from πρό and ἁμαρτάνω; to sin previously (to conversion): sin already, heretofore sin.
  4158. προαύλιον neuter of a presumed compound of πρό and αὐλή; a forecourt, i.e. vestibule (alley-way): porch.
  4159. προβαίνω from πρό and the base of βάσις; to walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years): + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken.
  4160. προβάλλω from πρό and βάλλω; to throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate: put forward, shoot forth.
  4161. προβατικός from πρόβατον; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem: sheep (market).
  4162. πρόβατον probably neuter of a presumed derivative of προβαίνω; something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively): sheep(-fold).
  4163. προβιβάζω from πρό and a reduplicated form of βιάζω; to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate: draw, before instruct.
  4164. προβλέπω from πρό and βλέπω; to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance: provide.
  4165. προγίνομαι from πρό and γίνομαι; to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired: be past.
  4166. προγινώσκω from πρό and γινώσκω; to know beforehand, i.e. foresee: foreknow (ordain), know (before).
  4167. πρόγνωσις from προγινώσκω; forethought: foreknowledge.
  4168. πρόγονος from προγίνομαι; an ancestor, (grand-)parent: forefather, parent.
  4169. προγράφω from πρό and γράφω; to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime).
  4170. πρόδηλος from πρό and δῆλος; plain before all men, i.e. obvious: evident, manifest (open) beforehand.
  4171. προδίδωμι from πρό and δίδωμι; to give before the other party has given: first give.
  4172. προδότης from προδίδωμι (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands); a surrender: betrayer, traitor.
  4173. πρόδρομος from the alternate of προτρέχω; a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor): forerunner.
  4174. προείδω from πρό and εἴδω; foresee: foresee, saw before.
  4175. προελπίζω from πρό and ἐλπίζω; to hope in advance of other confirmation: first trust.
  4176. προέπω from πρό and ἔπω; to say already, to predict: forewarn, say (speak, tell) before. Compare προερέω.
  4177. προενάρχομαι from πρό and ἐνάρχομαι; to commence already: begin (before).
  4178. προεπαγγέλλομαι middle voice from πρό and ἐπαγγέλλω; to promise of old: promise before.
  4179. προερέω from πρό and ἐρέω; used as alternate of προέπω; to say already, predict: foretell, say (speak, tell) before.
  4180. προέρχομαι from πρό and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to go onward, precede (in place or time): go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.
  4181. προετοιμάζω from πρό and ἑτοιμάζω; to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively): ordain before, prepare afore.
  4182. προευαγγελίζομαι middle voice from πρό and εὐαγγελίζω; to announce glad news in advance: preach before the gospel.
  4183. προέχομαι middle voice from πρό and ἔχω; to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel: be better.
  4184. προηγέομαι from πρό and ἡγέομαι; to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference: prefer.
  4185. πρόθεσις from προτίθεμαι; a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God: purpose, shew(-bread).
  4186. προθέσμιος from πρό and a derivative of τίθημι; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with ἡμέρα implied) a designated day: time appointed.
  4187. προθυμία from πρόθυμος; predisposition, i.e. alacrity: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.
  4188. πρόθυμος from πρό and θυμός; forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity: ready, willing.
  4189. προθύμως adverb from πρόθυμος; with alacrity: willingly.
  4190. προΐστημι from πρό and ἵστημι; to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise: maintain, be over, rule.
  4191. προκαλέομαι middle voice from πρό and καλέω; to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate: provoke.
  4192. προκαταγγέλλω from πρό and καταγγέλλω; to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise: foretell, have notice, (shew) before.
  4193. προκαταρτίζω from πρό and καταρτίζω; to prepare in advance: make up beforehand.
  4194. πρόκειμαι from πρό and κεῖμαι; to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward): be first, set before (forth).
  4195. προκηρύσσω from πρό and κηρύσσω; to herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance: before (first) preach.
  4196. προκοπή from προκόπτω; progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or objectively): furtherance, profit.
  4197. προκόπτω from πρό and κόπτω; to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along): increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax.
  4198. πρόκριμα from a compound of πρό and κρίνω; a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. prepossession: prefer one before another.
  4199. προκυρόω from πρό and κυρόω; to ratify previously: confirm before.
  4200. προλαμβάνω from πρό and λαμβάνω; to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise: come aforehand, overtake, take before.
  4201. προλέγω from πρό and λέγω; to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn: foretell, tell before.
  4202. προμαρτύρομαι from πρό and μαρτύρομαι; to be a witness in advance i.e. predict: testify beforehand.
  4203. προμελετάω from πρό and μελετάω; to premeditate: meditate before.
  4204. προμεριμνάω from πρό and μεριμνάω; to care (anxiously) in advance: take thought beforehand.
  4205. προνοέω from πρό and νοιέω; to consider in advance, i.e. look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself): provide (for).
  4206. πρόνοια from προνοέω; forethought, i.e. provident care or supply: providence, provision.
  4207. προοράω from πρό and ὁράω; to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view: foresee, see before.
  4208. προορίζω from πρό and ὁρίζω; to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine: determine before, ordain, predestinate.
  4209. προπάσχω from πρό and πάσχω; to undergo hardship previously: suffer before.
  4210. προπέμπω from πρό and πέμπω; to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in travel: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth.
  4211. προπετής from a compound of πρό and πίπτω; falling forward, i.e. headlong (figuratively, precipitate): heady, rash(-ly).
  4212. προπορεύομαι from πρό and πορεύομαι; to precede (as guide or herald): go before.
  4213. πρός a strengthened form of πρό; a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is predicated): about, according to, against, among, at, because of, before, between, (where-)by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), X together, to (you) -ward, unto, with(-in). In the comparative case, it denotes essentially the same applications, namely, motion towards, accession to, or nearness at.
  4214. προσάββατον from πρό and σάββατον; a fore-sabbath, i.e. the Sabbath-eve: day before the sabbath. Compare παρασκευή.
  4215. προσαγορεύω from πρός and a derivative of ἀγορά (mean to harangue); to address, i.e. salute by name: call.
  4216. προσάγω from πρός and ἄγω; to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach: bring, draw near.
  4217. προσαγωγή from προσάγω (compare ἀγωγή); admission: access.
  4218. προσαιτέω from πρός and αἰτέω; to ask repeatedly (importune), i.e. solicit: beg.
  4219. προσαναβαίνω from πρός and ἀναβαίνω; to ascend farther, i.e. be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat): go up.
  4220. προσαναλίσκω from πρός and ἀναλίσκω; to expend further: spend.
  4221. προσαναπληρόω from πρός and ἀναπληρόω; to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully: supply.
  4222. προσανατίθημι from πρός and ἀνατίθεμαι; to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult: in conference add, confer.
  4223. προσαπειλέω from πρός and ἀπειλέω; to menace additionally: i.e. threaten further.
  4224. προσδαπανάω from πρός and δαπανάω; to expend additionally: spend more.
  4225. προσδέομαι from πρός and δέομαι; to require additionally, i.e. want further: need.
  4226. προσδέχομαι from πρός and δέχομαι; to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence, or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with confidence or patience): accept, allow, look (wait) for, take.
  4227. προσδοκάω from πρός and dokeuo (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await: (be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for.
  4228. προσδοκία from προσδοκάω; apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated: expectation, looking after.
  4229. προσεάω from πρός and ἐάω; to permit further progress: suffer.
  4230. προσεγγίζω from πρός and ἐγγίζω; to approach near: come nigh.
  4231. προσεδρεύω from a compound of πρός and the base of ἑδραῖος; to sit near, i.e. attend as a servant: wait at.
  4232. προσεργάζομαι from πρός and ἐργάζομαι; to work additionally, i.e. (by implication) acquire besides: gain.
  4233. προσέρχομαι from πρός and ἔρχομαι (including its alternate); to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to: (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto).
  4234. προσευχή from προσεύχομαι; prayer (worship); by implication, an oratory (chapel): X pray earnestly, prayer.
  4235. προσεύχομαι from πρός and εὔχομαι; to pray to God, i.e. supplicate, worship: pray (X earnestly, for), make prayer.
  4236. προσέχω from πρός and ἔχω; (figuratively) to hold the mind (νοῦς implied) towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to: (give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard.
  4237. προσηλόω from πρός and a derivative of ἧλος; to peg to, i.e. spike fast: nail to.
  4238. προσήλυτος from the alternate of προσέρχομαι; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte"): proselyte.
  4239. πρόσκαιρος from πρός and καιρός; for the occasion only, i.e. temporary: dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal.
  4240. προσκαλέομαι middle voice from πρός and καλέω; to call toward oneself, i.e. summon, invite: call (for, to, unto).
  4241. προσκαρτερέω from πρός and καρτερέω; to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor): attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually).
  4242. προσκαρτέρησις from προσκαρτερέω; persistancy: perseverance.
  4243. προσκεφάλαιον neuter of a presumed compound of πρός and κεφαλή; something for the head, i.e. a cushion: pillow.
  4244. προσκληρόω from πρός and κληρόω; to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with: consort with.
  4245. πρόσκλισις from a compound of πρός and κλίνω; a leaning towards, i.e. (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism): partiality.
  4246. προσκολλάω from πρός and κολλάω; to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere: cleave, join (self).
  4247. πρόσκομμα from προσκόπτω; a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy: offence, stumbling(-block, (-stone)).
  4248. προσκοπή from προσκόπτω; a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin: offence.
  4249. προσκόπτω from πρός and κόπτω; to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively): beat upon, dash, stumble (at).
  4250. προσκυλίω from πρός and κυλιόω; to roll towards, i.e. block against: roll (to).
  4251. προσκυνέω from πρός and a probable derivative of κύων (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore): worship.
  4252. προσκυνητής from προσκυνέω; an adorer: worshipper.
  4253. προσλαλέω from πρός and λαλέω; to talk to, i.e. converse with: speak to (with).
  4254. προσλαμβάνω from πρός and λαμβάνω; to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality): receive, take (unto).
  4255. πρόσληψις from προσλαμβάνω; admission: receiving.
  4256. προσμένω from πρός and μένω; to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with).
  4257. προσορμίζω from πρός and a derivative of the same as ὁρμή (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at: draw to the shore.
  4258. προσοφείλω from πρός and ὀφείλω; to be indebted additionally: over besides.
  4259. προσοχθίζω from πρός and a form of ochtheo (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at: be grieved at.
  4260. πρόσπεινος from πρός and the same as πεινάω; hungering further, i.e. intensely hungry: very hungry.
  4261. προσπήγνυμι from πρός and πήγνυμι; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross): crucify.
  4262. προσπίπτω from πρός and πίπτω; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm): beat upon, fall (down) at (before).
  4263. προσποιέομαι middle voice from πρός and ποιέω; to do forward for oneself, i.e. pretend (as if about to do a thing): make as though.
  4264. προσπορεύομαι from πρός and πορεύομαι; to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as προπορεύομαι): go before.
  4265. προσρήγνυμι from πρός and ῥήγνυμι; to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood): beat vehemently against (upon).
  4266. προστάσσω from πρός and τάσσω; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin: bid, command.
  4267. προστάτις feminine of a derivative of προΐστημι; a patroness, i.e. assistant: succourer.
  4268. προστίθημι from πρός and τίθημι; to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex, repeat: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more.
  4269. προστρέχω from πρός and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join: run (thither to, to).
  4270. προσφάγιον neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of πρός and φάγω; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare ὀψάριον): meat.
  4271. πρόσφατος from πρό and a derivative of σφάζω; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made: new.
  4272. προσφάτως adverb from πρόσφατος; recently: lately.
  4273. προσφέρω from πρός and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.
  4274. προσφιλής from a presumed compound of πρός and φιλέω; friendly towards, i.e. acceptable: lovely.
  4275. προσφορά from προσφέρω; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice: offering (up).
  4276. προσφωνέω from πρός and φωνέω; to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim, summon: call unto, speak (un-)to.
  4277. πρόσχυσις from a comparative of πρός and cheo (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e. affusion: sprinkling.
  4278. προσψαύω from πρός and psauo (to touch); to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in order to relieve): touch.
  4279. προσωποληπτέω from προσωπολήπτης; to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality: have respect to persons.
  4280. προσωπολήπτης from πρόσωπον and λαμβάνω; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality: respecter of persons.
  4281. προσωποληψία from προσωπολήπτης; partiality, i.e. favoritism: respect of persons.
  4282. πρόσωπον from πρός and ops (the visage, from ὀπτάνομαι); the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.
  4283. προτάσσω from πρό and τάσσω; to pre-arrange, i.e. prescribe: before appoint.
  4284. προτείνω from πρό and teino (to stretch); to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging): bind.
  4285. πρότερον neuter of πρότερος as adverb (with or without the article); previously: before, (at the) first, former.
  4286. πρότερος comparative of πρό; prior or previous: former.
  4287. προτίθεμαι middle voice from πρό and τίθημι; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine): purpose, set forth.
  4288. προτρέπομαι middle voice from πρό and the base of τροπή; to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage: exhort.
  4289. προτρέχω from πρό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede: outrun, run before.
  4290. προϋπάρχω from πρό and ὑπάρχω; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously: + be before(-time).
  4291. πρόφασις from a compound of πρό and φαίνω; an outward showing, i.e. pretext: cloke, colour, pretence, show.
  4292. προφέρω from πρό and φέρω; to bear forward, i.e. produce: bring forth.
  4293. προφητεία from προφήτης ("prophecy"); prediction (scriptural or other): prophecy, prophesying.
  4294. προφητεύω from προφήτης; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office: prophesy.
  4295. προφήτης from a compound of πρό and φημί; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet: prophet.
  4296. προφητικός from προφήτης; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic"): of prophecy, of the prophets.
  4297. προφῆτις feminine of προφήτης; a female foreteller or an inspired woman: prophetess.
  4298. προφθάνω from πρό and φθάνω; to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate: prevent.
  4299. προχειρίζομαι middle voice from πρό and a derivative of χείρ; to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose: choose, make.
  4300. προχειροτονέω from πρό and χειροτονέω; to elect in advance: choose before.
  4301. Πρόχορος from πρό and χορός; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian: Prochorus.
  4302. πρύμνα feminine of prumnus (hindmost); the stern of a ship: hinder part, stern.
  4303. πρωΐ adverb from πρό; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch: early (in the morning), (in the) morning.
  4304. πρωΐα feminine of a derivative of πρωΐ as noun; day-dawn: early, morning.
  4305. πρώϊμος from πρωΐ; dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season): early.
  4306. πρωϊνός from πρωΐ; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal: morning.
  4307. πρῶρα feminine of a presumed derivative of πρό as noun; the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel: forepart(-ship).
  4308. πρωτεύω from πρῶτος; to be first (in rank or influence): have the preeminence.
  4309. πρωτοκαθεδρία from πρῶτος and καθέδρα; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council: chief (highest, uppermost) seat.
  4310. πρωτοκλισία from πρῶτος and κλισία; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals: chief (highest, uppermost) room.
  4311. πρῶτον neuter of πρῶτος as adverb (with or without ὁ); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance): before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all).
  4312. πρῶτος contracted superlative of πρό; foremost (in time, place, order or importance): before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former.
  4313. πρωτοστάτης from πρῶτος and ἵστημι; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion): ringleader.
  4314. πρωτοτόκια from πρωτότοκος; primogeniture (as a privilege): birthright.
  4315. πρωτότοκος from πρῶτος and the alternate of τίκτω; first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively): firstbegotten(-born).
  4316. πταίω a form of πίπτω; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation): fall, offend, stumble.
  4317. πτέρνα of uncertain derivation; the heel (figuratively): heel.
  4318. πτερύγιον neuter of a presumed derivative of πτέρυξ; a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner): pinnacle.
  4319. πτέρυξ from a derivative of πέτομαι (meaning a feather); a wing: wing.
  4320. πτηνόν contraction for πετεινόν; a bird: bird.
  4321. πτοέω probably akin to the alternate of πίπτω (through the idea of causing to fall) or to πέτομαι (through that of causing to fly away); to scare: frighten.
  4322. πτόησις from πτοέω; alarm: amazement.
  4323. Πτολεμαΐς from Ptolemaios (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine: Ptolemais.
  4324. πτύον from πτύω; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle): fan.
  4325. πτύρω from a presumed derivative of πτύω (and thus akin to πτοέω); to frighten: terrify.
  4326. πτύσμα from πτύω; saliva: spittle.
  4327. πτύσσω probably akin to petannumi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to πέτομαι through the idea of expansion, and to πτύω through that of flattening; compare πατέω); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll: close.
  4328. πτύω a primary verb (compare πτύσσω); to spit: spit.
  4329. πτῶμα from the alternate of πίπτω; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion): dead body, carcase, corpse.
  4330. πτῶσις from the alternate of πίπτω; a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or figuratively): fall.
  4331. πτωχεία from πτωχεύω; beggary, i.e. indigence (literally or figuratively): poverty.
  4332. πτωχεύω from πτωχός; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively): become poor.
  4333. πτωχός from ptosso (to crouch); akin to πτοέω and the alternate of πίπτω); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas πένης properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed): beggar(-ly), poor.
  4334. πυγμή from a primary pux (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing): oft.
  4335. Πύθων from Putho (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying): divination.
  4336. πυκνός from the same as σκηνοποιός; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently: often(-er).
  4337. πυκτέω from a derivative of the same as πυγμή; to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively): fight.
  4338. πύλη apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively): gate.
  4339. πυλών from πύλη; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule: gate, porch.
  4340. πυνθάνομαι middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from ἐρωτάω, which properly means a request as a favor; and from αἰτέω, which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from ζητέω, which implies a search for something hidden; and from δέομαι, which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence): ask, demand, enquire, understand.
  4341. πῦρ a primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning): fiery, fire.
  4342. πυρά from πῦρ; a fire (concretely): fire.
  4343. πύργος apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle: tower.
  4344. πυρέσσω from πυρά; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever: be sick of a fever.
  4345. πυρετός from πυρέσσω; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever): fever.
  4346. πύρινος from πυρά; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming: of fire.
  4347. πυρόω from πῦρ; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust): burn, fiery, be on fire, try.
  4348. πυῤῥάζω from πυῤῥός; to redden (intransitively): be red.
  4349. πυῤῥός from πῦρ; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored: red.
  4350. πύρωσις from πυρόω; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test): burning, trial.
  4351. -πω another form of the base of -πώς; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See μηδέπω, μήπω, οὐδέπω, οὔπω, πώποτε.
  4352. πωλέω probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell: sell, whatever is sold.
  4353. πῶλος apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass: colt.
  4354. πώποτε from -πω and ποτέ; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time: at any time, + never (…to any man), + yet, never man.
  4355. πωρόω apparently from poros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous): blind, harden.
  4356. πώρωσις from πωρόω; stupidity or callousness: blindness, hardness.
  4357. -πώς adverb from the base of πού; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition: haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See εἴ πως, μήπως. Compare πῶς.
  4358. πῶς adverb from the base of ποῦ; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!: how, after (by) what manner (means), that. (Occasionally unexpressed in English).
  4359. Ῥαάβ of Hebrew origin (רָחָב); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess: Rahab. See also Ῥαχάβ.
  4360. ῥαββί of Hebrew origin (רָב with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor: Master, Rabbi.
  4361. ῥαββονί, or rhabbouni of Chaldee origin; corresponding to ῥαββί: Lord, Rabboni.
  4362. ῥαβδίζω from ῥάβδος; to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado: beat (with rods).
  4363. ῥάβδος from the base of ῥαπίζω; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty): rod, sceptre, staff.
  4364. ῥαβδοῦχος from ῥάβδος and ἔχω; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner): serjeant.
  4365. Ῥαγαῦ of Hebrew origin (רְעוּ); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch: Ragau.
  4366. ῥᾳδιούργημα from a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and ἔργον; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime: lewdness.
  4367. ῥᾳδιουργία from the same as ῥᾳδιούργημα; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity: mischief.
  4368. ῥακά of Chaldee origin (compare רֵק); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification): Raca.
  4369. ῥάκος from ῥήγνυμι; a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth: cloth.
  4370. Ῥαμᾶ of Hebrew origin (רָמָה); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine: Rama.
  4371. ῥαντίζω from a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively): sprinkle.
  4372. ῥαντισμός from ῥαντίζω; aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively): sprinkling.
  4373. ῥαπίζω from a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, "rap"); to slap: smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare τύπτω.
  4374. ῥάπισμα from ῥαπίζω; a slap: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.
  4375. ῥαφίς from a primary rhapto (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω through the idea of puncturing); a needle: needle.
  4376. Ῥαχάβ from the same as Ῥαάβ; Rachab, a Canaanitess: Rachab.
  4377. Ῥαχήλ of Hebrew origin (רָחֵל); Rachel, the wife of Jacob: Rachel.
  4378. Ῥεβέκκα of Hebrew origin (רִבְקָה); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac: Rebecca.
  4379. ῥέδα of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding): chariot.
  4380. Ῥεμφάν by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (כִּיּוּן); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol: Remphan.
  4381. ῥέω a primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form rheuo is used; to flow ("run"; as water): flow.
  4382. ῥέω, for certain tenses of which a prolonged form ereo is used; and both as alternate for ἔπω perhaps akin (or identical) with ῥέω (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. speak or say: command, make, say, speak (of). Compare λέγω.
  4383. Ῥήγιον of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy: Rhegium.
  4384. ῥῆγμα from ῥήγνυμι; something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall): ruin.
  4385. ῥήγνυμι or rhesso both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi (see in κατάγνυμι)) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; κατάγνυμι being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and θραύω a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like λύω) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions: break (forth), burst, rend, tear.
  4386. ῥῆμα from ῥέω; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever: + evil, + nothing, saying, word.
  4387. Ῥησά probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for רְפָיָה); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite: Rhesa.
  4388. ῥήτωρ from ῥέω; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate: orator.
  4389. ῥητῶς adverb from a derivative of ῥέω; out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly: expressly.
  4390. ῥίζα apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively): root.
  4391. ῥιζόω from ῥίζα; to root (figuratively, become stable): root.
  4392. ῥιπή from ῥίπτω; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant): twinkling.
  4393. ῥιπίζω from a derivative of ῥίπτω (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves): toss.
  4394. ῥιπτέω from a derivative of ῥίπτω; to toss up: cast off.
  4395. ῥίπτω a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of ῥαπίζω, through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from βάλλω, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from teino (see in ἐκτείνω), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse: cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.
  4396. Ῥοβοάμ of Hebrew origin (רְחַבְעָם); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite: Roboam.
  4397. Ῥόδη probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl: Rhoda.
  4398. Ῥόδος probably from rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean: Rhodes.
  4399. ῥοιζηδόν adverb from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash: with a great noise.
  4400. ῥομφαία probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively): sword.
  4401. Ῥουβήν of Hebrew origin (רְאוּבֵן); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite: Reuben.
  4402. Ῥούθ of Hebrew origin (רוּת); Ruth, a Moabitess: Ruth.
  4403. Ῥοῦφος of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian: Rufus.
  4404. ῥύμη prolongation from ῥύομαι in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded): lane, street.
  4405. ῥύομαι middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to ῥέω (through the idea of a current; compare ῥύσις); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue: deliver(-er).
  4406. ῥυπαρία from ῥυπαρός; dirtiness (morally): turpitude.
  4407. ῥυπαρός from ῥύπος; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked: vile.
  4408. ῥύπος of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity: filth.
  4409. ῥυπόω from ῥύπος; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally): be filthy.
  4410. ῥύσις from ῥύομαι in the sense of its congener ῥέω; a flux (of blood): issue.
  4411. ῥυτίς from ῥύομαι; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face): wrinkle.
  4412. Ῥωμαϊκός from Ῥωμαῖος; Romaic, i.e. Latin: Latin.
  4413. Ῥωμαῖος from Ῥώμη; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun): Roman, of Rome.
  4414. Ῥωμαϊστί adverb from a presumed derivative of Ῥώμη; Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language: Latin.
  4415. Ῥώμη from the base of ῥώννυμι; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy: Rome.
  4416. ῥώννυμι prolongation from rhoomai (to dart; probably akin to ῥύομαι); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye): farewell.
  4417. σαβαχθάνι of Chaldee or (שְׁבַק with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress: sabachthani.
  4418. σαβαώθ of Hebrew origin (צָבָא in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God: sabaoth.
  4419. σαββατισμός from a derivative of σάββατον; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven): rest.
  4420. σάββατον of Hebrew origin (שַׁבָּת); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications: sabbath (day), week.
  4421. σαγήνη from a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing: net.
  4422. Σαδδουκαῖος probably from Σαδώκ; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite: Sadducee.
  4423. Σαδώκ of Hebrew origin (צָדוֹק); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite: Sadoc.
  4424. σαίνω akin to σείω; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb): move.
  4425. σάκκος of Hebrew origin (שָׂק); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief): sackcloth.
  4426. Σαλά of Hebrew origin (שָׁ֫לַח); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch : Sala.
  4427. Σαλαθιήλ of Hebrew origin (שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite: Salathiel.
  4428. Σαλαμίς probably from σάλος (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus: Salamis.
  4429. Σαλείμ probably from the same as σαλεύω; Salim, a place in Palestine: Salim.
  4430. σαλεύω from σάλος; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.
  4431. Σαλήμ of Hebrew origin (שָׁלֵם); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine: Salem.
  4432. Σαλμών of Hebrew origin (שַׂלְמוֹן); Salmon, an Israelite: Salmon.
  4433. Σαλμώνη perhaps of similar origin to Σαλαμίς; Salmone, a place in Crete: Salmone.
  4434. σάλος probably from the base of σαίνω; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow: wave.
  4435. σάλπιγξ perhaps from σάλος (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet: trump(-et).
  4436. σαλπίζω from σάλπιγξ; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively): (which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).
  4437. σαλπιστής from σαλπίζω; a trumpeter: trumpeter.
  4438. Σαλώμη probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from שָׁלוֹם); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess: Salome.
  4439. Σαμάρεια of Hebrew origin (שֹׁמְרוֹן); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine: Samaria.
  4440. Σαμαρείτης from Σαμάρεια; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria: Samaritan.
  4441. Σαμαρεῖτις feminine of Σαμαρείτης; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria: of Samaria.
  4442. Σαμοθρᾴκη from Σάμος and Thraike (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean: Samothracia.
  4443. Σάμος of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean: Samos.
  4444. Σαμουήλ of Hebrew origin (שְׁמוּאֵל); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite: Samuel.
  4445. Σαμψών of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְשׁוֹן); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite: Samson.
  4446. σανδάλιον neuter of a derivative of sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad: sandal.
  4447. σανίς of uncertain affinity; a plank: board.
  4448. Σαούλ of Hebrew origin (שָׁאוּל); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul: Saul. Compare Σαῦλος.
  4449. σαπρός from σήπω; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally): bad, corrupt. Compare πονηρός.
  4450. Σαπφείρη feminine of σάπφειρος; Sapphire, an Israelitess: Sapphira.
  4451. σάπφειρος of Hebrew origin (סַפִּיר); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem: sapphire.
  4452. σαργάνη apparently of Hebrew origin (שָׂרַג); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work: basket.
  4453. Σάρδεις plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor: Sardis.
  4454. σάρδινος from the same as σάρδιος; sardine (λίθος being implied), i.e. a gem, so called: sardine.
  4455. σάρδιος properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (λίθος being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called: sardius.
  4456. σαρδόνυξ from the base of σάρδιος and onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called: sardonyx.
  4457. Σάρεπτα of Hebrew origin (צָרְפַת); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine: Sarepta.
  4458. σαρκικός from σάρξ; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate: carnal, fleshly.
  4459. σάρκινος from σάρξ; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft: fleshly.
  4460. σάρξ probably from the base of σαρόω; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such): carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly).
  4461. Σαρούχ of Hebrew origin (שְׂרוּג); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch: Saruch.
  4462. σαρόω from a derivative of sairo (to brush off; akin to σύρω); meaning a broom; to sweep: sweep.
  4463. Σάῤῥα of Hebrew origin (שָׂרָה); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham: Sara, Sarah.
  4464. Σάρων of Hebrew origin (NONE); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine: Saron.
  4465. Σατᾶν of Hebrew origin (שָׂטָן); Satan, i.e. the devil: Satan. Compare Σατανᾶς.
  4466. Σατανᾶς of Chaldee origin corresponding to מַעְבָּדִים (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil: Satan.
  4467. σάτον of Hebrew origin (סְאָה־); a certain measure for things dry: measure.
  4468. Σαῦλος of Hebrew origin, the same as Σαούλ; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul: Saul.
  4469. σβέννυμι a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively): go out, quench.
  4470. σέ accusative case singular of σύ; thee: thee, thou, X thy house.
  4471. σεαυτοῦ, genitive case from σέ and αὐτός, also dative case of the same, seautoi, and accusative case seauton, likewise contracted sautou, sautoi, and sauton, respectively; of (with, to) thyself: thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).
  4472. σεβάζομαι middle voice from a derivative of σέβομαι; to venerate, i.e. adore: worship.
  4473. σέβασμα from σεβάζομαι; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc): devotion, that is worshipped.
  4474. σεβαστός from σεβάζομαι; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial: Augustus(-').
  4475. σέβομαι middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore: devout, religious, worship.
  4476. σειρά probably from σύρω through its congener eiro (to fasten; akin to αἱρέομαι); a chain (as binding or drawing): chain.
  4477. σεισμός from σείω; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake: earthquake, tempest.
  4478. σείω apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern): move, quake, shake.
  4479. Σεκοῦνδος of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian: Secundus.
  4480. Σελεύκεια from Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria: Seleucia.
  4481. σελήνη from selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon: moon.
  4482. σεληνιάζομαι middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of σελήνη; to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy: be a lunatic.
  4483. Σεμεΐ of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעִי); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite: Semei.
  4484. σεμίδαλις probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour: fine flour.
  4485. σεμνός from σέβομαι; venerable, i.e. honorable: grave, honest.
  4486. σεμνότης from σεμνός; venerableness, i.e. probity: gravity, honesty.
  4487. Σέργιος of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman: Sergius.
  4488. Σήθ of Hebrew origin (שֵׁת); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch: Seth.
  4489. Σήμ of Hebrew origin (שֵׁם); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch: Sem.
  4490. σημαίνω from sema (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate: signify.
  4491. σημεῖον neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of σημαίνω; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally: miracle, sign, token, wonder.
  4492. σημειόω from σημεῖον; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance): note.
  4493. σήμερον neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ὁ (t changed to s) and ἡμέρα; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto): this (to-)day.
  4494. σήπω apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish: be corrupted.
  4495. σηρικός from Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric): silk.
  4496. σής apparently of Hebrew origin (סָס); a moth: moth.
  4497. σητόβρωτος from σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; moth-eaten: motheaten.
  4498. σθενόω from sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of ἵστημι); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power): strengthen.
  4499. σιαγών of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face: cheek.
  4500. σιγάω from σιγή; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively): keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.
  4501. σιγή apparently from sizo (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence: silence. Compare σιωπάω.
  4502. σιδήρεος from σίδηρος; made of iron: (of) iron.
  4503. σίδηρος of uncertain derivation; iron: iron.
  4504. Σιδών of Hebrew origin (צִידוֹן); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine: Sidon.
  4505. Σιδώνιος from Σιδών; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon: of Sidon.
  4506. σικάριος of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans): murderer. Compare φονεύς.
  4507. σίκερα of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor: strong drink.
  4508. Σίλας contraction for Σιλουανός; Silas, a Christian: Silas.
  4509. Σιλουανός of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian: Silvanus. Compare Σίλας.
  4510. Σιλωάμ of Hebrew origin (שִׁלֹ֫חַ); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem: Siloam.
  4511. σιμικίνθιον of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron): apron.
  4512. Σίμων of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעוֹן); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites: Simon. Compare Συμεών.
  4513. Σινᾶ of Hebrew origin (סִינַי); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia: Sina.
  4514. σίναπι perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant): mustard.
  4515. σινδών of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it): (fine) linen (cloth).
  4516. σινιάζω from sinion (a sieve); to riddle (figuratively): sift.
  4517. σιτευτός from a derivative of σῖτος; grain-fed, i.e. fattened: fatted.
  4518. σιτιστός from a derivative of σῖτος; grained, i.e. fatted: fatling.
  4519. σιτόμετρον from σῖτος and μέτρον; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food): portion of meat.
  4520. σῖτος, also plural irregular neuter sita of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat: corn, wheat.
  4521. Σιών of Hebrew origin (צִיּוֹן); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant): Sion.
  4522. σιωπάω from siope (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from σιγή, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like κωφός properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water): dumb, (hold) peace.
  4523. σκανδαλίζω from σκάνδαλον; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure): (make to) offend.
  4524. σκάνδαλον ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of κάμπτω; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin): occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.
  4525. σκάπτω apparently a primary verb; to dig: dig.
  4526. σκάφη a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing): boat.
  4527. σκέλος apparently from skello (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank): leg.
  4528. σκέπασμα from a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of σκοπός through the idea of noticeableness); clothing: raiment.
  4529. Σκευᾶς apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite: Sceva.
  4530. σκευή from σκεῦος; furniture, i.e. spare tackle: tackling.
  4531. σκεῦος of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]): goods, sail, stuff, vessel.
  4532. σκηνή apparently akin to σκεῦος and σκιά; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively): habitation, tabernacle.
  4533. σκηνοπηγία from σκῆνος and πήγνυμι; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes): tabernacles.
  4534. σκηνοποιός from σκηνή and ποιέω; a manufacturer of tents: tent-maker.
  4535. σκῆνος from σκηνή; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit): tabernacle.
  4536. σκηνόω from σκῆνος; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion): dwell.
  4537. σκήνωμα from σκηνόω; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul): tabernacle.
  4538. σκιά apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)): shadow.
  4539. σκιρτάω akin to skairo (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus): leap (for joy).
  4540. σκληροκαρδία feminine of a compound of σκληρός and καρδία; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception: hardness of heart.
  4541. σκληρός from the base of σκέλος; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe): fierce, hard.
  4542. σκληρότης from σκληρός; callousness, i.e. (figuratively) stubbornness: hardness.
  4543. σκληροτράχηλος from σκληρός and τράχηλος; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate: stiffnecked.
  4544. σκληρύνω from σκληρός; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn: harden.
  4545. σκολιός from the base of σκέλος; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse: crooked, froward, untoward.
  4546. σκόλοψ perhaps from the base of σκέλος and ὀπτάνομαι; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability): thorn.
  4547. σκοπέω from σκοπός; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.
  4548. σκοπός from skeptomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to σκάπτω through the idea of concealment; compare σκέπασμα); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal: mark.
  4549. σκορπίζω apparently from the same as σκορπίος (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal: disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).
  4550. σκορπίος probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of σκοπός and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting): scorpion.
  4551. σκοτεινός from σκότος; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted: dark, full of darkness.
  4552. σκοτία from σκότος; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively): dark(-ness).
  4553. σκοτίζω from σκότος; to obscure (literally or figuratively): darken.
  4554. σκότος from the base of σκιά; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively): darkness.
  4555. σκοτόω from σκότος; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively): be full of darkness.
  4556. σκύβαλον neuter of a presumed derivative of εἰς and κύων and βάλλω; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure): dung.
  4557. Σκύθης probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage: Scythian.
  4558. σκυθρωπός from skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance: of a sad countenance.
  4559. σκύλλω apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass: trouble(self).
  4560. σκῦλον neuter from σκύλλω; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty: spoil.
  4561. σκωληκόβρωτος from σκώληξ and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots: eaten of worms.
  4562. σκώληξ of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm: worm.
  4563. σμαράγδινος from σμάραγδος; consisting of emerald: emerald.
  4564. σμάραγδος of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called: emerald.
  4565. σμύρνα apparently strengthened for μύρον; myrrh: myrrh.
  4566. Σμύρνα the same as σμύρνα; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor: Smyrna.
  4567. Σμυρναῖος from Σμύρνα; a Smyrnæan: in Smyrna.
  4568. σμυρνίζω from Σμύρνα; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic): mingle with myrrh.
  4569. Σόδομα plural of Hebrew origin (סְדֹם); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine: Sodom.
  4570. σοί dative case of σύ; to thee: thee, thine own, thou, thy.
  4571. Σολομών of Hebrew origin (שְׁלֹמֹה); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David: Solomon.
  4572. σορός probably akin to the base of σωρεύω; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier: bier.
  4573. σός from σύ; thine: thine (own), thy (friend).
  4574. σοῦ genitive case of σύ; of thee, thy: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.
  4575. σουδάριον of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse): handkerchief, napkin.
  4576. Σουσάννα of Hebrew origin (שׁוֹשָׁן feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess: Susanna.
  4577. σοφία from σοφός; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual): wisdom.
  4578. σοφίζω from σοφός; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error: cunningly devised, make wise.
  4579. σοφός akin to saphes (clear); wise (in a most general application): wise. Compare φρόνιμος.
  4580. Σπανία probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe: Spain.
  4581. σπαράσσω prolongation from spairo (to grasp; apparently strengthened from σπάω through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy: rend, tear.
  4582. σπαργανόω from sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of σπαράσσω meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom): wrap in swaddling clothes.
  4583. σπαταλάω from spatale (luxury); to be voluptuous: live in pleasure, be wanton.
  4584. σπάω a primary verb; to draw: draw (out).
  4585. σπεῖρα of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of αἱρέομαι in the sense of its cognate εἱλίσσω; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors): band.
  4586. σπείρω probably strengthened from σπάω (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively): sow(- er), receive seed.
  4587. σπεκουλάτωρ of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman): executioner.
  4588. σπένδω apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"): (be ready to) be offered.
  4589. σπέρμα from σπείρω; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting): issue, seed.
  4590. σπερμολόγος from σπέρμα and λέγω; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk): babbler.
  4591. σπεύδω probably strengthened from πούς; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly: (make, with) haste unto.
  4592. σπήλαιον neuter of a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort: cave, den.
  4593. σπιλάς of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea: spot (by confusion with spilos).
  4594. σπιλόω from σπίλος; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively): defile, spot.
  4595. σπίλος of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace: spot.
  4596. σπλαγχνίζομαι middle voice from σπλάγχνον; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity: have (be moved with) compassion.
  4597. σπλάγχνον probably strengthened from splen (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy: bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.
  4598. σπόγγος perhaps of foreign origin; a "sponge": spunge.
  4599. σποδός of uncertain derivation; ashes: ashes.
  4600. σπορά from σπείρω; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage: seed.
  4601. σπόριμος from σπόρος; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field: corn(-field).
  4602. σπόρος from σπείρω; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown): seed (X sown).
  4603. σπουδάζω from σπουδή; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.
  4604. σπουδαῖος from σπουδή; prompt, energetic, earnest: diligent.
  4605. σπουδαιότερον neuter of σπουδαιότερος as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly: very diligently.
  4606. σπουδαιότερος comparative of σπουδαῖος; more prompt, more earnest: more diligent (forward).
  4607. σπουδαιοτέρως adverb from σπουδαιότερος; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise: more carefully.
  4608. σπουδαίως adverb from σπουδαῖος; earnestly, promptly: diligently, instantly.
  4609. σπουδή from σπεύδω; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness: business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste.
  4610. σπυρίς from σπείρω (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle: basket.
  4611. στάδιον, or masculine (in plural) stadios from the base of ἵστημι (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course: furlong, race.
  4612. στάμνος from the base of ἵστημι (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank: pot.
  4613. στάσις from the base of ἵστημι; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy: dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.
  4614. στατήρ from the base of καύχησις; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin: piece of money.
  4615. σταυρός from the base of ἵστημι; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ: cross.
  4616. σταυρόω from σταυρός; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness: crucify.
  4617. σταφυλή probably from the base of στέφανος; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined): grapes.
  4618. στάχυς from the base of ἵστημι; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk): ear (of corn).
  4619. Στάχυς the same as στάχυς; Stachys, a Christian: Stachys.
  4620. στέγη strengthened from a primary tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof: roof.
  4621. στέγω from στέγη; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently): (for-)bear, suffer.
  4622. στείρος a contraction from στερεός (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile": barren.
  4623. στέλλω probably strengthened from the base of ἵστημι; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with): avoid, withdraw self.
  4624. στέμμα from the base of στέφανος; a wreath for show: garland.
  4625. στεναγμός from στενάζω; a sigh: groaning.
  4626. στενάζω from στενός; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly: with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.
  4627. στενός probably from the base of ἵστημι; narrow (from obstacles standing close about): strait.
  4628. στενοχωρέω from the same as στενοχωρία; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp: distress, straiten.
  4629. στενοχωρία from a compound of στενός and χώρα; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity: anguish, distress.
  4630. στερεός from ἵστημι; stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively): stedfast, strong, sure.
  4631. στερεόω from στερεός; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively): establish, receive strength, make strong.
  4632. στερέωμα from στερεόω; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability): stedfastness.
  4633. Στεφανᾶς probably contraction for stephanotos (crowned; from στεφανόω); Stephanas, a Christian: Stephanas.
  4634. στέφανος from an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, διάδημα), literally or figuratively: crown.
  4635. Στέφανος the same as στέφανος; Stephanus, a Christian: Stephen.
  4636. στεφανόω from στέφανος; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively): crown.
  4637. στῆθος from ἵστημι (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest: breast.
  4638. στήκω from the perfect tense of ἵστημι; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere: stand (fast).
  4639. στηριγμός from στηρίζω; stability (figuratively): stedfastness.
  4640. στηρίζω from a presumed derivative of ἵστημι (like στερεός); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm: fix, (e-)stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.
  4641. στίγμα from a primary stizo (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service: mark.
  4642. στιγμή feminine of στίγμα; a point of time, i.e. an instant: moment.
  4643. στίλβω apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. flash intensely: shining.
  4644. στοά probably from ἵστημι; a colonnade or interior piazza: porch.
  4645. στοιβάς from a primary steibo (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed: branch.
  4646. στοιχεῖον neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of στοιχέω; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively): element, principle, rudiment.
  4647. στοιχέω from a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety: walk (orderly).
  4648. στολή from στέλλω; equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity): long clothing (garment), (long) robe.
  4649. στόμα probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of τομώτερος; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon): edge, face, mouth.
  4650. στόμαχος from στόμα; an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach": stomach.
  4651. στρατεία from στρατεύομαι; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger): warfare.
  4652. στράτευμα from στρατεύομαι; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic): army, soldier, man of war.
  4653. στρατεύομαι middle voice from the base of στρατιά; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations: soldier, (go to) war(-fare).
  4654. στρατηγός from the base of στρατιά and ἄγω or ἡγέομαι; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens: captain, magistrate.
  4655. στρατιά feminine of a derivative of stratos (an army; from the base of στρώννυμι, as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries: host.
  4656. στρατιώτης from a presumed derivative of the same as στρατιά; a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively): soldier.
  4657. στρατολογέω from a compound of the base of στρατιά and λέγω (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army: choose to be a soldier.
  4658. στρατοπεδάρχης from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω; a ruler of an army, i.e. præfect: captain of the guard.
  4659. στρατόπεδον from the base of στρατιά and the same as πεδινός; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops: army.
  4660. στρεβλόω from a derivative of στρέφω; to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert: wrest.
  4661. στρέφω strengthened from the base of τροπή; to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively): convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).
  4662. στρηνιάω from a presumed derivative of στρῆνος; to be luxurious: live deliciously.
  4663. στρῆνος akin to στερεός; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness): delicacy.
  4664. στρουθίον diminutive of strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow: sparrow.
  4665. στρώννυμι, or simpler stronnuo, prolongation from a still simpler stroo, (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to στερεός through the idea of positing); to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch): make bed, furnish, spread, strew.
  4666. στυγνητός from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate); hated, i.e. odious: hateful.
  4667. στυγνάζω from the same as στυγνητός; to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech): lower, be sad.
  4668. στῦλος from stuo (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of ἵστημι); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support: pillar.
  4669. Στωϊκός from στοά; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy: Stoick.
  4670. σύ the personal pronoun of the second person singular; thou: thou. See also σέ, σοί, σοῦ; and for the plural ὑμᾶς, ὑμεῖς, ὑμῖν, ὑμῶν.
  4671. συγγένεια from συγγενής; relationship, i.e. (concretely) relatives: kindred.
  4672. συγγενής from σύν and γένος; a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman: cousin, kin(-sfolk, -sman).
  4673. συγγνώμη from a compound of σύν and γινώσκω; fellow knowledge, i.e. concession: permission.
  4674. συγκάθημαι from σύν and κάθημαι; to seat oneself in company with: sit with.
  4675. συγκαθίζω from σύν and καθίζω; to give (or take) a seat in company with: (make) sit (down) together.
  4676. συγκακοπαθέω from σύν and κακοπαθέω; to suffer hardship in company with: be partaker of afflictions.
  4677. συγκακουχέω from σύν and κακουχέω; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together: suffer affliction with.
  4678. συγκαλέω from σύν and καλέω; to convoke: call together.
  4679. συγκαλύπτω from σύν and καλύπτω; to conceal altogether: cover.
  4680. συγκάμπτω from σύν and κάμπτω; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict: bow down.
  4681. συγκαταβαίνω from σύν and καταβαίνω; to descend in company with: go down with.
  4682. συγκατάθεσις from συγκατατίθεμαι; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with: agreement.
  4683. συγκατατίθεμαι middle from σύν and κατατίθημι; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with: consent.
  4684. συγκαταψηφίζω from σύν and a compound of κατά and ψηφίζω; to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among: number with.
  4685. συγκεράννυμι from σύν and κεράννυμι; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate: mix with, temper together.
  4686. συγκινέω from σπαράσσω and κινέω; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition): stir up.
  4687. συγκλείω from σύν and κλείω; to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to: conclude, inclose, shut up.
  4688. συγκληρονόμος from σύν and κληρονόμος; a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common: fellow (joint)-heir, heir together, heir with.
  4689. συγκοινωνέω from σύν and κοινωνέω; to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.
  4690. συγκοινωνός from σύν and κοινωνός; a co-participant: companion, partake(-r, -r with).
  4691. συγκομίζω from σύν and κομίζω; to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others: carry.
  4692. συγκρίνω from σύν and κρίνω; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance): compare among (with).
  4693. συγκύπτω from σύν and κύπτω; to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by: bow together.
  4694. συγκυρία from a comparative of σύν and kureo (to light or happen; from the base of κύριος); concurrence, i.e. accident: chance.
  4695. συγχαίρω from σύν and χαίρω; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate: rejoice in (with).
  4696. συγχέω or sugchuno from σύν and cheo (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind): confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.
