  4697. συγχράομαι from σύν and χράομαι; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common: have dealings with.
  4698. σύγχυσις from συγχέω; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance: confusion.
  4699. συζάω from σύν and ζάω; to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively): live with.
  4700. συζεύγνυμι from σύν and the base of ζεῦγος; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage): join together.
  4701. συζητέω from σύν and ζητέω; to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil: dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).
  4702. συζήτησις from συζητέω; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion: disputation(-ting), reasoning.
  4703. συζητητής from συζητέω; a disputant, i.e. sophist: disputer.
  4704. σύζυγος from συζεύγνυμι; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian: yokefellow.
  4705. συζωοποιέω from σύν and ζωοποιέω; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively): quicken together with.
  4706. συκάμινος of Hebrew origin (שִׁקְמִים) in imitation of συκομωραία; a sycamore-fig tree: sycamine tree.
  4707. συκῆ from σῦκον; a fig-tree: fig tree.
  4708. συκομωραία from σῦκον and moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree: sycamore tree. Compare συκάμινος.
  4709. σῦκον apparently a primary word; a fig: fig.
  4710. συκοφαντέω from a compound of σῦκον and a derivative of φαίνω; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort): accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
  4711. συλαγωγέω from the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce: spoil.
  4712. συλάω from a derivative of sullo (to strip; probably akin to αἱρέομαι; compare σκῦλον); to despoil: rob.
  4713. συλλαλέω from σύν and λαλέω; to talk together, i.e. converse: commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.
  4714. συλλαμβάνω from σύν and λαμβάνω; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid: catch, conceive, help, take.
  4715. συλλέγω from σύν and λέγω in its original sense; to collect: gather (together, up).
  4716. συλλογίζομαι from σύν and λογίζομαι; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate: reason with.
  4717. συλλυπέω from σύν and λυπέω; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone: be grieved.
  4718. συμβαίνω from σύν and the base of βάσις; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place): be(-fall), happen (unto).
  4719. συμβάλλω from σύν and βάλλω; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.
  4720. συμβασιλεύω from σύν and βασιλεύω; to be co-regent (figuratively): reign with.
  4721. συμβιβάζω from σύν and bibazo (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of βάσις); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
  4722. συμβουλεύω from σύν and βουλεύω; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine: consult, (give, take) counsel (together).
  4723. συμβούλιον neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court: consultation, counsel, council.
  4724. σύμβουλος from σύν and βουλή; a consultor, i.e. adviser: counsellor.
  4725. Συμεών from the same as Σίμων; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites: Simeon, Simon.
  4726. συμμαθητής from a compound of σύν and μανθάνω; a co-learner (of Christianity): fellow disciple.
  4727. συμμαρτυρέω from σύν and μαρτυρέω; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence: testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).
  4728. συμμερίζομαι middle voice from σύν and μερίζω; to share jointly, i.e. participate in: be partaker with.
  4729. συμμέτοχος from σύν and μέτοχος; a co-participant: partaker.
  4730. συμμιμητής from a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary: follower together.
  4731. σύμμορφος from σύν and μορφή; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar: conformed to, fashioned like unto.
  4732. συμμορφόω from σύμμορφος; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate: make conformable unto.
  4733. συμπαθέω from συμπαθής; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
  4734. συμπαθής from συμπάσχω; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative: having compassion one of another.
  4735. συμπαραγίνομαι from σύν and παραγίνομαι; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid: come together, stand with.
  4736. συμπαρακαλέω from σύν and παρακαλέω; to console jointly: comfort together.
  4737. συμπαραλαμβάνω from σύν and παραλαμβάνω; to take along in company: take with.
  4738. συμπαραμένω from σύν and παραμένω; to remain in company, i.e. still live: continue with.
  4739. συμπάρειμι from σύν and πάρειμι; to be at hand together, i.e. now present: be here present with.
  4740. συμπάσχω from σύν and πάσχω (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize"): suffer with.
  4741. συμπέμπω from σύν and πέμπω; to despatch in company: send with.
  4742. συμπεριλαμβάνω from σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one: embrace.
  4743. συμπίνω from σύν and πίνω; to partake a beverage in company: drink with.
  4744. συμπληρόω from σύν and πληρόω; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete): (fully) come, fill up.
  4745. συμπνίγω from σύν and πνίγω; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd: choke, throng.
  4746. συμπολίτης from σύν and πολίτης; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian): fellow- citizen.
  4747. συμπορεύομαι from σύν and πορεύομαι; to journey together; by implication, to assemble: go with, resort.
  4748. συμπόσιον neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests: company.
  4749. συμπρεσβύτερος from σύν and πρεσβύτερος; a co-presbyter: presbyter, also an elder.
  4750. συμφέρω from σύν and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).
  4751. σύμφημι from σύν and φημί; to say jointly, i.e. assent to: consent unto.
  4752. συμφυλέτης from σύν and a derivative of φυλή; a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country: countryman.
  4753. σύμφυτος from σύν and a derivative of φύω; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to: planted together.
  4754. συμφύω from σύν and φύω; passive, to grow jointly: spring up with.
  4755. συμφωνέω from σύμφωνος; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact): agree (together, with).
  4756. συμφώνησις from συμφωνέω; accordance: concord.
  4757. συμφωνία from σύμφωνος; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note): music.
  4758. σύμφωνος from σύν and φωνή; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement): consent.
  4759. συμψηφίζω from σύν and ψηφίζω; to compute jointly: reckon.
  4760. σύμψυχος from σύν and ψυχή; co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment: like-minded.
  4761. σύν a primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than μετά or παρά), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.: beside, with. In composition it has similar applications, including completeness.
  4762. συνάγω from σύν and ἄγω; to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably): + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.
  4763. συναγωγή from (the reduplicated form of) συνάγω; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church: assembly, congregation, synagogue.
  4764. συναγωνίζομαι from σύν and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant): strive together with.
  4765. συναθλέω from σύν and ἀθλέω; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly: labour with, strive together for.
  4766. συναθροίζω from σύν and athroizo (to hoard); to convene: call (gather) together.
  4767. συναίρω from σύν and αἴρω; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account): reckon, take.
  4768. συναιχμάλωτος from σύν and αἰχμάλωτος; a co-captive: fellowprisoner.
  4769. συνακολουθέω from σύν and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany: follow.
  4770. συναλίζω from σύν and halizo (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene: assemble together.
  4771. συναναβαίνω from σύν and ἀναβαίνω; to ascend in company with: come up with.
  4772. συνανάκειμαι from σύν and ἀνακεῖμαι; to recline in company with (at a meal): sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).
  4773. συναναμίγνυμι from σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with: (have, keep) company (with).
  4774. συναναπαύομαι middle from σύν and ἀναπαύω; to recruit oneself in company with: refresh with.
  4775. συναντάω from σύν and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet with; figuratively, to occur: befall, meet.
  4776. συνάντησις from συναντάω; a meeting with: meet.
  4777. συναντιλαμβάνομαι from σύν and ἀντιλαμβάνομαι; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist): help.
  4778. συναπάγω from σύν and ἀπάγω; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield): carry (lead) away with, condescend.
  4779. συναποθνήσκω from σύν and ἀποθνήσκω; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to: be dead (die) with.
  4780. συναπόλλυμι from σύν and ἀπόλλυμι; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with: perish with.
  4781. συναποστέλλω from σύν and ἀποστέλλω; to despatch (on an errand) in company with: send with.
  4782. συναρμολογέω from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ἁρμός and λέγω (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly: be fitly framed (joined) together.
  4783. συναρπάζω from σύν and ἁρπάζω; to snatch together, i.e. seize: catch.
  4784. συναυξάνω from σύν and αὐξάνω; to increase (grow up) together: grow together.
  4785. σύνδεσμος from σύν and δεσμόν; a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control: band, bond.
  4786. συνδέω from σύν and δέω; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively): be bound with.
  4787. συνδοξάζω from σύν and δοξάζω; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with: glorify together.
  4788. σύνδουλος from σύν and δοῦλος; a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine): fellowservant.
  4789. συνδρομή from (the alternate of) συντρέχω; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse: run together.
  4790. συνεγείρω from σύν and ἐγείρω; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to: raise up together, rise with.
  4791. συνέδριον neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of σύν and the base of ἑδραῖος; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal: council.
  4792. συνείδησις from a prolonged form of συνείδω; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness: conscience.
  4793. συνείδω from σύν and εἴδω; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of: consider, know, be privy, be ware of.
  4794. σύνειμι from σύν and εἰμί (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. present at the time: be with.
  4795. σύνειμι from σύν and eimi (to go); to assemble: gather together.
  4796. συνεισέρχομαι from σύν and εἰσέρχομαι; to enter in company with: go in with, go with into.
  4797. συνέκδημος from σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller: companion in travel, travel with.
  4798. συνεκλεκτός from a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι; chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian): elected together with.
  4799. συνελαύνω from σύν and ἐλαύνω; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation): + set at one again.
  4800. συνεπιμαρτυρέω from σύν and ἐπιμαρτυρέω; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence: also bear witness.
  4801. συνέπομαι middle voice from σύν and a primary hepo (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with: accompany.
  4802. συνεργέω from συνεργός; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate: help (work) with, work(-er) together.
  4803. συνεργός from a presumed compound of σύν and the base of ἔργον; a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.
  4804. συνέρχομαι from σύν and ἔρχομαι; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally): accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.
  4805. συνεσθίω from σύν and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to take food in company with: eat with.
  4806. σύνεσις from συνίημι; a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect: knowledge, understanding.
  4807. συνετός from συνίημι; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious: prudent. Compare φρόνιμος.
  4808. συνευδοκέω from σύν and εὐδοκέω; to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.
  4809. συνευωχέω from σύν and a derivative of a presumed compound of εὖ and a derivative of ἔχω (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together: feast with.
  4810. συνεφίστημι from σύν and ἐφίστημι; to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly: rise up together.
  4811. συνέχω from σύν and ἔχω; to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy: constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.
  4812. συνήδομαι middle voice from σύν and the base of ἡδονή; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning: delight.
  4813. συνήθεια from a compound of σύν and ἦθος; mutual habituation, i.e. usage: custom.
  4814. συνηλικιώτης from σύν and a derivative of ἡλικία; a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years: equal.
  4815. συνθάπτω from σύν and θάπτω; to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin): bury with.
  4816. συνθλάω from σύν and thlao (to crush); to dash together, i.e. shatter: break.
  4817. συνθλίβω from σύν and θλίβω; to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides: throng.
  4818. συνθρύπτω from σύν and thrupto (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit: break.
  4819. συνίημι from σύν and hiemi (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously: consider, understand, be wise.
  4820. συνιστάω, or (strengthened) sunistano, or sunistemi from σύν and ἵστημι (including its collateral forms); to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute: approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with).
  4821. συνοδεύω from σύν and ὁδεύω; to travel in company with: journey with.
  4822. συνοδία from a compound of σύν and ὁδός ("synod"); companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan: company.
  4823. συνοικέω from σύν and οἰκέω; to reside together (as a family): dwell together.
  4824. συνοικοδομέω from σύν and οἰκοδομέω; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively): build together.
  4825. συνομιλέω from σύν and ὁμιλέω; to converse mutually: talk with.
  4826. συνομορέω from σύν and a derivative of a compound of the base of ὁμοῦ and the base of ὅριον; to border together, i.e. adjoin: join hard.
  4827. συνοχή from συνέχω; restraint, i.e. (figuratively) anxiety: anguish, distress.
  4828. συντάσσω from σύν and τάσσω; to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct: appoint.
  4829. συντέλεια from συντελέω; entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation): end.
  4830. συντελέω from σύν and τελέω; to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively): end, finish, fulfil, make.
  4831. συντέμνω from σύν and the base of τομώτερος; to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily): (cut) short.
  4832. συντηρέω from σύν and τηρέω; to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey): keep, observe, preserve.
  4833. συντίθεμαι middle voice from σύν and τίθημι; to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur: agree, assent, covenant.
  4834. συντόμως adverb from a derivative of συντέμνω; concisely (briefly): a few words.
  4835. συντρέχω from σύν and τρέχω (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively): run (together, with).
  4836. συντρίβω from σύν and the base of τρίβος; to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively): break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.
  4837. σύντριμμα from συντρίβω; concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin: destruction.
  4838. σύντροφος from σύν and τροφός (in a passive sense); a fellow-nursling, i.e. comrade: brought up with.
  4839. συντυγχάνω from σύν and τυγχάνω; to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach): come at.
  4840. Συντύχη from συντυγχάνω; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female: Syntyche.
  4841. συνυποκρίνομαι from σύν and ὑποκρίνομαι; to act hypocritically in concert with: dissemble with.
  4842. συνυπουργέω from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ὑπό and the base of ἔργον; to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist: help together.
  4843. συνωδίνω from σύν and ὠδίνω; to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering): travail in pain together.
  4844. συνωμοσία from a compound of σύν and ὀμνύω; a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot: comspiracy.
  4845. Συράκουσαι plural of uncertain derivation; Syracuse, the capital of Sicily: Syracuse.
  4846. Συρία probably of Hebrew origin (צֹר); Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia: Syria.
  4847. Σύρος from the same as Συρία; a Syran (i.e. probably Tyrian), a native of Syria: Syrian.
  4848. Συροφοίνισσα feminine of a compound of Σύρος and the same as Φοινίκη; a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria: Syrophenician.
  4849. σύρτις from σύρω; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa: quicksands.
  4850. σύρω probably akin to αἱρέομαι; to trail: drag, draw, hale.
  4851. συσπαράσσω from σύν and σπαράσσω; to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently: throw down.
  4852. σύσσημον neuter of a compound of σύν and the base of σημαίνω; a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal: token.
  4853. σύσσωμος from σύν and σῶμα; of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community: of the same body.
  4854. συστασιαστής from a compound of σύν and a derivative of στάσις; a fellow-insurgent: make insurrection with.
  4855. συστατικός from a derivative of συνιστάω; introductory, i.e. recommendatory: of commendation.
  4856. συσταυρόω from σύν and σταυρόω; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively): crucify with.
  4857. συστέλλω from σύν and στέλλω; to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval): short, wind up.
  4858. συστενάζω from σύν and στενάζω; to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity: groan together.
  4859. συστοιχέω from σύν and στοιχέω; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to: answer to.
  4860. συστρατιώτης from σύν and στρατιώτης; a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil: fellowsoldier.
  4861. συστρέφω from σύν and στρέφω; to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd): gather.
  4862. συστροφή from συστρέφω; a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd: + band together, concourse.
  4863. συσχηματίζω from σύν and a derivative of σχῆμα; to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively): conform to, fashion self according to.
  4864. Συχάρ of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine: Sychar.
  4865. Συχέμ of Hebrew origin (שְׁכֶם); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine: Sychem.
  4866. σφαγή from σφάζω; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)): slaughter.
  4867. σφάγιον neuter of a derivative of σφαγή; a victim (in sacrifice): slain beast.
  4868. σφάζω a primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently): kill, slay, wound.
  4869. σφόδρα neuter plural of sphodros (violent; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. in a high degree, much: exceeding(-ly), greatly, sore, very.
  4870. σφοδρῶς adverb from the same as σφόδρα; very much: exceedingly.
  4871. σφραγίζω from σφραγίς; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest: (set a, set to) seal up, stop.
  4872. σφραγίς probably strengthened from φράσσω; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively: seal.
  4873. σφυρόν neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as sphaira (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine sphura, a hammer); the ankle (as globular): ancle bone.
  4874. σχεδόν neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω as adverb; nigh, i.e. nearly: almost.
  4875. σχῆμα from the alternate of ἔχω; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition: fashion.
  4876. σχίζω apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively): break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.
  4877. σχίσμα from σχίζω; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively: division, rent, schism.
  4878. σχοινίον diminutive of schoinos (a rush or flag-plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally): small cord, rope.
  4879. σχολάζω from σχολή; to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house): empty, give self.
  4880. σχολή probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω; properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment): school.
  4881. σώζω from a primary sos (contraction for obsolete saos, "safe"); to save, i.e. deliver or protect (literally or figuratively): heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.
  4882. σῶμα from σώζω; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively: bodily, body, slave.
  4883. σωματικός from σῶμα; corporeal or physical: bodily.
  4884. σωματικῶς adverb from σωματικός; corporeally or physically: bodily.
  4885. Σώπατρος from the base of σώζω and πατήρ; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian: Sopater. Compare Σωσίπατρος.
  4886. σωρεύω from another form of σορός; to pile up (literally or figuratively): heap, load.
  4887. Σωσθένης from the base of σώζω and that of σθενόω; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian: Sosthenes.
  4888. Σωσίπατρος prolongation for Σώπατρος; Sosipatrus, a Christian: Sosipater.
  4889. σωτήρ from σώζω; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ: saviour.
  4890. σωτηρία feminine of a derivative of σωτήρ as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally): deliver, health, salvation, save, saving.
  4891. σωτήριον neuter of the same as σωτηρία as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence: salvation.
  4892. σωφρονέω from σώφρων; to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate: be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.
  4893. σωφρονίζω from σώφρων; to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct: teach to be sober.
  4894. σωφρονισμός from σωφρονίζω; discipline, i.e. self-control: sound mind.
  4895. σωφρόνως adverb from σώφρων; with sound mind, i.e. moderately: soberly.
  4896. σωφροσύνη from σώφρων; soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control: soberness, sobriety.
  4897. σώφρων from the base of σώζω and that of φρήν; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion): discreet, sober, temperate.
  4898. Ταβέρναι plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ: taverns.
  4899. Ταβιθά of Chaldee origin (compare צְבִיָּה); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female: Tabitha.
  4900. τάγμα from τάσσω; something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession: order.
  4901. τακτός from τάσσω; arranged, i.e. appointed or stated: set.
  4902. ταλαιπωρέω from ταλαίπωρος; to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery: be afflicted.
  4903. ταλαιπωρία from ταλαίπωρος; wretchedness, i.e. calamity: misery.
  4904. ταλαίπωρος from the base of τάλαντον and a derivative of the base of πεῖρα; enduring trial, i.e. miserable: wretched.
  4905. ταλαντιαῖος from τάλαντον; talent-like in weight: weight of a talent.
  4906. τάλαντον neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of tlao (to bear; equivalent to φέρω); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent": talent.
  4907. ταλιθά of Chaldee origin (compare טָלֶה); the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden): talitha.
  4908. ταμεῖον neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of tamias (a dispenser or distributor; akin to temno, to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. a chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement): secret chamber, closet, storehouse.
  4909. τάξις from τάσσω; regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity: order.
  4910. ταπεινός of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition): base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly.
  4911. ταπεινοφροσύνη from a compound of ταπεινός and the base of φρήν; humiliation of mind, i.e. modesty: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind).
  4912. ταπεινόω from ταπεινός; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart): abase, bring low, humble (self).
  4913. ταπείνωσις from ταπεινόω; depression (in rank or feeling): humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile.
  4914. ταράσσω of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate (roil water): trouble.
  4915. ταραχή feminine from ταράσσω; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition: trouble(-ing).
  4916. τάραχος masculine from ταράσσω; a disturbance, i.e. (popular) tumult: stir.
  4917. Ταρσεύς from Ταρσός; a Tarsean, i.e. native of Tarsus: of Tarsus.
  4918. Ταρσός perhaps the same as tarsos (a flat basket); Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor: Tarsus.
  4919. ταρταρόω from Tartaros (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment: cast down to hell.
  4920. τάσσω a prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot): addict, appoint, determine, ordain, set.
  4921. ταῦρος apparently a primary word (compare תּוֹרִין, "steer"); a bullock: bull, ox.
  4922. ταῦτα nominative or accusative case neuter plural of οὗτος; these things: + afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus.
  4923. ταὐτά neuter plural of ὁ and αὐτός as adverb; in the same way: even thus, (manner) like, so.
  4924. ταύταις, and tautas dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of οὗτος; (to or with or by, etc.) these: hence, that, then, these, those.
  4925. ταύτῃ, and tauten, and tautes dative case, accusative case and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of οὗτος; (towards or of) this: her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same).
  4926. ταφή feminine from θάπτω; burial (the act): X bury.
  4927. τάφος masculine from θάπτω; a grave (the place of interment): sepulchre, tomb.
  4928. τάχα as if neuter plural of ταχύς (adverbially); shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly: peradventure(-haps).
  4929. ταχέως adverb from ταχύς; briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly: hastily, quickly, shortly, soon, suddenly.
  4930. ταχινός from τάχος; curt, i.e. impending: shortly, swift.
  4931. τάχιον neuter singular of the comparative of ταχύς (as adverb); more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily: out (run), quickly, shortly, sooner.
  4932. τάχιστα neuter plural of the superlative of ταχύς (as adverb); most quickly, i.e. (with ὡς prefixed) as soon as possible: + with all speed.
  4933. τάχος from the same as ταχύς; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with ἐν prefixed) in haste: + quickly, + shortly, + speedily.
  4934. ταχύ neuter singular of ταχύς (as adverb); shortly, i.e. without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily: lightly, quickly.
  4935. ταχύς of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready: swift.
  4936. τέ a primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly, as correlation of καί): also, and, both, even, then, whether. Often used in composition, usually as the latter participle.
  4937. τεῖχος akin to the base of τίκτω; a wall (as formative of a house): wall.
  4938. τεκμήριον neuter of a presumed derivative of tekmar (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), i.e. criterion of certainty: infallible proof.
  4939. τεκνίον diminutive of τέκνον; an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts): little children.
  4940. τεκνογονέω from a compound of τέκνον and the base of γίνομαι; to be a child-bearer, i.e. parent (mother): bear children.
  4941. τεκνογονία from the same as τεκνογονέω; childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties): childbearing.
  4942. τέκνον from the base of τιμωρία; a child (as produced): child, daughter, son.
  4943. τεκνοτροφέω from a compound of τέκνον and τρέφω; to be a childrearer, i.e. fulfil the duties of a female parent: bring up children.
  4944. τέκτων from the base of τιμωρία; an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood: carpenter.
  4945. τέλειος from τέλος; complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with ὁ) completeness: of full age, man, perfect.
  4946. τελειότης from τέλειος; (the state) completeness (mentally or morally): perfection(-ness).
  4947. τελειόω from τέλειος; to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character): consecrate, finish, fulfil, make) perfect.
  4948. τελείως adverb from τέλειος; completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering: to the end.
  4949. τελείωσις from φυσιόω; (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution: perfection, performance.
  4950. τελειωτής from τελειόω; a completer, i.e. consummater: finisher.
  4951. τελεσφορέω from a compound of τέλος and φέρω; to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. to ripen fruit (figuratively): bring fruit to perfection.
  4952. τελευτάω from a presumed derivative of τελέω; to finish life (by implication, of βίος), i.e. expire (demise): be dead, decease, die.
  4953. τελευτή from τελευτάω; decease: death.
  4954. τελέω from τέλος; to end, i.e. complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt): accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform.
  4955. τέλος from a primary tello (to set out for a definite point or goal); properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic), purpose); specially, an impost or levy (as paid): + continual, custom, end(-ing), finally, uttermost. Compare φόρος.
  4956. τελώνης from τέλος and ὠνέομαι; a tax-farmer, i.e. collector of public revenue: publican.
  4957. τελώνιον neuter of a presumed derivative of τελώνης; a tax-gatherer's place of business: receipt of custom.
  4958. τέρας of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen: wonder.
  4959. Τέρτιος of Latin origin; third; Tertius, a Christian: Tertius.
  4960. Τέρτυλλος of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman: Tertullus.
  4961. τεσσαράκοντα the decade of τέσσαρες; forty: forty.
  4962. τεσσαρακονταετής from τεσσαράκοντα and ἔτος; of forty years of age: (+ full, of) forty years (old).
  4963. τέσσαρες, or neuter tessara a plural number; four: four.
  4964. τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος from τέσσαρες and καί and δέκατος; fourteenth: fourteenth.
  4965. τεταρταῖος from τέσσαρες; pertaining to the fourth day: four days.
  4966. τέταρτος ordinal from τέσσαρες; fourth: four(-th).
  4967. τετράγωνος from τέσσαρες and γωνία; four-cornered, i.e. square: foursquare.
  4968. τετράδιον neuter of a presumed derivative of tetras (a tetrad; from τέσσαρες); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers: quaternion.
  4969. τετρακισχίλιοι from the multiplicative adverb of τέσσαρες and χίλιοι; four times a thousand: four thousand.
  4970. τετρακόσιοι, or neuter tetrakosia plural from τέσσαρες and ἑκατόν; four hundred: four hundred.
  4971. τετράμηνον neuter of a compound of τέσσαρες and μήν; a four months' space: four months.
  4972. τετραπλόος from τέσσαρες and a derivative of the base of πλεῖστος; quadruple: fourfold.
  4973. τετράπους from τέσσαρες and πούς; a quadruped: fourfooted beast.
  4974. τετραρχέω from τετράρχης; to be a tetrarch: (be) tetrarch.
  4975. τετράρχης from τέσσαρες and ἄρχω; the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch"): tetrarch.
  4976. τεφρόω from tephra (ashes); to incinerate, i.e. consume: turn to ashes.
  4977. τέχνη from the base of τίκτω; art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill: art, craft, occupation.
  4978. τεχνίτης from τέχνη; an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator): builder, craftsman.
  4979. τήκω apparently a primary verb; to liquefy: melt.
  4980. τηλαυγῶς adverb from a compound of a derivative of τέλος and αὐγή; in a far-shining manner, i.e. plainly: clearly.
  4981. τηλικοῦτος, or feminine telikaute from a compound of ὁ with ἡλίκος and οὗτος; such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast: so great, so mighty.
  4982. τηρέω from teros (a watch; perhaps akin to θεωρέω); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from φυλάσσω, which is properly to prevent escaping; and from κουστωδία, which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. to note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried): hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch.
  4983. τήρησις from τηρέω; a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison: hold.
  4984. Τιβεριάς from Τιβέριος; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine: Tiberias.
  4985. Τιβέριος of Latin origin; probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor: Tiberius.
  4986. τίθημι, a prolonged form of a primary theo (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from ἵστημι, which properly denotes an upright and active position, while κεῖμαι is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate): + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.
  4987. τίκτω a strengthened form of a primary teko tek'-o (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively: bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.
  4988. τίλλω perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, and thus to σύρω; to pull off: pluck.
  4989. Τιμαῖος probably of Chaldee origin (compare טָמֵא); Timæus (i.e. Timay), an Israelite: Timæus.
  4990. τιμάω from τίμιος; to prize, i.e. fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere: honour, value.
  4991. τιμή from τίνω; a value, i.e. money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself: honour, precious, price, some.
  4992. τίμιος, including the comparative timioteros, and the superlative timiotatos from τιμή; valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved: dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.
  4993. τιμιότης from τίμιος; expensiveness, i.e. (by implication) magnificence: costliness.
  4994. Τιμόθεος from τιμή and θεός; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian: Timotheus, Timothy.
  4995. Τίμων from τιμή; valuable; Timon, a Christian: Timon.
  4996. τιμωρέω from a comparative of τιμή and ouros (a guard); properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. to avenge (inflict a penalty): punish.
  4997. τιμωρία from τιμωρέω; vindication, i.e. (by implication) a penalty: punishment.
  4998. τίνω, strengthened for a primary tio (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses) to pay a price, i.e. as a penalty: be punished with.
  4999. τὶς an enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object: a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever).
  5000. τίς probably emphatic of τὶς; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions): every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.
  5001. τίτλος of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard): title.
  5002. Τίτος of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian: Titus.
  5003. τοί probably for the dative case of ὁ; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth: (used only with other particles in the comparative, as kaitoige, mentoi, toigaroun, toinun, etc.)
  5004. τοιγαροῦν from τοί and γάρ and οὖν; truly for then, i.e. consequently: there-(where-)fore.
  5005. τοίνυν from τοί and νῦν; truly now, i.e. accordingly: then, therefore.
  5006. τοιόσδε (including the other inflections); from a derivative of τοί and δέ; such-like then, i.e. so great: such.
  5007. τοιοῦτος (including the other inflections); from τοί and οὗτος; truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality): like, such (an one).
  5008. τοῖχος another form of τεῖχος; a wall: wall.
  5009. τόκος from the base of τίκτω; interest on money loaned (as a produce): usury.
  5010. τολμάω from tolma (boldness; probably itself from the base of τέλος through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while θαῤῥέω is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous: be bold, boldly, dare, durst.
  5011. τολμηρότερον neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of τολμάω (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise: the more boldly.
  5012. τολμητής from τολμάω; a daring (audacious) man: presumptuous.
  5013. τομώτερος comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than κόπτω, as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen: sharper.
  5014. τόξον from the base of τίκτω; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric): bow.
  5015. τοπάζιον neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite: topaz.
  5016. τόπος apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas χώρα is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.
  5017. τοσοῦτος from tosos (so much; apparently from ὁ and ὅς) and οὗτος (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space): as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.
  5018. τότε from (the neuter of) ὁ and ὅτε; the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution): that time, then.
  5019. τοῦ properly, the genitive case of ὁ; sometimes used for τούτου; of this person: his.
  5020. τοὐναντίον contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ἐναντίον; on the contrary: contrariwise.
  5021. τοὔνομα contraction for the neuter of ὁ and ὄνομα; the name (is): named.
  5022. τουτέστι contraction for τοῦτο and ἐστί; that is: that is (to say).
  5023. τοῦτο neuter singular nominative or accusative case of οὗτος; that thing: here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).
  5024. τούτοις dative case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things): such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those.
  5025. τοῦτον accusative case singular masculine of οὗτος; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition): him, the same, that, this.
  5026. τούτου genitive case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing): here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus.
  5027. τούτους accusative case plural masculine of οὗτος; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition): such, them, these, this.
  5028. τούτῳ dative case singular masculine or neuter of οὗτος; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing): here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this.
  5029. τούτων genitive case plural masculine or neuter of οὗτος; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things): such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.
  5030. τράγος from the base of τρώγω; a he-goat (as a gnawer): goat.
  5031. τράπεζα probably contracted from τέσσαρες and πεζῇ; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest): bank, meat, table.
  5032. τραπεζίτης from τράπεζα; a money-broker or banker: exchanger.
  5033. τραῦμα from the base of titrosko (to wound; akin to the base of θραύω, τρίβος, τρίζω, etc.); a wound: wound.
  5034. τραυματίζω from τραῦμα; to inflict a wound: wound.
  5035. τραχηλίζω from τράχηλος; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare): opened.
  5036. τράχηλος probably from τρέχω (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life: neck.
  5037. τραχύς perhaps strengthened from the base of ῥήγνυμι (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy): rock, rough.
  5038. Τραχωνῖτις from a derivative of τραχύς; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria: Trachonitis.
  5039. τρεῖς, or neuter tria a primary (plural) number; "three": three.
  5040. τρέμω strengthened from a primary treo (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear: be afraid, trembling.
  5041. τρέφω a primary verb (properly, threpho; but perhaps strengthened from the base of τροπή through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear): bring up, feed, nourish.
  5042. τρέχω apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho; compare θρίξ); which uses dremo drem'-o (the base of δρόμος) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively): have course, run.
  5043. τριάκοντα the decade of τρεῖς; thirty: thirty.
  5044. τριακόσιοι plural from τρεῖς and ἑκατόν; three hundred: three hundred.
  5045. τρίβολος from τρεῖς and βέλος; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop): brier, thistle.
  5046. τρίβος from tribo (to "rub"; akin to teiro, truo, and the base of τράγος, τραῦμα); a rut or worn track: path.
  5047. τριετία from a compound of τρεῖς and ἔτος; a three years' period (triennium): space of three years.
  5048. τρίζω apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy): gnash.
  5049. τρίμηνον neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and μήν as noun; a three months' space: three months.
  5050. τρίς adverb from τρεῖς; three times: three times, thrice.
  5051. τρίστεγον neuter of a compound of τρεῖς and στέγη as noun; a third roof (story): third loft.
  5052. τρισχίλιοι from τρίς and χίλιοι; three times a thousand: three thousand.
  5053. τρίτος ordinal from τρεῖς; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly: third(-ly).
  5054. τρίχινος from θρίξ; hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair): of hair.
  5055. τρόμος from τρέμω; a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear: + tremble(-ing).
  5056. τροπή from an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. revolution (figuratively, variation): turning.
  5057. τρόπος from the same as τροπή; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character: (even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.
  5058. τροποφορέω from τρόπος and φορέω; to endure one's habits: suffer the manners.
  5059. τροφή from τρέφω; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages): food, meat.
  5060. Τρόφιμος from τροφή; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian: Trophimus.
  5061. τροφός from τρέφω; a nourisher, i.e. nurse: nurse.
  5062. τροχιά from τροχός; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct: path.
  5063. τροχός from τρέχω; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects: course.
  5064. τρύβλιον neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl: dish.
  5065. τρυγάω from a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage: gather.
  5066. τρυγών from truzo (to murmur; akin to τρίζω, but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing): turtle-dove.
  5067. τρυμαλιά from a derivative of truo (to wear away; akin to the base of τραῦμα, τρίβος and τρώγω); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye: eye. Compare τρύπημα.
  5068. τρύπημα from a derivative of the base of τρυμαλιά; an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye: eye.
  5069. Τρύφαινα from τρυφή; luxurious; Tryphæna, a Christian woman: Tryphena.
  5070. τρυφάω from τρυφή; to indulge in luxury: live in pleasure.
  5071. τρυφή from thrupto (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. luxury or debauchery: delicately, riot.
  5072. Τρυφῶσα from τρυφή; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female: Tryphosa.
  5073. Τρωάς from Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor: Troas.
  5074. Τρωγύλλιον of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor: Trogyllium.
  5075. τρώγω probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of τραῦμα and τρίβος through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of τρυγών and τρίζω through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat: eat.
  5076. τυγχάνω probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of τίκτω through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with εἰ), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with οὐ, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were): be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special. Compare τύπτω.
  5077. τυμπανίζω from a derivative of τύπτω (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death: torture.
  5078. τύπος from τύπτω; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning): en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.
  5079. τύπτω a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from παίω and πατάσσω, which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or πλήσσω with the fist (or a hammer), or ῥαπίζω with the palm; as well as from τυγχάνω, an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience): beat, smite, strike, wound.
  5080. Τύραννος a provincial form of the derivative of the base of κύριος; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian: Tyrannus.
  5081. τυρβάζω from turbe (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to θόρυβος); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb: trouble.
  5082. Τύριος from Τύρος; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus: of Tyre.
  5083. Τύρος of Hebrew origin (צֹר): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine: Tyre.
  5084. τυφλός from, τυφόω; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally): blind.
  5085. τυφλόω from τυφλός; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure: blind.
  5086. τυφόω from a derivative of τύφω; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.
  5087. τύφω apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame: smoke.
  5088. τυφωνικός from a derivative of τύφω; stormy (as if smoky): tempestuous.
  5089. Τυχικός from a derivative of τυγχάνω; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian: Tychicus.
  5090. ὑακίνθινος from ὑάκινθος; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. deep blue: jacinth.
  5091. ὑάκινθος of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon: jacinth.
  5092. ὑάλινος from ὕαλος; glassy, i.e. transparent: of glass.
  5093. ὕαλος perhaps from the same as ὑετός (as being transparent like rain); glass: glass.
  5094. ὑβρίζω from ὕβρις; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse: use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).
  5095. ὕβρις from ὑπέρ; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury: harm, hurt, reproach.
  5096. ὑβριστής from ὑβρίζω; an insulter, i.e. maltreater: despiteful, injurious.
  5097. ὑγιαίνω from ὑγιής; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine): be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).
  5098. ὑγιής from the base of αὐξάνω; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine): sound, whole.
  5099. ὑγρός from the base of ὑετός; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh): green.
  5100. ὑδρία from ὕδωρ; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply: water-pot.
  5101. ὑδροποτέω from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages: drink water.
  5102. ὑδρωπικός from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical": have the dropsy.
  5103. ὕδωρ, and genitive case, hudatos, etc. from the base of ὑετός; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively: water.
  5104. ὑετός from a primary huo (to rain); rain, especially a shower: rain.
  5105. υἱοθεσία from a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God): adoption (of children, of sons).
  5106. υἱός apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship: child, foal, son.
  5107. ὕλη perhaps akin to ξύλον; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel: matter.
  5108. ὑμᾶς accusative case of ὑμεῖς; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition): ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own).
  5109. ὑμεῖς irregular plural of σύ; you (as subjective of verb): ye (yourselves), you.
  5110. Ὑμεναῖος from Humen (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity: Hymenæus.
  5111. ὑμέτερος from ὑμεῖς; yours, i.e. pertaining to you: your (own).
  5112. ὑμῖν irregular dative case of ὑμεῖς; to (with or by) you: ye, you, your(-selves).
  5113. ὑμνέω from ὕμνος; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song: sing a hymn (praise unto).
  5114. ὕμνος apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate; probably akin to ᾄδω; compare עֲבוֹט); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms): hymn.
  5115. ὑμῶν genitive case of ὑμεῖς; of (from or concerning) you: ye, you, your (own, -selves).
  5116. ὑπάγω from ὑπό and ἄγω; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively: depart, get hence, go (a-)way.
  5117. ὑπακοή from ὑπακούω; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission: obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing).
  5118. ὑπακούω from ὑπό and ἀκούω; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority: hearken, be obedient to, obey.
  5119. ὕπανδρος from ὑπό and ἀνήρ; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman: which hath an husband.
  5120. ὑπαντάω from ὑπό and a derivative of ἀντί; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with: (go to) meet.
  5121. ὑπάντησις from ὑπαντάω; an encounter or concurrence (with εἰς for infinitive, in order to fall in with): meeting.
  5122. ὕπαρξις from ὑπάρχω; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth: goods, substance.
  5123. ὑπάρχοντα neuter plural of present participle active of ὑπάρχω as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions: goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.
  5124. ὑπάρχω from ὑπό and ἄρχομαι; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb): after, behave, live.
  5125. ὑπείκω from ὑπό and eiko (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender: submit self.
  5126. ὑπεναντίος from ὑπό and ἐναντίος; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent: adversary, against.
  5127. ὑπέρ a primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than: (+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very. In the comparative, it retains many of the above applications.
  5128. ὑπεραίρομαι middle voice from ὑπέρ and αἴρω; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty: exalt self, be exalted above measure.
  5129. ὑπέρακμος from ὑπέρ and the base of ἀκμήν; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth: + pass the flower of (her) age.
  5130. ὑπεράνω from ὑπέρ and ἄνω; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank): far above, over.
  5131. ὑπεραυξάνω from ὑπέρ and αὐξάνω; to increase above ordinary degree: grow exceedingly.
  5132. ὑπερβαίνω from ὑπέρ and the base of βάσις; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach: go beyond.
  5133. ὑπερβαλλόντως adverb from present participle active of ὑπερβάλλω; excessively: beyond measure.
  5134. ὑπερβάλλω from ὑπέρ and βάλλω; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent): exceeding, excel, pass.
  5135. ὑπερβολή from ὑπερβάλλω; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with εἰς or κατά) pre- eminently: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.
  5136. ὑπερείδω from ὑπέρ and εἴδω; to overlook, i.e. not punish: wink at.
  5137. ὑπερέκεινα from ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος; above those parts, i.e. still farther: beyond.
  5138. ὑπερεκτείνω from ὑπέρ and ἐκτείνω; to extend inordinately: stretch beyond.
  5139. ὑπερεκχύνω from ὑπέρ and the alternate form of ἐκχέω; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow: run over.
  5140. ὑπερεντυγχάνω from ὑπέρ and ἐντυγχάνω; to intercede in behalf of: make intercession for.
  5141. ὑπερέχω from ὑπέρ and ἔχω; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority: better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.
  5142. ὑπερηφανία from ὑπερήφανος; haughtiness: pride.
  5143. ὑπερήφανος from ὑπέρ and φαίνω; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty: proud.
  5144. ὑπερνικάω from ὑπέρ and νικάω; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory: more than conquer.
  5145. ὑπέρογκος from ὑπέρ and ὄγκος; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent: great swelling.
  5146. ὑπεροχή from ὑπερέχω; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character): authority, excellency.
  5147. ὑπερπερισσεύω from ὑπέρ and περισσεύω; to super-abound: abound much more, exceeding.
  5148. ὑπερπερισσῶς from ὑπέρ and περισσῶς; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly: beyond measure.
  5149. ὑπερπλεονάζω from ὑπέρ and πλεονάζω; to superabound: be exceeding abundant.
  5150. ὑπερυψόω from ὑπέρ and ὑψόω; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position: highly exalt.
  5151. ὑπερφρονέω from ὑπέρ and φρονέω; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant: think more highly.
  5152. ὑπερῷον neuter of a derivative of ὑπέρ; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story: upper chamber (room).
  5153. ὑπέχω from ὑπό and ἔχω; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience: suffer.
  5154. ὑπήκοος from ὑπακούω; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive: obedient.
  5155. ὑπηρετέω from ὑπηρέτης; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve: minister (unto), serve.
  5156. ὑπηρέτης from ὑπό and a derivative of eresso (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable): minister, officer, servant.
  5157. ὕπνος from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to ὑπό through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor: sleep.
  5158. ὑπό a primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)): among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.
  5159. ὑποβάλλω from ὑπό and βάλλω; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion: suborn.
  5160. ὑπογραμμός from a compound of ὑπό and γράφω; an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively): example.
  5161. ὑπόδειγμα from ὑποδείκνυμι; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration): en-(ex-)ample, pattern.
  5162. ὑποδείκνυμι from ὑπό and δεικνύω; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish): show, (fore-)warn.
  5163. ὑποδέχομαι from ὑπό and δέχομαι; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably: receive.
  5164. ὑποδέω from ὑπό and δέω; to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals: bind on, (be) shod.
  5165. ὑπόδημα from ὑποδέω; something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal: shoe.
  5166. ὑπόδικος from ὑπό and δίκη; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned: guilty.
  5167. ὑποζύγιον neuter of a compound of ὑπό and ζυγός; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey: ass.
  5168. ὑποζώννυμι from ὑπό and ζώννυμι; to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck): undergirt.
  5169. ὑποκάτω from ὑπό and κάτω; down under, i.e. beneath: under.
  5170. ὑποκρίνομαι middle voice from ὑπό and κρίνω; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend): feign.
  5171. ὑπόκρισις from ὑποκρίνομαι; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"): condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.
  5172. ὑποκριτής from ὑποκρίνομαι; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite": hypocrite.
  5173. ὑπολαμβάνω from ὑπό and λαμβάνω; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume): answer, receive, suppose.
  5174. ὑπολείπω from ὑποτρέχω and λείπω; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive): be left.
  5175. ὑπολήνιον neuter of a presumed compound of ὑπό and ληνός; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat: winefat.
  5176. ὑπολιμπάνω a prolonged form for ὑπολείπω; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath: leave.
  5177. ὑπομένω from ὑπό and μένω; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere: abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.
  5178. ὑπομιμνήσκω from ὑπό and μιμνήσκω; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.
  5179. ὑπόμνησις from ὑπομιμνήσκω; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection: remembrance.
  5180. ὑπομονή from ὑπομένω; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy: enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting).
  5181. ὑπονοέω from ὑπό and νοιέω; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture: think, suppose, deem.
  5182. ὑπόνοια from ὑπονοέω; suspicion: surmising.
  5183. ὑποπλέω from ὑπό and πλέω; to sail under the lee of: sail under.
  5184. ὑποπνέω from ὑπό and πνέω; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze: blow softly.
  5185. ὑποπόδιον neuter of a compound of ὑπό and πούς; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively): footstool.
  5186. ὑπόστασις from a compound of ὑπό and ἵστημι; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively): confidence, confident, person, substance.
  5187. ὑποστέλλω from ὑπό and στέλλω; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve): draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.
  5188. ὑποστολή from ὑποστέλλω; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy: draw back.
  5189. ὑποστρέφω from ὑπό and στρέφω; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively): come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).
  5190. ὑποστρώννυμι from ὑπό and στρώννυμι; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet): spread.
  5191. ὑποταγή from ὑποτάσσω; subordination: subjection.
  5192. ὑποτάσσω from ὑπό and τάσσω; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.
  5193. ὑποτίθημι from ὑπό and τίθημι; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest: lay down, put in remembrance.
  5194. ὑποτρέχω from ὑπό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past: run under.
  5195. ὑποτύπωσις from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of τύπος; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation: form, pattern.
  5196. ὑποφέρω from ὑπό and φέρω; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship: bear, endure.
  5197. ὑποχωρέω from ὑπό and χωρέω; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly: go aside, withdraw self.
  5198. ὑπωπιάζω from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions): keep under, weary.
  5199. ὗς apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"): sow.
  5200. ὕσσωπος of foreign origin (אֵזוֹב); "hyssop": hyssop.
  5201. ὑστερέω from ὕστερος; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient): come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.
  5202. ὑστέρημα from ὑστερέω; a deficit; specially, poverty: that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want.
  5203. ὑστέρησις from ὑστερέω; a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury: want.
  5204. ὕστερον neuter of ὕστερος as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually: afterward, (at the) last (of all).
  5205. ὕστερος comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind); later: latter.
  5206. ὑφαντός from huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted: woven.
  5207. ὑψηλός from ὕψος; lofty (in place or character): high(-er, -ly) (esteemed).
  5208. ὑψηλοφρονέω from a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant: be highminded.
  5209. ὕψιστος superlative from the base of ὕψος; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens: most high, highest.
  5210. ὕψος from a derivative of ὑπέρ; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity: be exalted, height, (on) high.
  5211. ὑψόω from ὕψος; to elevate (literally or figuratively): exalt, lift up.
  5212. ὕψωμα from ὑψόω; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively): height, high thing.
  5213. φάγος from φάγω; a glutton: gluttonous.
  5214. φάγω a primary verb (used as an alternate of ἐσθίω in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively): eat, meat.
  5215. φαίνω prolongation for the base of φῶς; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative): appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.
  5216. Φάλεκ of Hebrew origin (פָּ֫לֶג); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch: Phalec.
  5217. φανερός from φαίνω; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly).
  5218. φανερόω from φανερός; to render apparent (literally or figuratively): appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).
  5219. φανερῶς adverb from φανερός; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly: evidently, openly.
  5220. φανέρωσις from φανερόω; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment: manifestation.
  5221. φανός from φαίνω; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern: lantern.
  5222. Φανουήλ of Hebrew origin (פְּנוּאֵל); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite: Phanuel.
  5223. φαντάζω from a derivative of φαίνω; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle): sight.
  5224. φαντασία from a derivative of φαντάζω; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"): pomp.
  5225. φάντασμα from φαντάζω; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre: spirit.
  5226. φάραγξ properly, strengthened from the base of πέραν or rather of ῥήγνυμι; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent): valley.
  5227. Φαραώ of foreign origin (פַּרְעֹה); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king: Pharaoh.
  5228. Φάρες of Hebrew origin (פָּ֫רֶץ); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite: Phares.
  5229. Φαρισαῖος of Hebrew origin (compare פָּרַשׁ); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary: Pharisee.
  5230. φαρμακεία from φαρμακεύς; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively): sorcery, witchcraft.
  5231. φαρμακεύς from pharmakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician: sorcerer.
  5232. φάρμακος the same as φαρμακεύς: sorcerer.
  5233. φάσις from φημί (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω); a saying, i.e. report: tidings.
  5234. φάσκω prolongation from the same as φημί; to assert: affirm, profess, say.
  5235. φάτνη from pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder): manager, stall.
  5236. φαῦλος apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked: evil.
  5237. φέγγος probably akin to the base of φῶς (compare φθέγγομαι); brilliancy: light.
  5238. φείδομαι of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently: forbear, spare.
  5239. φειδομένως adverb from participle of φείδομαι; abstemiously, i.e. stingily: sparingly.
  5240. φελόνης by transposition for a derivative probably of φαίνω (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout): cloke.
  5241. φέρω a primary verb -- for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio oy'-o; and enegko en-eng'-ko; to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows): be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.
  5242. φεύγω apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish: escape, flee (away).
  5243. Φῆλιξ of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman: Felix.
  5244. φήμη from φημί; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"): fame.
  5245. φημί properly, the same as the base of φῶς and φαίνω; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say: affirm, say. Compare λέγω.
  5246. Φῆστος of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman: Festus.
  5247. φθάνω apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at: (already) attain, come, prevent.
  5248. φθαρτός from φθείρω; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable: corruptible.
  5249. φθέγγομαι probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim: speak.
  5250. φθείρω probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave): corrupt (self), defile, destroy.
  5251. φθινοπωρινός from derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of φθείρω) and ὀπώρα (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves): whose fruit withereth.
  5252. φθόγγος from φθέγγομαι; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental): sound.
  5253. φθονέω from φθόνος; to be jealous of: envy.
  5254. φθόνος probably akin to the base of φθείρω; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite): envy.
  5255. φθορά from φθείρω; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively): corruption, destroy, perish.
  5256. φιάλη of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"): vial.
  5257. φιλάγαθος from φίλος and ἀγαθός; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue: love of good men.
  5258. Φιλαδέλφεια from Philadelphos (the same as φιλάδελφος), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor: Philadelphia.
  5259. φιλαδελφία from φιλάδελφος; fraternal affection: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.
  5260. φιλάδελφος from φίλος and ἀδελφός; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal: love as brethren.
  5261. φίλανδρος from φίλος and ἀνήρ; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife: love their husbands.
  5262. φιλανθρωπία from the same as φιλανθρώπως; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"): kindness, love towards man.
  5263. φιλανθρώπως adverb from a compound of φίλος and ἄνθρωπος; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely: courteously.
  5264. φιλαργυρία from φιλάργυρος; avarice: love of money.
  5265. φιλάργυρος from φίλος and ἄργυρος; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious: covetous.
  5266. φίλαυτος from φίλος and αὐτός; fond of self, i.e. selfish: lover of own self.
  5267. φιλέω from φίλος; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while ἀγαπάω is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as θέλω and βούλομαι, or as θυμός and νοῦς respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness): kiss, love.
  5268. φιλήδονος from φίλος and ἡδονή; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous: lover of pleasure.
  5269. φίλημα from φιλέω; a kiss: kiss.
  5270. Φιλήμων from φιλέω; friendly; Philemon, a Christian: Philemon.
  5271. Φίλητος from φιλέω; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity: Philetus.
  5272. φιλία from φίλος; fondness: friendship.
  5273. Φιλιππήσιος from Φίλιπποι; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi: Philippian.
  5274. Φίλιπποι plural of Φίλιππος; Philippi, a place in Macedonia: Philippi.
  5275. Φίλιππος from φίλος and ἵππος; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites: Philip.
  5276. φιλόθεος from φίλος and θεός; fond of God, i.e. pious: lover of God.
  5277. Φιλόλογος from φίλος and λόγος; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian: Philologus.
  5278. φιλονεικία from φιλόνεικος; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute: strife.
  5279. φιλόνεικος from φίλος and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to νῖκος); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious: contentious.
  5280. φιλονεξία from φιλόξενος; hospitableness: entertain stranger, hospitality.
  5281. φιλόξενος from φίλος and ξένος; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable: given to (lover of, use) hospitality.
  5282. φιλοπρωτεύω from a compound of φίλος and πρῶτος; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction: love to have the preeminence.
  5283. φίλος properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.): friend.
  5284. φιλοσοφία from φιλόσοφος; "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish sophistry: philosophy.
  5285. φιλόσοφος from φίλος and σοφός; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher": philosopher.
  5286. φιλόστοργος from φίλος and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian: kindly affectioned.
  5287. φιλότεκνος from φίλος and τέκνον; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal: love their children.
  5288. φιλοτιμέομαι middle voice from a compound of φίλος and τιμή; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something): labour, strive, study.
  5289. φιλοφρόνως adverb from φιλόφρων; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly: courteously.
  5290. φιλόφρων from φίλος and φρήν; friendly of mind, i.e. kind: courteous.
  5291. φιμόω from phimos (a muzzle); to muzzle: muzzle.
  5292. Φλέγων active participle of the base of φλόξ; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian: Phlegon.
  5293. φλογίζω from φλόξ; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion): set on fire.
  5294. φλόξ from a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze: flame(-ing).
  5295. φλυαρέω from φλύαρος; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously: prate against.
  5296. φλύαρος from phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater: tattler.
  5297. φοβερός from φόβος; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable: fearful, terrible.
  5298. φοβέω from φόβος; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere: be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.
  5299. φόβητρον neuter of a derivative of φοβέω; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent: fearful sight.
  5300. φόβος from a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright: be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.
  5301. Φοίβη feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of φῶς); Phœbe, a Christian woman: Phebe.
  5302. Φοινίκη from φοῖνιξ; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine: Phenice, Phenicia.
  5303. φοῖνιξ of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree: palm (tree).
  5304. Φοῖνιξ probably the same as φοῖνιξ; Phœnix, a place in Crete: Phenice.
  5305. φονεύς from φόνος; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος is a special term for a public bandit): murderer.
  5306. φονεύω from φονεύς; to be a murderer (of): kill, do murder, slay.
  5307. φόνος from an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder: murder, + be slain with, slaughter.
  5308. φορέω from φόρος; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment: bear, wear.
  5309. Φόρον of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Ἄππιος; a station on the Appian road: forum.
  5310. φόρος from φέρω; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas τέλος is usually a general toll on goods or travel): tribute.
  5311. φορτίζω from φόρτος; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety): lade, by heavy laden.
  5312. φορτίον diminutive of φόρτος; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service: burden.
  5313. φόρτος from φέρω; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship: lading.
  5314. Φορτουνᾶτος of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian: Fortunatus.
  5315. φραγέλλιον neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment: scourge.
  5316. φραγελλόω from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment: scourge.
  5317. φραγμός from φράσσω; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively): hedge (+ round about), partition.
