  5318. φράζω probably akin to φράσσω through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound: declare.
  5319. φράσσω apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence): stop.
  5320. φρέαρ of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison): well, pit.
  5321. φρεναπατάω from φρεναπάτης; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude: deceive.
  5322. φρεναπάτης from φρήν and ἀπάτη; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer: deceiver.
  5323. φρήν probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare φράσσω); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties): understanding.
  5324. φρίσσω apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear): tremble.
  5325. φρονέω from φρήν; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience): set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.
  5326. φρόνημα from φρονέω; (mental) inclination or purpose: (be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).
  5327. φρόνησις from φρονέω; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight: prudence, wisdom.
  5328. φρόνιμος from φρήν; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative): wise(-r).
  5329. φρονίμως adverb from φρόνιμος; prudently: wisely.
  5330. φροντίζω from a derivative of φρήν; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious: be careful.
  5331. φρουρέω from a compound of πρό and ὁράω; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect: keep (with a garrison). Compare τηρέω.
  5332. φρυάσσω akin to βρύω, βρύχω; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult: rage.
  5333. φρύγανον neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of φλόξ); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig: stick.
  5334. Φρυγία probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor: Phrygia.
  5335. Φύγελλος probably from φεύγω; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian: Phygellus.
  5336. φυγή from φεύγω; a fleeing, i.e. escape: flight.
  5337. φυλακή from φυλάσσω; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively: cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.
  5338. φυλακίζω from φύλαξ; to incarcerate: imprison.
  5339. φυλακτήριον neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts: phylactery.
  5340. φύλαξ from φυλάσσω; a watcher or sentry: keeper.
  5341. φυλάσσω probably from φυλή through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid: beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare τηρέω.
  5342. φυλή from φύω (compare φύλλον); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan: kindred, tribe.
  5343. φύλλον from the same as φυλή; a sprout, i.e. leaf: leaf.
  5344. φύραμα from a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough: lump.
  5345. φυσικός from φύσις; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive: natural. Compare ψυχικός.
  5346. φυσικῶς adverb from φυσικός; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively: naturally.
  5347. φυσιόω from φύσις in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty): puff up.
  5348. φύσις from φύω; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage: (man-)kind, nature(-al).
  5349. φυσίωσις from φυσιόω; inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness: swelling.
  5350. φυτεία from φυτεύω; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable: plant.
  5351. φυτεύω from a derivative of φύω; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine: plant.
  5352. φύω a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively: spring (up).
  5353. φωλεός of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place: hole.
  5354. φωνέω from φωνή; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation: call (for), crow, cry.
  5355. φωνή probably akin to φαίνω through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language: noise, sound, voice.
  5356. φῶς from an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω, φημί); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative): fire, light.
  5357. φωστήρ from φῶς; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy: light.
  5358. φωσφόρος from φῶς and φέρω; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively): day star.
  5359. φωτεινός from φῶς; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively): bright, full of light.
  5360. φωτίζω from φῶς; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively): enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
  5361. φωτισμός from φωτίζω; illumination (figuratively): light.
  5362. χαίρω a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.
  5363. χάλαζα probably from χαλάω; hail: hail.
  5364. χαλάω from the base of χάσμα; to lower (as into a void): let down, strike.
  5365. Χαλδαῖος probably of Hebrew or (כַּשְׂדִּי); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates: Chaldæan.
  5366. χαλεπός perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious: fierce, perilous.
  5367. χαλιναγωγέω from a compound of χαλινός and the reduplicated form of ἄγω; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively): bridle.
  5368. χαλινός from χαλάω; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit): bit, bridle.
  5369. χάλκεος from χαλκός; coppery: brass.
  5370. χαλκεύς from χαλκός; a copper-worker or brazier: coppersmith.
  5371. χαλκηδών from χαλκός and perhaps εἶδος; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony": chalcedony.
  5372. χαλκίον diminutive from χαλκός; a copper dish: brazen vessel.
  5373. χαλκολίβανον neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre: fine brass.
  5374. χαλκός perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it): brass, money.
  5375. χαμαί adverb perhaps from the base of χάσμα through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate: on (to) the ground.
  5376. Χαναάν of Hebrew origin (כְּנַ֫עַן); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine: Chanaan.
  5377. Χανααναῖος from Χαναάν; a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine: of Canaan.
  5378. χαρά from χαίρω; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).
  5379. χάραγμα from the same as χάραξ; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue): graven, mark.
  5380. χαρακτήρ from the same as χάραξ; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation): express image.
  5381. χάραξ from charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to γράφω through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege): trench.
  5382. χαρίζομαι middle voice from χάρις; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue: deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant.
  5383. χάριν accusative case of χάρις as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully.
  5384. χάρις from χαίρω; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude): acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).
  5385. χάρισμα from χαρίζομαι; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty: (free) gift.
  5386. χαριτόω from χάρις; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor: make accepted, be highly favoured.
  5387. Χαῤῥάν of Hebrew origin (חָרָן); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia: Charran.
  5388. χάρτης from the same as χάραξ; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over): paper.
  5389. χάσμα from a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval): gulf.
  5390. χεῖλος from a form of the same as χάσμα; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water): lip, shore.
  5391. χειμάζω from the same as χειμών; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale: be tossed with tempest.
  5392. χείμαῤῥος from the base of χειμών and ῥέω; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent: brook.
  5393. χειμών from a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of χάσμα through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter: tempest, foul weather, winter.
  5394. χείρ perhaps from the base of χειμών in the sense of its congener the base of χάσμα (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument): hand.
  5395. χειραγωγέω from χειραγωγός; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person): lead by the hand.
  5396. χειραγωγός from χείρ and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person): some to lead by the hand.
  5397. χειρόγραφον neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)): handwriting.
  5398. χειροποίητος from χείρ and a derivative of ποιέω; manufactured, i.e. of human construction: made by (make with) hands.
  5399. χειροτονέω from a comparative of χείρ and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint: choose, ordain.
  5400. χείρων irregular comparative of κακός; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally): sorer, worse.
  5401. χερουβίμ plural of Hebrew origin (כְּרוּב); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim): cherubims.
  5402. χήρα feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of χάσμα through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively: widow.
  5403. χθές of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto: yesterday.
  5404. χιλιάς from χίλιοι; one thousand ("chiliad"): thousand.
  5405. χιλίαρχος from χίλιοι and ἄρχω; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel: (chief, high) captain.
  5406. χίλιοι plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand: thousand.
  5407. Χίος of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean: Chios.
  5408. χιτών of foreign origin (כֻּתֹּ֫נֶת); a tunic or shirt: clothes, coat, garment.
  5409. χιών perhaps akin to the base of χάσμα (χαλάω) or χειμών (as descending or empty); snow: snow.
  5410. χλαμύς of uncertain derivation; a military cloak: robe.
  5411. χλευάζω from a derivative probably of χεῖλος; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at: mock.
  5412. χλιαρός from chlio (to warm); tepid: lukewarm.
  5413. Χλόη feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloë, a Christian female: Chloe.
  5414. χλωρός from the same as Χλόη; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored: green, pale.
  5415. χξϛ the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (στίγμα as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral: six hundred threescore and six.
  5416. χοϊκός from χόος; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene: earthy.
  5417. χοῖνιξ of uncertain derivation; a chœnix or certain dry measure: measure.
  5418. χοῖρος of uncertain derivation; a hog: swine.
  5419. χολάω from χολή; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"): be angry.
  5420. χολή feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Χλόη (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.): gall.
  5421. χόος from the base of χειμών; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt: dust.
  5422. Χοραζίν of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine: Chorazin.
  5423. χορηγέω from a compound of χορός and ἄγω; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish: give, minister.
  5424. χορός of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir": dancing.
  5425. χορτάζω from χόρτος; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance): feed, fill, satisfy.
  5426. χόρτασμα from χορτάζω; forage, i.e. food: sustenance.
  5427. χόρτος apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation: blade, grass, hay.
  5428. Χουζᾶς of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod: Chuza.
  5429. χράομαι middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from χείρ, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner: entreat, use. Compare χράω; χρή.
  5430. χράω probably the same as the base of χράομαι; to loan: lend.
  5431. χρεία from the base of χράομαι or χρή; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want.
  5432. χρεωφειλέτης from a derivative of χράω and ὀφειλέτης; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person: debtor.
  5433. χρή third person singular of the same as χράομαι or χράω used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be: ought.
  5434. χρῄζω from χρεία; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of: (have) need.
  5435. χρῆμα something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price: money, riches.
  5436. χρηματίζω from χρῆμα; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of χράομαι), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of χρεία) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.
  5437. χρηματισμός from χρηματίζω; a divine response or revelation: answer of God.
  5438. χρήσιμος from χρῆσις; serviceable: profit.
  5439. χρῆσις from χράομαι; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body): use.
  5440. χρηστεύομαι middle voice from χρηστός; to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently: be kind.
  5441. χρηστολογία from a compound of χρηστός and λέγω; fair speech, i.e. plausibility: good words.
  5442. χρηστός from χράομαι; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals): better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind.
  5443. χρηστότης from χρηστός; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor): gentleness, good(-ness), kindness.
  5444. χρῖσμα from χρίω; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit: anointing, unction.
  5445. Χριστιανός from Χριστός; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ: Christian.
  5446. Χριστός from χρίω; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus: Christ.
  5447. χρίω probably akin to χράομαι through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service: anoint.
  5448. χρονίζω from χρόνος; to take time, i.e. linger: delay, tarry.
  5449. χρόνος of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from καιρός, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from αἰών, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while.
  5450. χρονοτριβέω from a presumed compound of χρόνος and the base of τρίβος; to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger): spend time.
  5451. χρύσεος from χρυσός; made of gold: of gold, golden.
  5452. χρυσίον diminutive of χρυσός; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin: gold.
  5453. χρυσοδακτύλιος from χρυσός and δακτύλιος; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry: with a gold ring.
  5454. χρυσόλιθος from χρυσός and λίθος; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite"): chrysolite.
  5455. χρυσόπρασος from χρυσός and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase"): chrysoprase.
  5456. χρυσός perhaps from the base of χράομαι (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin: gold.
  5457. χρυσόω from χρυσός; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments: deck.
  5458. χρώς probably akin to the base of χράομαι through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin): body.
  5459. χωλός apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping: cripple, halt, lame.
  5460. χώρα feminine of a derivative of the base of χάσμα through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants): coast, county, fields, ground, land, region. Compare τόπος.
  5461. χωρέω from χώρα; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively): come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.
  5462. χωρίζω from χώρα; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away: depart, put asunder, separate.
  5463. χωρίον diminutive of χώρα; a spot or plot of ground: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.
  5464. χωρίς adverb from χώρα; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition): beside, by itself, without.
  5465. χῶρος of Latin origin; the north-west wind: north west.
  5466. ψάλλω probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare ψώχω); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes): make melody, sing (psalms).
  5467. ψαλμός from ψάλλω; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms: psalm. Compare ᾠδή.
  5468. ψευδάδελφος from ψευδής and ἀδελφός; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate: false brethren.
  5469. ψευδαπόστολος from ψευδής and ἀπόστολος; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher: false teacher.
  5470. ψευδής from ψεύδομαι; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked: false, liar.
  5471. ψευδοδιδάσκαλος from ψευδής and διδάσκαλος; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine: false teacher.
  5472. ψευδολόγος from ψευδής and λέγω; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine: speaking lies.
  5473. ψεύδομαι middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood: falsely, lie.
  5474. ψευδομάρτυρ from ψευδής and a kindred form of μάρτυς; a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony: false witness.
  5475. ψευδομαρτυρέω from ψευδομάρτυρ; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence: be a false witness.
  5476. ψευδομαρτυρία from ψευδομάρτυρ; untrue testimony: false witness.
  5477. ψευδοπροφήτης from ψευδής and προφήτης; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor: false prophet.
  5478. ψεῦδος from ψεύδομαι; a falsehood: lie, lying.
  5479. ψευδόχριστος from ψευδής and Χριστός; a spurious Messiah: false Christ.
  5480. ψευδώνυμος from ψευδής and ὄνομα; untruly named: falsely so called.
  5481. ψεῦσμα from ψεύδομαι; a fabrication, i.e. falsehood: lie.
  5482. ψεύστης from ψεύδομαι; a falsifier: liar.
  5483. ψηλαφάω from the base of ψάλλω (compare ψῆφος); to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for: feel after, handle, touch.
  5484. ψηφίζω from ψῆφος; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute: count.
  5485. ψῆφος from the same as ψηλαφάω; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote: stone, voice.
  5486. ψιθυρισμός from a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to ψεύδομαι); whispering, i.e. secret detraction: whispering.
  5487. ψιθυριστής from the same as ψιθυρισμός; a secret calumniator: whisperer.
  5488. ψιχίον diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψάλλω (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel: crumb.
  5489. ψυχή from ψύχω; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from πνεῦμα, which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from ζωή, which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew נָ֫פֶשׁ, ר֫וּחַ and חָי): heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.
  5490. ψυχικός from ψυχή; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from πνευματικός, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from φυσικός, which is the lower or bestial nature): natural, sensual.
  5491. ψύχος from ψύχω; coolness: cold.
  5492. ψυχρός from ψύχος; chilly (literally or figuratively): cold.
  5493. ψύχω a primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from πνέω, which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of ἀήρ, which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively): wax cold.
  5494. ψωμίζω from the base of ψωμίον; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish: (bestow to) feed.
  5495. ψωμίον diminutive from a derivative of the base of ψώχω; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful: sop.
  5496. ψώχω prolongation from the same base as ψάλλω; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand): rub.
  5497. Ω the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality: Omega.
  5498. ὦ a primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh: O.
  5499. ὦ, including the oblique forms, as well as es; e; etc. the subjunctive of εἰμί; (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with εἰ and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be: + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.
  5500. Ὠβήδ of Hebrew origin (עוֹבֵד); Obed, an Israelite: Obed.
  5501. ὧδε from an adverb form of ὅδε; in this same spot, i.e. here or hither: here, hither, (in) this place, there.
  5502. ᾠδή from ᾄδω; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while ὕμνος denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and ψαλμός still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation): song.
  5503. ὠδίν akin to ὀδύνη; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth: pain, sorrow, travail.
  5504. ὠδίνω from ὠδίν; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively): travail in (birth).
  5505. ὦμος perhaps from the alternate of φέρω; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne): shoulder.
  5506. ὤν, including the feminine ousa; and the neuter on present participle of εἰμί; being: be, come, have.
  5507. ὠνέομαι middle voice from an apparently primary onos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier πίμπρημι): buy.
  5508. ὠόν apparently a primary word; an "egg": egg.
  5509. ὥρα apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively): day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time.
  5510. ὡραῖος from ὥρα; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)): beautiful.
  5511. ὠρύομαι middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar": roar.
  5512. ὡς probably adverb of comparative from ὅς; which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows): about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed.
  5513. ὡσαννά of Hebrew origin (יָשַׁע and נָא); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration: hosanna.
  5514. ὡσαύτως from ὡς and an adverb from αὐτός; as thus, i.e. in the same way: even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.
  5515. ὡσεί from ὡς and εἰ; as if: about, as (it had been, it were), like (as).
  5516. Ὡσηέ of Hebrew origin (הוֹשֵׁ֫עַ); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite: Osee.
  5517. ὥσπερ from ὡς and περ; just as, i.e. exactly like: (even, like) as.
  5518. ὡσπερεί from ὥσπερ and εἰ; just as if, i.e. as it were: as.
  5519. ὥστε from ὡς and τέ; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow): (insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore.
  5520. ὠτίον diminutive of οὖς; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear: ear.
  5521. ὠφέλεια from a derivative of the base of ὠφέλιμος; usefulness, i.e. benefit: advantage, profit.
  5522. ὠφελέω from the same as ὠφέλεια; to be useful, i.e. to benefit: advantage, better, prevail, profit.
  5523. ὠφέλιμος from a form of ὄφελος; helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous: profit(-able).
